commands.name: GetAddOnVersion
commands.description: Retrieves the version of the Tapir Additional JSON Commands Add-On.

version.description: Version number in the form of "1.1.1".

example.description: Prints the version of the Tapir Add-On with GetAddOnVersion.

"""Prints the version of the Tapir Add-On with GetAddOnVersion."""

commands.name: GetCommands
commands.description: Retrieves every command of the Tapir Add-On with its command group, the Tapir version it was introduced in and its description, so a script can check that a command exists before calling it.
Every command of the Tapir Add-On, in the order of the command reference.

name.description: The name of the command.

group.description: The name of the command group, e.g. "Application Commands".

version.description: The Tapir version the command was introduced in, in the form of "1.1.1".

description.description: The description of the command, as in the command reference.

example.description: Lists the commands of the Tapir Add-On with GetCommands and checks that a command exists before calling it.

commands.name: GetArchicadLocation
commands.description: Retrieves the location of the currently running Archicad executable.

archicadLocation.description: The location of the Archicad executable in the filesystem.

example.description: Prints where the running Archicad executable is, with GetArchicadLocation.
example.code:
"""Prints where the running Archicad executable is, with GetArchicadLocation."""

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetArchicadLocation'))

commands.name: GetArchicadReleaseInfo
commands.description: Retrieves the main version, release version and build number of the running Archicad, with the caption of its window.

mainVersion.description: The main version of the running Archicad, e.g. 29.

releaseVersion.description: The release (update) version of the running Archicad.

buildNumber.description: The build number of the running Archicad.

caption.description: The caption of the Archicad application window. Missing when Archicad does not report it.

example.description: Prints the version, release and build number of the running Archicad with GetArchicadReleaseInfo.

"""Prints the version, release and build number of the running Archicad with GetArchicadReleaseInfo."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetArchicadReleaseInfo'))

commands.name: GetArchicadLicenseInfo
commands.description: Retrieves the license the running Archicad runs on: its type (Full, Education, Trial, Demo, Start or BIMcloud Team Client), the raw protection mode with its bits by name, and the highest Software Service Agreement (SSA) level of the license, so a script can warn before it uses a feature the license lacks. The SSA level is not available in Archicad 25.

licenseType.description: The kind of license Archicad runs on, read from protectionMode: Trial, Demo, Education (an education license with or without a key), BIMcloudTeamClient, Start (the Start edition), otherwise Full.

protectionMode.description: The raw protection mode bit mask reported by Archicad (the APIPROT_*_MASK bits of the Archicad API).

licenseFlags.description: The bits set in protectionMode, by name: Site (more licenses), NotForResale, School, PayPerUse, Network (network licensing), Teamwork (Teamwork functionality is on), Education (education key), Start (Start edition), Solo (SOLO edition), LiveSubscription, OEM (Archicad 27 or later), SSA (SSA license, Archicad 25 only), and without a hardware or software key EducationWithoutKey, Demo, Trial and BIMcloudTeamClient.

ssaLevel.description: The highest Software Service Agreement (SSA) level the license has: NoSSA, SSA or Forward. A script needing a level checks that this is at least that level, in this order. Missing in Archicad 25, which cannot report it.

example.description: Prints the license type, the license flags and the SSA level of the running Archicad with GetArchicadLicenseInfo, then warns when the license is not a full one. The SSA level is not reported in Archicad 25.
example.code:
"""Prints the license type, the license flags and the SSA level of the running Archicad with GetArchicadLicenseInfo,
then warns when the license is not a full one.

The SSA level is not reported in Archicad 25.
"""
import aclib

licenseInfo = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetArchicadLicenseInfo')
aclib.PrintJson (licenseInfo)

if licenseInfo and licenseInfo['licenseType'] != 'Full':
    print (f"Warning: Archicad runs on a {licenseInfo['licenseType']} license.")

commands.name: GetPointFromUser
commands.description: Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled.

prompt.description: Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.

snapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to. Default: Archicad's usual snapping.

constraint.description: Constrains the click, for example to a fixed X coordinate or to a direction. Default: no constraint.

position.description: The clicked point in the project's coordinates.

example.description: Asks the user to click a point in the current window with GetPointFromUser and prints it. Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape cancels the input and the command fails. The optional snapFilter makes the cursor snap only to the end points and reference lines of walls.

commands.name: ModelToScreen
commands.description: Converts model coordinates to pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. In a 3D window the coordinates are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded. Available from Archicad 29.

coordinates.description: Model coordinates in the current database (meters). In a 3D window they are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded.

screenPoints.description: One item per input coordinate, in the same order: the pixel position local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), or an error.

example.description: Converts two model points to pixel positions of the current view window with ModelToScreen. The pixels depend on the window's size, scale and zoom. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

commands.name: ScreenToModel
commands.description: Converts pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window to 2D model coordinates of the current database, using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. It is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and several model coordinates can map to the same pixel.

screenPoints.description: Pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates).

coordinates.description: One item per input screen point, in the same order: the 2D model coordinate in the current database (meters), or an error. This is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and in a 3D window the result is not a point of the model.

example.description: Converts two pixel positions of the current view window to model coordinates with ScreenToModel. The result depends on the window's size, scale and zoom.

commands.name: GetElementFromUser
commands.description: Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.

prompt.description: Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.

elementTypes.description: Only an element of one of these types is accepted. A click on empty space or on an element of another type asks for the click again. Default: any element.

snapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to, for example only the points and edges of the element types asked for. Default: Archicad's usual snapping.

constraint.description: Constrains every click, for example to a fixed X coordinate or to a direction. Default: no constraint.

elementId.description: The clicked element. In a section or elevation window it is the model element the section element was cut from.

elementType.description: The type of the clicked element (one of the ElementType values, or Unknown).

position.description: The clicked point in the project's coordinates, as GetPointFromUser returns it.

elementPosition.description: The coordinate of the clicked part of the element (e.g. its node or hotspot), when Archicad gives one for it.

cancelled.description: True when the input was cancelled with Escape; no other field is returned then.

example.description: Asks the user to click a wall or a column with GetElementFromUser and prints its id, type and the clicked point. Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled. The optional snapFilter makes the cursor snap only to the points and lines of walls and columns.

commands.name: GetCurrentTool
commands.description: Returns the tool active in the Toolbox: its element type, its variation (the subtype, e.g. Door, Skylight or a library part subtype of an add-on) and, for the tools of add-ons, its class id, in the form SetCurrentTool accepts. Nothing is returned when the active tool makes no element, e.g. the Arrow or the Marquee.

outputSchema.description: The tool active in the Toolbox, in the form SetCurrentTool accepts. Empty when the active tool makes no element, e.g. the Arrow or the Marquee.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

example.description: Gets the tool active in the Toolbox with GetCurrentTool. The result (element type, variation, class id) can be given to SetCurrentTool as it is. It is empty when the Arrow or the Marquee is active.
example.code:
"""Gets the tool active in the Toolbox with GetCurrentTool.

The result (element type, variation, class id) can be given to SetCurrentTool as it is. It is empty
when the Arrow or the Marquee is active.
"""
import aclib

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentTool')

if result:
    aclib.PrintJson (result)
else:
    print ('The active tool makes no element (Arrow or Marquee).')

commands.name: SetCurrentTool
commands.description: Activates a tool in the Toolbox, given as GetCurrentTool or GetToolboxItems returns it; an empty input activates the Arrow. Archicad switches the tool once it processes its events, so GetCurrentTool may still return the previous tool right after this command.

inputSchema.description: The tool to activate, in the form GetCurrentTool and GetToolboxItems return. An empty object activates the Arrow.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

example.description: Activates the Wall tool with SetCurrentTool, then the Door tool, then restores the tool that was active. Archicad switches the tool once it processes its events, so it may take a moment to show in the Toolbox. An empty input activates the Arrow.
example.code:
"""Activates the Wall tool with SetCurrentTool, then the Door tool, then restores the tool that was active.

Archicad switches the tool once it processes its events, so it may take a moment to show in the Toolbox.
An empty input activates the Arrow.
"""
import aclib

original = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentTool')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetCurrentTool', {'elementType': 'Wall'}))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetCurrentTool', {'elementType': 'Door'}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetCurrentTool', original))

commands.name: GetToolboxItems
commands.description: Lists the tools of the Toolbox, the tools of add-ons included, in the form SetCurrentTool accepts, and the active tool. includeHidden also lists the tools without an icon, e.g. the Slab Accessory.

includeHidden.description: Also list the tools that have no icon in the Toolbox but can be active, e.g. the Slab Accessory. Default: false.

toolboxItems.description: The tools installed in the Toolbox, the tools of add-ons included, each in the form SetCurrentTool accepts.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

currentTool.description: The tool active in the Toolbox, as GetCurrentTool returns it. Empty for the Arrow and the Marquee.

elementType.description: The element type of the tool. Unknown for the tools of add-ons, which classId identifies.

variation.description: The four-character subtype of the tool, e.g. DOOR, SKYL, CRWD, or the signature of a library part subtype registered by an add-on. Missing for the generic tool of the element type.

classId.description: The class id (a guid) of the tool of an add-on, whose elementType is Unknown. Archicad 26 and later.

example.description: Lists the tools of the Toolbox with GetToolboxItems, the tools of add-ons included, and the active tool. Each item can be given to SetCurrentTool as it is. includeHidden also lists the tools without an icon, e.g. the Slab Accessory.
example.code:
"""Lists the tools of the Toolbox with GetToolboxItems, the tools of add-ons included, and the active tool.

Each item can be given to SetCurrentTool as it is. includeHidden also lists the tools without an icon,
e.g. the Slab Accessory.
"""
import aclib

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetToolboxItems', {'includeHidden': False})

for item in result['toolboxItems']:
    print (item)
print ('Active tool:', result['currentTool'] or 'Arrow or Marquee')

commands.name: GetLineFromUser
commands.description: Waits for the user to input a line in the active Archicad window and returns start and end coordinates.

startPrompt.description: Prompt for selecting the line start point.
startPrompt.default: Click the start point of the line

endPrompt.description: Prompt for selecting the line end point.
endPrompt.default: Click the end point of the line

showRubberLineFeedback.description: If true, draws a unit-square rubber feedback around the cursor while input is active.

snapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to, for both points. Default: Archicad's usual snapping.

constraint.description: Constrains the end point, for example to a direction from the start point (type Angle with fromLastPoint). The start point is not constrained. Default: no constraint.

cancelled.description: True if the user cancelled the input (ESC).

startPoint.description: The start point of the line.

endPoint.description: The end point of the line. It is only valid if cancelled is false.

example.description: Asks the user to draw a line in the current window with GetLineFromUser and prints its end points. Waits for two clicks in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled. The optional snapFilter makes the cursor snap only to points (end points, vertices, hotspots), not to edges, and never to hatches. The optional constraint keeps the end point on the horizontal line through the start point (angle 0 measured from the last clicked point), so the line is always horizontal.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to draw a line in the current window with GetLineFromUser and prints its end points.

Waits for two clicks in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled. The optional snapFilter makes the
cursor snap only to points (end points, vertices, hotspots), not to edges, and never to hatches.
The optional constraint keeps the end point on the horizontal line through the start point
(angle 0 measured from the last clicked point), so the line is always horizontal.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLineFromUser', {
    'startPrompt': 'Click the start point of the line',
    'endPrompt': 'Click the end point of the horizontal line',
    'snapFilter': {'base': 'Nodes', 'exclude': ['Hatch']},
    'constraint': {'type': 'Angle', 'value': 0.0, 'fromLastPoint': True}
}))

commands.name: GetArcFromUser
commands.description: Asks the designer to draw an arc in the current window - its center, its start point (which sets the radius) and its end point - with a rubber-band circle shown while drawing, and returns its center, radius, start and end angles, the angle it turns through, its direction and its start and end points. Archicad waits for the clicks or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.

centerPrompt.description: Prompt for clicking the center of the arc. Single-byte text: the control box takes a char field.
centerPrompt.default: Click the center of the arc

startPrompt.description: Prompt for clicking the start point of the arc, which also sets its radius.
startPrompt.default: Click the start point of the arc

endPrompt.description: Prompt for clicking the end point of the arc. Archicad draws the arc while the cursor moves; the direction the cursor goes around the center decides whether the arc is clockwise.
endPrompt.default: Click the end point of the arc

showRubberArcFeedback.description: If true, also draws the whole circle of the arc while the start and end points are chosen: its radius follows the cursor until the start point is clicked. Drawn in 2D windows only; the 3D window shows Archicad's default feedback.

snapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to for the center and the start point. Archicad's arc input has no snap filter, so the end point snaps as usual. Default: Archicad's usual snapping.

constraint.description: Constrains every click: the center, the start point and the end point. With fromLastPoint the start point is measured from the center (type Distance fixes the radius, type Angle the direction of the start point) and the end point from the start point. Default: no constraint.

cancelled.description: True if the user cancelled the input (Escape); no other field is returned then.

radius.description: The radius of the arc: the distance of the start point from the center in the x-y plane.

startAngle.description: The direction of the start point from the center, in radians from the x axis, counterclockwise, between -pi and pi.

endAngle.description: The direction of the end point from the center, in radians from the x axis, counterclockwise, between -pi and pi.

arcAngle.description: The angle the arc turns through from its start to its end, in radians: positive (up to 2*pi) for a counterclockwise arc, negative (down to -2*pi) for a clockwise one.

clockwise.description: True if the arc was drawn clockwise from its start to its end.

startPoint.description: The start point of the arc, as clicked.

endPoint.description: The end point of the arc: the point of its circle in the direction of the third click (its z is the clicked z).

example.description: Asks the user to draw an arc in the current window with GetArcFromUser and prints its center, radius and angles. Waits for three clicks in Archicad (center, start point, end point); Escape returns cancelled. The optional snapFilter makes the center and the start point snap only to points (end points, vertices, hotspots), not to edges, and never to hatches; the end point snaps as usual. The optional constraint keeps every click at the height 0 (type Z), which matters in the 3D window.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to draw an arc in the current window with GetArcFromUser and prints its center, radius and angles.

Waits for three clicks in Archicad (center, start point, end point); Escape returns cancelled.
The optional snapFilter makes the center and the start point snap only to points (end points,
vertices, hotspots), not to edges, and never to hatches; the end point snaps as usual. The
optional constraint keeps every click at the height 0 (type Z), which matters in the 3D window.
"""
import aclib

aclib.raiseOnError = True
aclib.RequireTapir ('1.8.1')
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetArcFromUser', {
    'centerPrompt': 'Click the center of the arc',
    'startPrompt': 'Click the start point of the arc',
    'endPrompt': 'Click the end point of the arc',
    'snapFilter': {'base': 'Nodes', 'exclude': ['Hatch']},
    'constraint': {'type': 'Z', 'value': 0.0}
}))

commands.name: GetPolygonFromUser
commands.description: Waits for the user to input a polygon in the active Archicad window and returns its points and arcs.

startPrompt.description: Prompt for selecting the polygon start point.
startPrompt.default: Click the start point of the polygon

prompt.description: Prompt shown while placing the remaining polygon nodes.
prompt.default: Click polygon nodes and finish the input

snapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to for the start point. Archicad's polygon input has no snap filter, so the other nodes snap as usual. Default: Archicad's usual snapping.

constraint.description: Constrains the nodes after the start point, for example to a direction from the previous node (type Angle with fromLastPoint). The start point is not constrained. Default: no constraint.

cancelled.description: True if the user cancelled the input (ESC).

example.description: Asks the user to draw a polygon in the current window with GetPolygonFromUser and prints its points and arcs. Waits for the polygon input in Archicad (a double click or Enter finishes it); Escape returns cancelled. The optional snapFilter makes the first corner snap only to the corners of zones; the other corners snap as usual.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to draw a polygon in the current window with GetPolygonFromUser and prints its points and arcs.

Waits for the polygon input in Archicad (a double click or Enter finishes it); Escape returns cancelled.
The optional snapFilter makes the first corner snap only to the corners of zones; the other corners
snap as usual.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPolygonFromUser', {
    'startPrompt': 'Click the first corner of the polygon on a zone corner',
    'prompt': 'Click the other corners, double click to finish',
    'method': 'General',
    'snapFilter': {'include': ['Zone']}
}))

commands.name: GetMagicWandSettings
commands.description: Returns the settings of Archicad's Magic Wand Settings dialog: how curves are approximated with straight segments (a number of segments along arcs or circles, a largest deviation from the curve, or a segment length) and the trace method. Useful to know how the Magic Wand will trace a curve. Changes nothing in the project.

curveApproximation.description: How the Magic Wand approximates curves with straight segments: a fixed number of segments along arcs or along full circles (segmentCount), segments that deviate from the curve by at most maxDeviation, or segments of segmentLength. Unknown for a mode this version of Tapir does not know.

segmentCount.description: The number of segments along an arc or circle, used by SegmentsAlongArcs and SegmentsAlongCircles.

maxDeviation.description: The largest distance of the segments from the curve, in meters, used by DeviationFromCurves.

segmentLength.description: The length of the segments, in meters, used by SegmentLength.

traceMethod.description: How curves are traced: Linear traces them with straight segments as set above, BestMatch with the curves that match them best. Unknown for a method this version of Tapir does not know.

example.description: Prints the Magic Wand settings (how curves are approximated with segments, and the trace method) with GetMagicWandSettings.
example.code:
"""Prints the Magic Wand settings (how curves are approximated with segments, and the trace method) with GetMagicWandSettings."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMagicWandSettings'))

commands.name: ConvertImages
commands.description: Converts base64 encoded images from one image format to another with Archicad's own image converters, for example a PNG preview image to JPEG. The formats are Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG and PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can read or write. The output is aligned with the input array of images. Changes nothing in the project.

image.description: The base64 encoded image, for example a previewImage returned by GetElementPreviewImage.

inputFormat.description: The format of the image: Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG or PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can read (for example image/x-targa).

outputFormat.description: The format to convert the image to: Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG or PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can write.

images.description: The converted images in the order of the input, or an error.

example.description: ConvertImages converts base64 encoded images with Archicad's own converters. The formats are Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG and PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can read or write. Here the PNG preview image of an element is converted to JPEG, and to a MIME type format.

commands.name: GetCurrentWindowType
commands.description: Returns the type of the current (active) window and, when it has one, the databaseId of the database it shows, which ChangeWindow takes to bring the window back after a script switched to another one. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned, as Archicad does not tell which one it was.

databaseId.description: The database shown in the current (active) window, the same id GetDatabases and GetContainingDatabases return. Pass it to ChangeWindow to bring this window back. Missing when the window has no database of its own that can be identified, for example a report, a rendering or a custom add-on window. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned: Archicad does not tell which one it was, and several saved views can show the same database.

example.description: Prints the type and the database id of the current window with GetCurrentWindowType.
example.code:
"""Prints the type and the database id of the current window with GetCurrentWindowType."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowType'))

commands.name: GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale
commands.description: Returns the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, as its denominator: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Unlike GetViewSettings it needs no saved view. It reads the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts always return 1.0.

scale.description: The denominator of the drawing scale of the current window: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Always 1.0 for layouts.

example.description: Prints the drawing scale of the current window (100.0 for 1:100) with GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.
example.code:
"""Prints the drawing scale of the current window (100.0 for 1:100) with GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale'))

commands.name: SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale
commands.description: Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable.

scale.description: The denominator of the new drawing scale: 100 for 1:100, 20 for 1:20. Archicad accepts scales between 1 and 30000.

rebuild.description: Rebuild the window after the scale changed (the API's zoom flag). Default: false.

example.description: Sets the drawing scale of the current window to 1:50 with SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale, then restores it. Needs a window other than a layout (layouts are always 1:1).
example.code:
"""Sets the drawing scale of the current window to 1:50 with SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale, then restores it.

Needs a window other than a layout (layouts are always 1:1).
"""
import aclib

originalScale = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale')['scale']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale', {'scale': 50}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale')

commands.name: ShowNotificationBubble
commands.description: Shows a non-blocking notification bubble with a message in the current Archicad window, e.g. to report progress or a result without stopping the user as ShowAlert does. The bubble disappears by itself after the timeout. It is shown at a model coordinate or a pixel position of the current view, by default at the center of the current 2D view. Optionally it gets a large icon, is shown at most a given number of times, or is turned off, until the user runs 'Enable all informational messages'. Returns the bubble's settings read back from Archicad. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

message.description: The text of the notification bubble.

icon.description: The icon shown in the bubble. Default: information.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long the bubble stays, in milliseconds. Default: Archicad's default, 1000 (1 second).

coordinate.description: The model coordinate in the current database (meters) where the bubble is shown, converted like ModelToScreen does: in a 3D window it is projected with the current camera, in other windows z is disregarded. Do not give it together with screenPoint. When neither is given, the bubble is shown at the center of the current view in 2D windows and at the project's local origin otherwise.

screenPoint.description: The pixel position local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates) where the bubble is shown, e.g. a point returned by ModelToScreen. Do not give it together with coordinate.

h.description: Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.

v.description: Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

offset.description: Moves the bubble from its position by this many pixels.

h.description: Horizontal offset in pixels, positive to the right.

v.description: Vertical offset in pixels, positive downwards.

largeIcon.description: The icon shown instead of icon when the "Use large alert cues" option is on in Work Environment. Not set by default.

redrawCountLimit.description: Shows the bubble at most this many times. After that it does not appear again, for any later ShowNotificationBubble call, until the user runs the 'Enable all informational messages' command in Archicad. Not set by default.

disabled.description: True turns the bubble off instead of showing it: it does not appear again, for any later ShowNotificationBubble call, until the user runs the 'Enable all informational messages' command in Archicad. False (the default) changes nothing.

outputSchema.description: The settings of the bubble after the call, read back from Archicad.

text.description: The text of the bubble. Missing when it has none.

largeIcon.description: The icon shown when the "Use large alert cues" option is on in Work Environment.

offset.description: The offset of the bubble from its position, in pixels.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long the bubble stays, in milliseconds.

redrawCountLimit.description: How many times the bubble is shown at most. Missing when it has no limit.

example.description: Shows a non-blocking notification bubble in Archicad with ShowNotificationBubble and prints the bubble's settings. Unlike ShowAlert, the script and the user go on at once; the bubble disappears after the timeout. Without a coordinate or screenPoint it is shown at the center of the current 2D view. largeIcon is used when "Use large alert cues" is on in Work Environment. The response is the bubble's text, icons, offset, timeout and redraw count limit as Archicad reports them. redrawCountLimit and disabled (not used here) stop the bubble from appearing until the user runs 'Enable all informational messages'. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Shows a non-blocking notification bubble in Archicad with ShowNotificationBubble and prints the bubble's settings.

Unlike ShowAlert, the script and the user go on at once; the bubble disappears after the timeout.
Without a coordinate or screenPoint it is shown at the center of the current 2D view. largeIcon is used
when "Use large alert cues" is on in Work Environment. The response is the bubble's text, icons, offset,
timeout and redraw count limit as Archicad reports them. redrawCountLimit and disabled (not used here)
stop the bubble from appearing until the user runs 'Enable all informational messages'.
Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ShowNotificationBubble', {
    'message': 'Tapir: the script has finished.',
    'icon': 'information',
    'timeoutMilliseconds': 3000,
    'largeIcon': 'information'
}))

example.code:
"""Creates a custom Project Info field, moves it to the top of the first group with MoveProjectInfoFields, then deletes it.

Requires Archicad 30 or later.
"""
import aclib

firstGroup = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoGroups')['projectInfoGroups'][0]

created = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateProjectInfoFields', {
    'projectInfoFields': [{'projectInfoName': 'Tapir Example Field', 'projectInfoGroupId': firstGroup['projectInfoGroupId']}]
})['fields'][0]
if 'projectInfoFieldId' not in created:
    raise SystemExit ('The field could not be created.')
fieldId = created['projectInfoFieldId']

move = {'projectInfoFieldId': fieldId, 'projectInfoGroupId': firstGroup['projectInfoGroupId']}
if firstGroup['fields']:
    move['beforeProjectInfoFieldId'] = firstGroup['fields'][0]['projectInfoFieldId']
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MoveProjectInfoFields', {'projectInfoFields': [move]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoGroups')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectInfoFields', {'projectInfoFieldIds': [{'projectInfoFieldId': fieldId}]})

stories = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')['stories']
original = [
    {'index': s['index'], 'dispOnSections': s['dispOnSections'], 'level': s['level'], 'name': s['name']}
    for s in stories
]

changed = [dict (s) for s in original]
changed[-1]['name'] = 'Tapir Top Story'
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetStories', {'stories': changed}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetStories', {'stories': original}))

commands.name: GetAutoTextKeys
commands.description: Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. elementId.description: Optional. The element to retrieve context dependent autotext keys for (its own properties, plus the ones common to all element types, e.g. 'Element ID', 'Area'). When omitted, only the property based autotext keys common to all element types are returned. The other autotexts (Project Info, layout, drawing, date, ...) are returned either way.

name.description: The autotext's name, as shown in the Insert Autotext dialog of Archicad.

key.description: The autotext's key. To embed it in the content of a Text or Label element, surround it with '<' and '>', e.g. '<PROJECTNAME>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>'.

commands.name: InterpretAutoTexts

}))

commands.name: GetHotlinks
commands.description: Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules and the instance elements placed from each node. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.

commands.name: CreateHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink module nodes to create. A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).

name.description: Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

storyRangeType.description: Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

refFloorIndex.description: Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

hotlinkNodes.description: One item per requested node, in order: the node guid with its existing flag, or an error.

example.description: Saves the first wall as a module in the temp folder, creates a hotlink node from it with CreateHotlinkNodes, then deletes the node. Needs at least one Wall.

commands.name: CreateHotlinkInstances
commands.description: Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring.

example.description: Places an instance of a hotlink node at (50, 0), rotated by 30 degrees, with CreateHotlinkInstances. The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Places an instance of a hotlink node at (50, 0), rotated by 30 degrees, with CreateHotlinkInstances.

The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is
deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import math
import os
import tempfile
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
modulePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'TapirExample.mod')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SaveAsModuleFile', {'moduleFilePath': modulePath, 'elements': walls})
nodeId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkNodes', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'sourceLocation': modulePath}]})['hotlinkNodes'][0]['hotlinkNodeId']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkInstances', {
    'hotlinkInstances': [{
        'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId,
        'origin': {'x': 50.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'rotationAngle': math.radians (30),
        'mirrored': False
    }]
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteHotlinkNodes', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId}]})

commands.name: ChangeHotlinkInstances
commands.description: Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances.

hotlinkInstances.description: The placed hotlink instances to change. Every field but elementId is optional; a field that is omitted keeps its current value.

example.description: Moves the first placed hotlink instance 1 m along x with ChangeHotlinkInstances, then moves it back. Needs at least one placed Hotlink.

commands.name: UpdateHotlinks
commands.description: Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to update, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. Each node's cached content is re-read from its source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

example.description: Re-reads the source files of every top-level hotlink node with UpdateHotlinks, as the Hotlink Manager's Update does. Needs at least one hotlink.

commands.name: ChangeHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content.

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to repoint at another source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. The placed instances stay where they are. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks on the same nodes to re-read the content from the new file.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the new module source file (.mod or .pln).

example.description: Relinks the first hotlink node to a copy of its source file in the temp folder with ChangeHotlinkNodes, then back. Needs at least one hotlink whose source is a file on disk.
example.code:
"""Relinks the first hotlink node to a copy of its source file in the temp folder with ChangeHotlinkNodes, then back.

Needs at least one hotlink whose source is a file on disk.
"""
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import aclib

hotlinks = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotlinks')['hotlinks']
if not hotlinks:
    raise SystemExit ('No hotlink in the project.')
node = hotlinks[0]

copyPath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), os.path.basename (node['location']))
shutil.copyfile (node['location'], copyPath)

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeHotlinkNodes', {
    'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId'], 'sourceLocation': copyPath}]
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UpdateHotlinks', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId']}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotlinks')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeHotlinkNodes', {
    'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId'], 'sourceLocation': node['location']}]
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UpdateHotlinks', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId']}]})

commands.name: BreakHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Breaks hotlink nodes, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does: the elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file.

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to break, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. The elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does. In Teamwork the Hotlink and XRef management has to be reserved first (ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement).

example.description: Places a hotlink made from the first wall and breaks it with BreakHotlinkNodes. The node's source is the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder. After the break the placed copy of the wall stays in the project as an ordinary wall at (50, 0). Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Places a hotlink made from the first wall and breaks it with BreakHotlinkNodes.

The node's source is the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder. After the break the
placed copy of the wall stays in the project as an ordinary wall at (50, 0). Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import os
import tempfile
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
modulePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'TapirExample.mod')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SaveAsModuleFile', {'moduleFilePath': modulePath, 'elements': walls})
nodeId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkNodes', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'sourceLocation': modulePath}]})['hotlinkNodes'][0]['hotlinkNodeId']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkInstances', {'hotlinkInstances': [{'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId, 'origin': {'x': 50.0, 'y': 0.0}}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('BreakHotlinkNodes', {
    'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId}]
}))

commands.name: DeleteHotlinkNodes

In Teamwork the Hotlink and XRef management has to be reserved first (ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement).

    'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId}]

commands.name: SaveProject

commands.name: SaveProjectAsArchive

commands.name: PhotoRender
commands.description: Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene, or with the given one, as Document > Creative Imaging > PhotoRender Projection does, and saves the image to a file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif). example.description: Gets what the 3D window shows as a png with GetCurrentViewImage and writes it to the temp folder. Needs the 3D window to be open. Requires Archicad 30 or later.
example.code:
"""Gets what the 3D window shows as a png with GetCurrentViewImage and writes it to the temp folder.

Needs the 3D window to be open. Requires Archicad 30 or later.
"""
import base64
import os
import tempfile
import aclib

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentViewImage', {'source': '3DWindow', 'format': 'png'})
if not response or 'image' not in response:
    raise SystemExit ('No image: {}'.format (response))

filePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'Tapir3DWindow.png')
with open (filePath, 'wb') as imageFile:
    imageFile.write (base64.b64decode (response['image']))
print ('Saved the {}x{} image to {}'.format (response['width'], response['height'], filePath))

commands.name: ResolveNames
commands.description: Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters), or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and deterministic. Read only.

names.description: The words or phrases to look up in the open project, for example taken from a user's question.

name.description: The word or phrase.

kind.description: The kind of item the word names. When it is left out, every kind is searched.

maxCloseMatches.description: The most close matches returned for one word, best first. The default is 5.

results.description: One result for each of the given names, in the same order.

name.description: The given word or phrase.

status.description: found: an item of the project has exactly this name (see found). closeMatches: no item has exactly this name, but some are close (see closeMatches). notFound: nothing in the project is close to it; the project has no such item, so it must not be guessed.

found.description: The items named exactly so (the same characters), with match 'exact'. More than one when items of different kinds, or several stories, have the name.

closeMatches.description: When nothing is named exactly so: the nearest items, best first. Empty when the status is found or notFound.

example.description: Checks words from a user's question against the open project with ResolveNames before using them: a story, a building material, an element type, a property, a classification and a word looked up among every kind of name. Each result says whether the project has an item named exactly so (found), only similar names (closeMatches, best first) or nothing close (notFound). A matched property carries the propertyId that GetPropertyValuesOfElements takes, a matched classification item its classificationSystemId and classificationItemId.
example.code:
"""Checks words from a user's question against the open project with ResolveNames before using them:
a story, a building material, an element type, a property, a classification and a word looked up
among every kind of name. Each result says whether the project has an item named exactly so (found),
only similar names (closeMatches, best first) or nothing close (notFound). A matched property carries
the propertyId that GetPropertyValuesOfElements takes, a matched classification item its
classificationSystemId and classificationItemId."""
import aclib

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ResolveNames', {
    'names': [
        {'name': 'ground floor', 'kind': 'Story'},
        {'name': 'concrete', 'kind': 'BuildingMaterial'},
        {'name': 'door', 'kind': 'ElementType'},
        {'name': 'fire rating', 'kind': 'Property'},
        {'name': 'wall', 'kind': 'Classification'},
        {'name': 'Fire Rating'}
    ],
    'maxCloseMatches': 3
})
aclib.PrintJson (response)

for result in response['results']:
    matches = result['found'] or result['closeMatches']
    print (result['name'], '->', result['status'], [(match['kind'], match['name']) for match in matches])

commands.name: SetElementUserData
commands.description: Stores string values under keys on elements, for scripts to keep their own state per element (external database ids, sync timestamps, markers). The data is saved with the project as the user data of the Tapir add-on on the element and appears nowhere in the Archicad UI. The given keys are merged into what the element already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. One undo step per call; in a Teamwork project the element has to be reserved.

elementUserData.description: The elements with the key-value pairs to store on them. Each item needs userData, keysToDelete or both.

userData.description: The key-value pairs to store on the element. A key that already exists on the element gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

key.description: The key of the value. Scripts should prefix their keys (for example 'myscript.databaseId') so that different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

value.description: The value to store. Any text, for example an id, a timestamp or a JSON document the script encodes itself.

keysToDelete.description: The keys to remove from the element. A key the element does not hold is ignored.

executionResults.description: One result per input item, in the input order.

example.description: Stores a key-value pair on the first wall with SetElementUserData, reads it back, then removes it. The data is saved with the project, invisible in the Archicad UI. Needs at least one Wall.

commands.name: GetElementUserData
commands.description: Reads the values stored on elements by SetElementUserData: every key of each element, or only the given keys.

keys.description: Optional. Only the pairs with these keys are returned; a key an element does not hold is left out of its pairs. When omitted, every pair stored on each element is returned.

elementUserData.description: One item per element, in the input order: the pairs stored on the element (none when the element holds no user data of Tapir), or an error when the element was not found or its data could not be read.

userData.description: The key-value pairs stored on the element.

value.description: The stored value.

Needs at least one Wall.

if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementUserData', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: CaptureElementState
commands.description: Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier.

type.description: How GetElementChangesSince finds the changed elements between this state and another one. ModificationStamp (the default) compares the modification stamps of the elements, so any change to a tracked element counts. 3DModel compares the 3D model of the elements, so only a change that alters the 3D model counts, and capturing it generates the 3D model of the project. Two states can only be compared when they were captured with the same type. With either type the changes come from Archicad's element difference generator, which tracks the model elements: 2D elements such as texts, labels and hatches can be missing from the result even when they were created, modified or deleted.

stateId.description: The identifier of the captured state, accepted by GetElementChangesSince and ReleaseElementState. It is only valid in the Archicad session and project it was captured in.

type.description: The type the state was captured with.

example.description: Captures the current state of the project's elements with CaptureElementState. GetElementChangesSince can compare a later state to it. The script releases the state at the end.
example.code:
"""Captures the current state of the project's elements with CaptureElementState.

GetElementChangesSince can compare a later state to it. The script releases the state at the end.
"""
import aclib

state = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CaptureElementState', {'type': 'ModificationStamp'})
print ('Captured state: {}'.format (state['stateId']['guid']))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElementState', {'stateId': state['stateId']})

commands.name: GetElementChangesSince
commands.description: Returns the new, modified and deleted elements between a state captured by CaptureElementState and either another captured state (toStateId) or the current state of the project. Scripts that keep an external copy of the model use it to sync only what changed instead of re-reading every element. The changes come from Archicad's element difference generator, which tracks the model elements: 2D elements such as texts, labels and hatches can be missing from the lists, so read those directly. Fails for a stateId that is unknown - never captured, released, or lost because the project was closed or Archicad restarted.

stateId.description: The state to compare from, as returned by CaptureElementState.

toStateId.description: The state to compare to, as returned by CaptureElementState with the same type as stateId. If omitted, the current state of the project is used, so the response lists what changed since stateId was captured.

newElements.description: The elements that exist in the later state but not in the earlier one.

modifiedElements.description: The elements that exist in both states and changed between them.

deletedElements.description: The elements that exist in the earlier state but not in the later one. They cannot be read any more, only their identifiers are known.

example.description: Lists what changed since a captured state with GetElementChangesSince. Captures a state, creates a wall, reads the changes (the new wall), then deletes the wall and releases the state.
example.code:
"""Lists what changed since a captured state with GetElementChangesSince.

Captures a state, creates a wall, reads the changes (the new wall), then deletes the wall and releases the state.
"""
import aclib

stateId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CaptureElementState', {})['stateId']

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements']

changes = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementChangesSince', {'stateId': stateId})
print ('{} new, {} modified, {} deleted elements.'.format (
    len (changes['newElements']), len (changes['modifiedElements']), len (changes['deletedElements'])))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElementState', {'stateId': stateId})

commands.name: ReleaseElementState
commands.description: Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState. Every state is freed anyway when the project is closed or Archicad quits.

stateId.description: The state to free, as returned by CaptureElementState.

example.description: Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState with ReleaseElementState. States are freed anyway when the project is closed; releasing them earlier frees their temporary file.
example.code:

States are freed anyway when the project is closed; releasing them earlier frees their temporary file.
"""

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElementState', {'stateId': stateId}))

commands.name: GetMarquee
commands.description: Gets the marquee of the current window: its shape (rectangle, rotated rectangle or polygon), whether it is multi-story, and its outline as a polygon. Returns the type 'none' when there is no marquee.

type.description: The shape of the marquee in the current window, or 'none' when there is no marquee.

multiStory.description: True for a multi-story (thick) marquee, false for a single-story (thin) one. Absent when there is no marquee.

box.description: The rectangle of a 'rectangle' or 'rotatedRectangle' marquee. For a rotated rectangle it is given as Archicad stores it: in the coordinate system rotated by rotationAngle around the project origin, not around the box itself. Use polygon for the corners on the plan.

rotationAngle.description: The rotation angle (radians) of a 'rotatedRectangle' marquee.

polygon.description: The vertices of the marquee outline on the plan, each listed once: the four corners of a 'rectangle' or 'rotatedRectangle' marquee, the vertices of a 'polygon' marquee.

example.description: Reads the marquee of the current window with GetMarquee: its shape, whether it is multi-story, and its outline. The type is 'none' when there is no marquee.

The type is 'none' when there is no marquee.
