commands.name: SetMarquee
commands.description: Draws a marquee in the current window from a polygon or a box (optionally rotated), single- or multi-story. Called without polygon and box it removes the marquee.

polygon.description: The vertices of a polygon marquee, in order. The polygon is closed automatically; a repeated first vertex at the end is accepted. Give either polygon or box.

box.description: A rectangle marquee. With rotationAngle it is a rotated rectangle, and the box is read the way Archicad stores it (see GetMarquee): in the coordinate system rotated by rotationAngle around the project origin. Give either polygon or box.

rotationAngle.description: Rotation angle (radians) of the box around the project origin. Only together with box. The default is 0: a horizontal rectangle.

multiStory.description: True for a multi-story (thick) marquee, false for a single-story (thin) one. The default is false.

example.description: Draws a 10 x 10 m rectangle marquee around the origin with SetMarquee, then reads it back. The original marquee (or no marquee) is restored at the end.

commands.name: FilterElements
commands.description: Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices), element type (elementTypes) and hotlink (fromHotlink, hotlinkIds). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.

filters.description: Optional. Archicad's own flag filters. An element is kept only when it fulfills all of them.

layerIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when it is on one of these layers (the layerIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

floorIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its home story is one of these (the floorIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

elementTypes.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its type is one of these.

fromHotlink.description: Optional. true keeps only the elements that came in through a placed hotlink (they are read-only), false only the project's own elements.

hotlinkIds.description: Optional. An element is kept only when it came in through one of these placed hotlink instances (the hotlinkId field of GetDetailsOfElements, elements of type Hotlink).

example.description: Keeps only the editable walls and slabs of all elements with FilterElements.
example.code:
"""Keeps only the editable walls and slabs of all elements with FilterElements."""
import aclib

elements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllElements', {})['elements']

filtered = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FilterElements', {
    'elements': elements,
    'filters': ['IsEditable'],
    'elementTypes': ['Wall', 'Slab']
})['elements']

print ('{} of {} elements are editable walls or slabs.'.format (len (filtered), len (elements)))

commands.name: GetElementsByCriteria
commands.description: Returns the elements, or with countOnly only their number, that match all the given criteria: element types, home stories, layers, Archicad's element filter flags and property criteria (a value compared in internal units, or a value status such as hasValue, isUserUndefined, isNotAvailable, isDefault or hasCustomValue). An unknown type, property or operator is an error, not ignored. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

layerIndices.description: Optional filter for layer attribute indices.

filters.description: Optional Archicad API element filter flags. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs, railings and curtain walls) are left out unless IncludeSubElemObjects is given, as in GetElementsByType and GetAllElements.

propertyCriteria.description: Optional list of property evaluation criteria. All criteria must match (AND condition).

propertyName.description: Case-insensitive property definition name, as shown in the project's language. An error is returned when it matches no property, or properties in more than one group and propertyGroupName is not given. Prefer propertyId in scripts that must work in any language.

propertyGroupName.description: Case-insensitive property group name, to choose between properties of the same name in different groups.

operator.description: Evaluation operator. Default is 'equals'. hasValue (alias hasAnyValue) matches a property with a value, isUserUndefined (alias isUndefined) one set to undefined by the user, isNotAvailable one that does not apply to the element. isDefault matches a property whose value comes from its default, hasCustomValue one whose value was set on the element (also to undefined). Archicad gives the default status only together with the evaluated value, so isDefault and hasCustomValue take as long as reading the value, also for expression properties.

value.description: Expected value as a string. Required for the comparison operators. For number, integer, length, area, volume and angle properties, equals, notEquals and the range operators compare numbers in internal units (m, m², m³, rad) written with a decimal point, independent of the project's display settings; other properties compare the displayed text, case-insensitively.

countOnly.description: If true, only returns the count of matching elements without listing their GUIDs. Minimizes token usage.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching elements to list. The count is still the total number of matches.

elements.description: List of matching elements.

example.description: Finds walls by story and by a property value with GetElementsByCriteria, first counting them only. The property criterion compares the wall thickness in metres, whatever the project's display units.

commands.name: GetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the details of elements (geometry parameters etc). When elements is omitted, all elements matching the optional server-side filter (types, floorIndices, layerIndices) are queried; an empty elements list returns no details. Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need (e.g. elementId, type, id, floorIndex) and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). Use the optional additionalFields parameter to also get the info string, the compound info string, the library part unique ID and the creator tool unique ID. An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true.

elements.description: Optional list of elements to get details for. When omitted, all elements in the current database (optionally filtered by the filter parameter) are used; an empty list returns no details.

fields.description: Optional filter for the fields to return for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.

filter.description: Optional server-side filter. Without elements, only the elements matching it are returned. A listed element that does not match it gets an error entry in its place.

additionalFields.description: Optional extra fields to return for each element, on top of the ones selected by fields. None of them is returned unless listed here, so callers that do not give this parameter get the same response as before.

detailsOfElements.description: One entry per input element, in the same order as the input elements array. An element that cannot be read, or that does not match the filter, gets an error entry in its place, so the position of an entry tells which input element it belongs to. Without elements, one entry per element that matches the filter.

example.description: Reads the details (type, story, layer, geometry etc.) of the first walls with GetDetailsOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. The second call asks only for the fields it needs, which is faster. The third gives no elements but a filter, so it reads every wall of the ground floor in one call.
example.code:
"""Reads the details (type, story, layer, geometry etc.) of the first walls with GetDetailsOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall. The second call asks only for the fields it needs, which is faster. The
third gives no elements but a filter, so it reads every wall of the ground floor in one call.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': walls, 'fields': ['id', 'floorIndex', 'layerIndex']}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {
    'filter': {'types': ['Wall'], 'floorIndices': [0]},
    'fields': ['elementId', 'id', 'layerIndex']
}))

commands.name: SetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Sets the details of the given elements. Every element type: Element ID (id), story (floorIndex), layer (layerIndex) and display order (drawIndex). In typeSpecificDetails: Wall - start and end point, height, base offset, and the start and end thickness of a trapezoid wall; Zone - the ZoneSettings fields (the same as ModifyZones); Line - start and end point, pen, line type, room separator; Arc and Circle - origin, radius, angle, ratio, start and end angle (arcs only), reflected, pen, line type, room separator; Polyline - points and arcs, pen, line type, room separator; Spline - pen, line type, room separator; Hatch - outline, holes, contour pen, fill pen and background pen or colors, fill or building material, area display, room special and fill orientation; Hotspot - position, height, pen; Text - text, position, angle, height, justification; Label - the text of a text label; Drawing - position, angle, ratio, model offset, clip polygon (isCutWithFrame), name, ID and numbering, scale in Autotext, border, title library part, pen table (penTableUsageMode, penTableIndex), colorMode, isTransparentBackground, rasterizeDPI and the anchor (anchorPoint, useOwnOriginAsAnchor). Not written, because the Archicad API does not take them: the geometry of a Spline, the source of a Drawing (use ChangeDrawingLink), the Drawing Manager's update type and stored in project, and often a placed Drawing's drawingScale, which comes from its source view (the element's result then names the kept value). Other wall, slab, column, beam, stair and object settings are written by their Modify commands. An element Archicad does not let you edit (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not reserved by you in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason; a Drawing setting Archicad kept unchanged is named in a failed execution result too.

id.description: The Element ID (the ID field of the element's Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels). The same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id.

example.description: Raises the height of a wall by 0.5 m with SetDetailsOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Wall. The keys of typeSpecificDetails depend on the element type, for example a Drawing takes {'penTableUsageMode': 'ModelPenTable', 'colorMode': 'Grayscale', 'isTransparentBackground': True, 'anchorPoint': 'BottomLeft'}; the command's description lists them for every type. GetDetailsOfElements returns the same keys.
example.code:
"""Raises the height of a wall by 0.5 m with SetDetailsOfElements, reads it back, then restores it.

Needs at least one editable Wall. The keys of typeSpecificDetails depend on the element type, for
example a Drawing takes {'penTableUsageMode': 'ModelPenTable', 'colorMode': 'Grayscale',
'isTransparentBackground': True, 'anchorPoint': 'BottomLeft'}; the command's description lists them
for every type. GetDetailsOfElements returns the same keys.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')
wallId = walls[0]['elementId']

def GetHeight ():
    details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': walls, 'fields': ['details']})
    return details['detailsOfElements'][0]['details']['height']

originalHeight = GetHeight ()

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetDetailsOfElements', {
    'elementsWithDetails': [{'elementId': wallId, 'details': {'typeSpecificDetails': {'height': originalHeight + 0.5}}}]
}))
print ('Height: {:.3f} m -> {:.3f} m'.format (originalHeight, GetHeight ()))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetDetailsOfElements', {
    'elementsWithDetails': [{'elementId': wallId, 'details': {'typeSpecificDetails': {'height': originalHeight}}}]
})

commands.name: SetElementInfoStrings
commands.description: Sets the info string of the given elements: the Element ID shown in the Info Box, which GetDetailsOfElements returns as id. Returns one execution result per element.

example.description: Changes the Element ID of a wall with SetElementInfoStrings, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Wall.

commands.name: GetElementCategories
commands.description: Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status, Renovation Filter and, in the German version, BRI) with their possible values. The names of the categories and values are localized: identify a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name.

categories.description: The element categories of the project, each with its possible values.

example.description: Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) and their values with GetElementCategories. The names are localized; scripts should pick a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId.
example.code:
"""Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) and their values with GetElementCategories.

The names are localized; scripts should pick a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId.
"""
import aclib

categories = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementCategories', {})['categories']
for category in categories:
    print ('{} ({}): {}'.format (category['type'], category['name'], ', '.join (value['name'] for value in category['values'])))

commands.name: GetCategoryValuesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, optionally only for the given category types. An element that has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

categories.description: The categories to read. Left out: every category the element has.

categoryValuesOfElements.description: The category values of each element, in the order of the input. A category the element does not have is left out of its list; an element that does not exist or has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) is represented by an error object.

example.description: Reads the Structural Function and Position of the first walls with GetCategoryValuesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. Without categories every category of the elements is returned.
example.code:
"""Reads the Structural Function and Position of the first walls with GetCategoryValuesOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall. Without categories every category of the elements is returned.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCategoryValuesOfElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'categories': ['StructuralFunction', 'Position']
}))

commands.name: GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults
commands.description: Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the tool defaults of the given element types, the values new elements of the type get, optionally only for the given category types. A category the default has no value in is listed without categoryValueId; an element type without any of the requested categories gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

elementTypes.description: The element types whose tool defaults (the settings new elements get) are read.

categories.description: The categories to read. Left out: every category of the project.

categoryValuesOfDefaults.description: The category values of the tool defaults of each element type, in the order of the input. A category Archicad cannot read for the type is left out of its list; an invalid element type, or one with none of the requested categories, is represented by an error object.

categoryValueId.description: Left out when the default has no value in this category.

name.description: The localized name of the value, for display only. Left out when the default has no value in this category.

example.description: Reads the category values new walls, slabs and columns get from their tool defaults, with GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.

commands.name: SetCategoryValuesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value in the category now (oldValue) and the value a real run would set (newValue).

elementCategoryValues.description: The category values to set: one element and one category per item. The same element can appear in several items, one per category.

executionResults.description: One result per item of the input, in the same order. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the category and the value exist, the element exists and has the category) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value in the category now and newValue the value a real run would set, both as GetCategoryValuesOfElements gives them (type, categoryId, categoryValueId and name; oldValue has only type and categoryId when the element has no value in the category). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them.

example.description: Changes the Structural Function of a wall with SetCategoryValuesOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Wall.

commands.name: Get3DBoundingBoxes
commands.description: Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements. An element without 3D geometry of its own gets an error item instead of a bounding box. Walls, Slabs, Roofs, Zones and Stairs are measured on their 3D model, so the box of a Wall includes its connections to other walls. The current window does not need to show the element: it works with a layout or a section open as well.

example.description: Reads the 3D bounding boxes of the first walls with Get3DBoundingBoxes. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Reads the 3D bounding boxes of the first walls with Get3DBoundingBoxes.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get3DBoundingBoxes', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: Get2DBoundingBoxes
commands.description: Get the 2D bounding box of elements as Archicad draws them, in the coordinates of the database the element is in: the floor plan, a section, a worksheet, a layout or a master layout. Works for 2D elements (Line, PolyLine, Arc, Hatch, Text, Label, Dimension, Drawing ...) as well as for model elements; a Text's box covers its drawn lines, a Drawing's box its frame with the title. The current window does not need to show the element. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements.

example.description: Reads the 2D bounding boxes of the first walls, as Archicad draws them on the floor plan, with Get2DBoundingBoxes. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get2DBoundingBoxes', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: GetLibPartTransformations
commands.description: Gets the placement transformation of library part instances (Window, Door, Object, Lamp, Zone) as Archicad computes it: the location, the rotation angle and the x/y scaling. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

transformations.description: The placement transformation of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

example.description: Reads the location, rotation angle and scaling of the first placed objects, windows and doors with GetLibPartTransformations. Needs at least one Object, Window or Door.
example.code:
"""Reads the location, rotation angle and scaling of the first placed objects, windows and doors with GetLibPartTransformations.

Needs at least one Object, Window or Door.
"""

elements = []
for elementType in ['Object', 'Window', 'Door']:
    elements += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': elementType})['elements']
if not elements:
    raise SystemExit ('No object, window or door in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLibPartTransformations', {'elements': elements[:5]}))

commands.name: GetSnapPointsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the snap points (hotspots) of the given elements, of any element type: the points of an element that the cursor snaps to and dimensions attach to (for example the endpoints of a Wall's reference line or the vertices of a Slab), in world coordinates, each with the neig kind and subindex identifying which point of the element it is. For the 2D hotspots of library part instances see GetHotspotsOfElements. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

snapPointsOfElements.description: The snap points (hotspots) of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

snapPoints.description: The snap points (hotspots) of the element: the points Archicad snaps to and dimensions attach to, in world coordinates (meters, absolute Z). Empty when the element has none.

neigId.description: Which kind of point of the element the hotspot is, as the DevKit's API_NeigID enumerator value of its neig (for example the begin or end point of a Wall's reference line, or a vertex of a Slab's polygon).

inIndex.description: Subindex of the point within its kind (API_Neig inIndex), for example the vertex index in the element's polygon.

example.description: Reads the snap points (hotspots) of a wall with GetSnapPointsOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Reads the snap points (hotspots) of a wall with GetSnapPointsOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSnapPointsOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: ConvertRevealOffsets
commands.description: Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27.

openings.description: Windows and doors placed in walls, each with exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset.

revealOffsets.description: The reveal depth offset of each opening in both references, aligned with the input, or an error.

example.description: Converts a reveal depth offset of 0 measured from the wall's core skin to the wall side reference with ConvertRevealOffsets. Needs at least one Window or Door placed in a wall. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: Get3DGeometryOfElements
commands.description: Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.

geometries3D.description: The 3D geometry of each element, aligned with the input: the solid bodies of its 3D model, or an error.

example.description: Reads the 3D geometry (vertices and faces of the solid bodies) of a wall with Get3DGeometryOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Reads the 3D geometry (vertices and faces of the solid bodies) of a wall with Get3DGeometryOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

geometry = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get3DGeometryOfElements', {'elements': walls})['geometries3D'][0]
for body in geometry.get ('bodies', []):
    print ('Body with {} vertices and {} faces'.format (len (body['vertices']), len (body['polygons'])))

commands.name: GetElementConnections
commands.description: Gets the connections among the given elements: each pair of touching elements once, with the polygons of the surface where they touch, in world coordinates. The 3D model of the elements is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. Also returns, aligned with the input array of elements, whether each element was found. Available from Archicad 28.

elements.description: The elements to search connections among. Only connections between two of these elements are returned.

connections.description: The connected pairs of the given elements. Each pair appears once.

polygons.description: The polygons of the surface where the two elements touch, in world coordinates. The last point of a polygon repeats its first.

executionResults.description: Aligned with the input array of elements: whether the element was found and taken into the search.

example.description: Finds where the walls and slabs of the project touch each other with GetElementConnections. Needs Walls or Slabs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Finds where the walls and slabs of the project touch each other with GetElementConnections.

Needs Walls or Slabs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

elements = []
for elementType in ['Wall', 'Slab']:
    elements += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': elementType})['elements']
if not elements:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall or slab in the project.')

connections = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementConnections', {'elements': elements})['connections']
for connection in connections:
    print ('{} touches {}'.format (connection['elementId1']['guid'], connection['elementId2']['guid']))

commands.name: GetBodyMaterialsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the building material of each body of the 3D model of the given elements. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.

bodyMaterials.description: The bodies of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

bodies.description: The bodies of the element's 3D model generated with separate components: a composite structure has one body per skin. Empty when the element has no 3D model.

bodyIndex.description: The index of the body in the element, starting from 0.

buildingMaterialId.description: The building material of the body. Left out when it cannot be found among the attributes of the project.

buildingMaterialName.description: The name of the building material. Left out together with buildingMaterialId.

example.description: Reads the building material of each body of the 3D model of the first walls with GetBodyMaterialsOfElements. A composite wall has one body per skin. Needs at least one Wall. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Reads the building material of each body of the 3D model of the first walls with GetBodyMaterialsOfElements.

A composite wall has one body per skin. Needs at least one Wall. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetBodyMaterialsOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: GetCutPolygonsOfElements
commands.description: Cuts each body of the 3D model of the given elements with a plane and returns, for each body, its building material, the area of the cut surface and its polygons (outline and holes) in 2D coordinates of the plane. From Archicad 28 the 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. Before Archicad 28 the bodies are those of the element's 3D model (a composite structure is one body) and their building materials are left out. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

cutPlane.description: The cutting plane. axisX, axisY and axisZ should be unit vectors perpendicular to each other; axisZ is the normal of the plane.

basePoint.description: A point of the plane, the origin of the returned 2D coordinates.

axisX.description: The direction of the x axis of the returned 2D coordinates.

axisY.description: The direction of the y axis of the returned 2D coordinates.

cutPolygons.description: The cut of each body of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

bodies.description: The bodies of the element's 3D model generated with separate components: a composite structure has one body per skin. Empty when the element has no 3D model.

bodyIndex.description: The index of the body in the element, starting from 0.

buildingMaterialId.description: The building material of the body. Left out when it cannot be found among the attributes of the project.

buildingMaterialName.description: The name of the building material. Left out together with buildingMaterialId.

area.description: The area of the cut surface of the body. 0 when the plane does not cut the body.

polygons.description: The polygons of the cut surface of the body, in 2D coordinates of the plane (basePoint, axisX, axisY). Curved edges are given by their end points. Empty when the plane does not cut the body.

example.description: Cuts the first walls with a horizontal plane 1 m above project zero with GetCutPolygonsOfElements. Returns the building material, cut area and cut polygons of each body. Needs at least one Wall. On Archicad 25-27 the building materials are left out.

commands.name: GetElementAtCoordinate
commands.description: Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser.

elementType.description: The type of the element to look for. Only polygonal element types can be searched, for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch.

coordinate.description: The point to search at, in the project's coordinates, on the floor plan of the current database.

z.description: Optional. The elevation of the search point, handed to Archicad together with the coordinate. Default is 0; without z a point 1 mm higher is also tried, so an element whose top is at 0 (for example a slab at the story level) is found.

filters.description: Optional. Only an element passing every given filter is found (the same values as FilterElements accepts).

found.description: True when an element of the given type was found at the coordinate.

elementId.description: The identifier of the found element. Absent when nothing was found.

example.description: Finds the Slab at a point of the floor plan, the way a click there would, with GetElementAtCoordinate. The point is the average of the first slab's outline vertices. Needs at least one Slab.
example.code:
"""Finds the Slab at a point of the floor plan, the way a click there would, with GetElementAtCoordinate.

The point is the average of the first slab's outline vertices. Needs at least one Slab.
"""
import aclib

slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Slab'})['elements'][:1]
if not slabs:
    raise SystemExit ('No slab in the project.')

outline = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': slabs, 'fields': ['details']})['detailsOfElements'][0]['details']['polygonOutline']
point = {'x': sum (c['x'] for c in outline) / len (outline), 'y': sum (c['y'] for c in outline) / len (outline)}

commands.name: GetQuantitiesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. commands.name: TriangulatePolygonsOfElements

triangulations.description: The triangulation of the polygon of each element, aligned with the input: its triangles (or with convex: true its convex polygons), or an error (for example for an element type that has no polygon).

With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that exists gets wouldDelete.

commands.name: FinishHierarchicalEditing
commands.description: Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). Requires Archicad 27 or later.

When no editing mode is open, it fails with "not in a hierarchical editing mode". Requires Archicad 27 or later.

includeMarkers.description: Whether the objects attached to the elements (window and door markers, drawing titles, ...) are drawn with them. When omitted, Archicad's current setting is used. The setting is changed back after the drawing.

shapePrimitivesOfElements.description: The drawing primitives of each element, in the order of the input elements.

example.code:
"""GetShapePrimitivesOfElements draws the elements as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrims draws them by default, in

afterwards. The floor plan must be the current database.
"""

from collections import Counter

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    print ('No walls in the project.')
    raise SystemExit (0)

for includeMarkers in [True, False]:
    result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetShapePrimitivesOfElements', {
        'elements': walls[:3],
        'includeMarkers': includeMarkers
    })
    if result is None or 'shapePrimitivesOfElements' not in result:
        print ('Failed: {}'.format (result))
        raise SystemExit (1)

    print ('=' * 30)
    print ('includeMarkers: {}'.format (includeMarkers))
    for wall, shapePrimitives in zip (walls, result['shapePrimitivesOfElements']):
        if 'error' in shapePrimitives:
            print ('Wall {}: error {}'.format (wall['elementId']['guid'], shapePrimitives['error']['message']))
            continue
        primitives = shapePrimitives['primitives']
        print ('Wall {}: {} primitives {}'.format (
            wall['elementId']['guid'], len (primitives), dict (Counter (p['type'] for p in primitives))))

This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires.

databases.description: The section, elevation or interior elevation databases to list the section elements of. If omitted, the current database is used.

sectionElements.description: The elements drawn in the given databases, each with the owner element it was generated from.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of the section element itself, accepted by CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection as sectionElementId.

ownerElementId.description: The identifier of the owner element the section element was generated from - this is what every other listing command returns.

ownerElementType.description: The type of the owner element. Only present when the owner's header is readable from the section database.

commands.name: LinkElements
commands.description: Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.

links.description: The links to create, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

example.description: Links the first wall to the second one with LinkElements, reads the link back, then removes it. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way. Needs at least two Walls.

commands.name: UnlinkElements
commands.description: Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable.

links.description: The links to remove, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

example.description: Removes a link created by LinkElements with UnlinkElements. Links the first wall to the second one first, so it needs at least two Walls. Only the link in the given direction is removed.
example.code:
"""Removes a link created by LinkElements with UnlinkElements.

Links the first wall to the second one first, so it needs at least two Walls. Only the link in the given direction is removed.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:2]
if len (walls) < 2:
    raise SystemExit ('Fewer than two walls in the project.')
link = {'fromElementId': walls[0]['elementId'], 'toElementId': walls[1]['elementId']}

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('LinkElements', {'links': [link]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UnlinkElements', {'links': [{'fromElementId': walls[0]['elementId'], 'toElementId': walls[1]['elementId']}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLinksOfElements', {'elements': walls[:1]})

zoneElementId.description: The identifier of a single Zone. Prefer the zones array: querying many Zones in one call is much faster than one call per Zone.

descriptorsOfElements.description: The descriptors of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

elements.description: A list of elements, or of element types to read the links of the element defaults of that type.

elementType.description: Read the links of the element defaults of this type instead of an element.

linkedPropertyObjectsOfElements.description: The property object links of each element or element default, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

A link that is not given stays unchanged. All changes are made in one undoable step.

elementsWithLinkedPropertyObjects.description: The property object links to set, each for an element or for the element defaults of an element type. A link that is not given stays unchanged.

linkByCriteria.description: Link the property objects matching their criteria to the element.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the property object to assign to the element individually, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 removes the individually assigned property object.

elementType.description: Set the links of the element defaults of this type instead of an element.

linkByCriteria.description: Link the property objects matching their criteria to the element defaults.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the property object to assign to the element defaults individually, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 removes the individually assigned property object.

commands.name: UpdateZones
commands.description: Updates Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements): the selected Zones, every Zone when nothing is selected, or the Zones given in zones. Archicad runs the update right after the command has returned, on the Zones selected at that moment, so the new geometry can only be read with a later command.

keepStampPosition.description: Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default is true.

undoTopTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default is false.

undoBottomTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The default is false.

zones.description: Optional list of the Zones to update, on any story. They are selected instead of the current selection and stay selected: Archicad updates the selected Zones right after the command has returned, not during it, and clears the selection when it is done. So do not change the selection until then, and read the new geometry with a later command. Every Zone is checked first; if one cannot be updated (not a Zone, listed twice, hidden or locked layer, not editable), nothing is selected or updated. An empty list updates nothing. Without the list the current selection is updated, or every Zone when nothing is selected.

example.description: Updates the first zone of the project (geometry, Zone Stamp and connected elements) with UpdateZones. Changes the zone, as Design > Update Zones does. Archicad updates it right after the command has returned and clears the selection.

Changes the zone, as Design > Update Zones does. Archicad updates it right after the command has returned and clears the selection.
"""

zones = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Zone'})['elements'][:1]
if not zones:
    raise SystemExit ('No zone in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UpdateZones', {
    'zones': zones,
    'keepStampPosition': True
}))

commands.name: GetCollisions
commands.description: Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements.

volumeTolerance.description: Intersection body volume greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

performSurfaceCheck.description: Enables surface collision check. If disabled the surfaceTolerance value will be ignored. By default it's false.

surfaceTolerance.description: Intersection body surface area greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

example.description: Finds the walls that collide with columns or beams with GetCollisions. Needs Walls and Columns or Beams.

commands.name: HighlightElements
commands.description: Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights. On Archicad 25 nonHighlightedColor is ignored.

highlightedColors.description: A list of colors to highlight elements.

items.description: Color of the highlighted element as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

wireframe3D.description: Optional parameter. Switch non highlighted elements in the 3D window to wireframe.

nonHighlightedColor.description: Optional parameter. Color of the non highlighted elements as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range. Ignored on Archicad 25.

example.description: Highlights the walls in red, with the other elements in transparent blue and wireframe in 3D, with HighlightElements. Needs at least one Wall. The highlight is removed after 5 seconds.
example.code:
"""Highlights the walls in red, with the other elements in transparent blue and wireframe in 3D, with HighlightElements.

Needs at least one Wall. The highlight is removed after 5 seconds.
"""
import time
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('HighlightElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'highlightedColors': [[255, 0, 0, 255] for wall in walls],
    'wireframe3D': True,
    'nonHighlightedColor': [0, 0, 255, 128]
}))
