# An empty elements array removes the highlight.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('HighlightElements', {'elements': [], 'highlightedColors': []}))

commands.name: MoveElements
commands.description: Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

elementsWithMoveVectors.description: The elements with move vector pairs.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be moved. By default it's false.

example.description: Moves a wall by 1 m along the X axis with MoveElements, then moves it back. Needs at least one editable Wall.

commands.name: AlignElements
commands.description: Aligns elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view to one edge of their plan bounding boxes (left, right, top or bottom) or to their middle (centerX, centerY), either of the whole set or of a reference element, by moving them in one undo step. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still aligned.

elements.description: The elements to align: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or Hotspot, in the current database.

alignTo.description: The edge of the plan bounding boxes to align: left (smallest X), right (largest X), bottom (smallest Y), top (largest Y), centerX (the middle in X, so the elements line up on one vertical line) or centerY (the middle in Y, on one horizontal line).

reference.description: Optional element to align to; it is not moved itself. Without it the elements are aligned to the outermost edge of the whole set (its leftmost left edge, its topmost top edge, ...), or for centerX and centerY to the middle of the bounding box of the whole set.

example.description: Aligns the left edges of three walls with AlignElements, prints their bounding boxes, then moves them back. Needs at least two editable Walls on the floor plan.

commands.name: DistributeElements
commands.description: Distributes 3 or more elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view evenly along X (horizontal) or Y (vertical), with equal distances between the middles of their plan bounding boxes (centers) or equal space between the boxes (gaps), by moving them in one undo step. The elements are taken in the order of their middles along the direction, and the two outermost stay where they are. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still distributed.

elements.description: At least 3 elements to distribute: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or Hotspot, in the current database. Their order does not matter: they are distributed in the order of the middles of their plan bounding boxes along the direction.

direction.description: horizontal distributes the elements along X, vertical along Y. They are not moved in the other direction.

mode.description: centers makes the distances between the middles of the plan bounding boxes equal, gaps makes the empty space between neighbouring bounding boxes equal (the gap is negative, so the boxes overlap, when the elements are wider together than the space between the two outermost elements).

example.description: Distributes up to five walls along X with equal gaps using DistributeElements, prints their new left edges, then moves them back. Needs at least three editable Walls on the floor plan.

commands.name: SplitElements
commands.description: Splits each given element along a line (the infinite line through its begin and end point, like Archicad's Split command). The original element keeps one part, copies of it (Drag a Copy, so they keep the layer, classifications, properties and every other setting) get the others; all are returned, the original first. Supports straight walls without doors, windows or openings, straight unslanted single segment beams without holes or openings, and lines (their arrows stay at the original ends), which are split in two, the original keeping the part from its begin point; and slabs, meshes without level lines or points, fills and single contour polylines, whose polygon (holes and arcs included) or points are cut along the line into one part per piece, the original keeping the largest piece (a polyline: the piece with its begin point). Slab edges keep their trim and side surface, the edges along the line are vertical; the corners a mesh gets on the line take their height from the edge they lie on. An element the line does not cross is reported as notCut, an unsupported one as an error naming its type. One undo step.

elements.description: The elements to split. Supported: straight walls (not polygonal, without doors, windows or openings), straight beams (not slanted or curved, one segment, without holes or openings), lines, slabs, meshes (without level lines or points), fills and polylines (one contour). Other types are reported with their type name.

line.description: The split line in project coordinates: the infinite line through begin and end, as the split line of Archicad's Split command.

results.description: One item per given element, in the same order.

elements.description: The parts, first the original element, then the new ones (copies of it). A wall, beam or line gives two parts: the original keeps the part from its begin point to the split line. A slab, mesh or fill gives one part per piece of its polygon on each side of the line (more than two when the line crosses a concave polygon more than twice); the original keeps the largest. A polyline is cut at every crossing; the original keeps the part with its begin point.

oneOf.description: The split line does not cross the element (or only touches one of its ends), so the element was left as it was.

example.description: Creates a 6 m wall and a 6 m x 5 m slab with a hole, splits both with SplitElements along the line x = 2, then deletes the parts. The wall gives two parts: the original wall (0 to 2 m) and a copy with the same settings (2 to 6 m). The slab gives two slabs with the same settings: the original keeps the larger piece (2 to 6 m, with the hole), the copy gets the rest.

commands.name: CopyElementsToDatabase
commands.description: Copies 2D elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, hotspots, texts, hatches, independent labels) from one database into another, e.g. from a worksheet into another worksheet, a detail or a layout, optionally moved by an offset. Returns the new elements in the order of the given ones.

elements.description: The 2D elements to copy: Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hotspot, Text, Hatch or Label (not associated with an element). Drawings are not copied yet: created from their own data they lose the link to their source view.

sourceDatabaseId.description: The database the elements are in. Default is the current database.

targetDatabaseId.description: The database to copy the elements into, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases).

offset.description: Optional vector the copies are moved by in the target database. Without it they keep the coordinates of the originals.

elements.description: The new element of each given element, in the same order, or the reason it was not copied.

example.description: Copies a polyline from the floor plan into a new worksheet, moved by 1 m, with CopyElementsToDatabase. Run it with the floor plan open. The polyline and the worksheet are created by the script and deleted at the end.

commands.name: ElevateElements
commands.description: Moves elements vertically by a given offset in meters, like Edit > Move > Elevate. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

elementsWithElevations.description: The elements with elevation offset pairs.

elevation.description: The vertical offset in meters to move the element by, like Edit > Move > Elevate. A positive value moves the element up, a negative value moves it down. The home story of the element does not change.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be elevated. By default it's false.

example.description: Moves a wall up by 1 m with ElevateElements, like Edit > Move > Elevate, then moves it back down. Needs at least one editable Wall.

commands.name: RotateElements
commands.description: Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

beginPoint.description: Starting point of the rotation arc.

endPoint.description: End point of the rotation arc.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a copy of the element is rotated. By default it's false.

example.description: Rotates a wall by 90 degrees around the project origin with RotateElements, then rotates it back. Needs at least one editable Wall. The angle is the one between origin-beginPoint and origin-endPoint.

commands.name: MirrorElements
commands.description: Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

example.description: Mirrors a wall across the Y axis with MirrorElements, then mirrors it back. Needs at least one editable Wall. With copy True the original would be kept and a mirrored copy created.

commands.name: CopyElements
commands.description: Copies elements by an offset, like dragging a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is moved by n times the offset, which makes a linear array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy (a part of a curtain wall, stair or railing, a locked element or one on a hidden or locked layer, ...) gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step.

elements.description: The elements to copy.

offset.description: The vector in meters the first copy is moved by from its element.

count.description: Optional number of copies of each element. Copy n is moved by n times the offset, so more than one makes a linear array. By default it's 1.

copies.description: One item for each given element, in the same order.

elements.description: The new elements made from this element, the first copy first. When the element is in a group and Suspend Groups is off, Archicad copies the whole group, and the copies of the other members are listed too.

error.description: Why the element, or some of its copies, could not be made. The copies made before the error are still listed in elements.

example.description: Makes a linear array of 5 copies of a wall, 2 m apart along the X axis, with CopyElements, then deletes the copies. Needs at least one editable Wall. Copy n is moved by n times the offset; the response lists the new elements of each given element in the order of the given ones.
example.code:
"""Makes a linear array of 5 copies of a wall, 2 m apart along the X axis, with CopyElements, then deletes the copies.

Needs at least one editable Wall. Copy n is moved by n times the offset; the response lists the
new elements of each given element in the order of the given ones.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CopyElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'offset': {'x': 2.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0},
    'count': 5
})

for copy in response['copies']:
    print ('Copies made:', len (copy['elements']), copy.get ('error', ''))

newElements = [element for copy in response['copies'] for element in copy['elements']]
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': newElements})

commands.name: RotateCopyElements
commands.description: Copies elements rotated around a center on the floor plan by an angle in radians, like rotating a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is rotated by n times the angle, which makes a circular array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step.

elements.description: The elements to copy.

center.description: The center of the rotation on the floor plan.

angle.description: The angle in radians the first copy is rotated by from its element, counterclockwise.

count.description: Optional number of copies of each element. Copy n is rotated by n times the angle, so more than one makes a circular array. By default it's 1.

copies.description: One item for each given element, in the same order.

elements.description: The new elements made from this element, the first copy first. When the element is in a group and Suspend Groups is off, Archicad copies the whole group, and the copies of the other members are listed too.

error.description: Why the element, or some of its copies, could not be made. The copies made before the error are still listed in elements.

example.description: Makes a circular array of 3 copies of a wall around the project origin, 90 degrees apart, with RotateCopyElements, then deletes the copies. Needs at least one editable Wall. The angle is in radians, counterclockwise; copy n is rotated by n times the angle.
example.code:
"""Makes a circular array of 3 copies of a wall around the project origin, 90 degrees apart, with RotateCopyElements, then deletes the copies.

Needs at least one editable Wall. The angle is in radians, counterclockwise; copy n is rotated by
n times the angle.
"""
import math
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RotateCopyElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'center': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'angle': math.pi / 2,
    'count': 3
})

for copy in response['copies']:
    print ('Copies made:', len (copy['elements']), copy.get ('error', ''))

newElements = [element for copy in response['copies'] for element in copy['elements']]
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': newElements})

commands.name: ScaleElements
commands.description: Scales elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view by a factor around a center point with Archicad's Resize edit, in one undo step. Resize scales X and Y by the same ratio, so factorY, if given, must equal factor. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch and Hotspot. An element of another type (library parts such as objects, lamps, doors and windows, stairs, railings, curtain walls, shells, morphs, texts, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still scaled.

elements.description: The elements to scale: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch or Hotspot, in the current database.

center.description: The fixed point of the scaling on the floor plan; every point of the elements moves away from it (factor > 1) or towards it (factor < 1).

factor.description: The scale factor, greater than 0: 2 doubles the distances from the center, 0.5 halves them.

factorY.description: Optional scale factor in Y. Archicad's Resize scales X and Y by one ratio, so it must be the same as factor (or left out); a different value is refused.

example.description: Scales a slab by 2 around the centre of its bounding box with ScaleElements, prints its bounding box before and after, then scales it back by 0.5. Needs at least one editable Slab. The bounding box after scaling should be twice as wide and deep, with the same centre.
example.code:
"""Scales a slab by 2 around the centre of its bounding box with ScaleElements, prints its bounding box before and after, then scales it back by 0.5.

Needs at least one editable Slab. The bounding box after scaling should be twice as wide and deep, with the same centre.
"""
import aclib

slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Slab', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not slabs:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable slab in the project.')

def GetBox ():
    return aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get2DBoundingBoxes', {'elements': slabs})['boundingBoxes2D'][0]['boundingBox2D']

box = GetBox ()
aclib.PrintJson (box)
center = {'x': (box['xMin'] + box['xMax']) / 2.0, 'y': (box['yMin'] + box['yMax']) / 2.0}

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ScaleElements', {'elements': slabs, 'center': center, 'factor': 2.0}))
aclib.PrintJson (GetBox ())

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ScaleElements', {'elements': slabs, 'center': center, 'factor': 0.5})

commands.name: DeleteElements
commands.description: Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before deleting gets wouldDelete, so a script can preview a deletion before making it.

elements.description: The elements to delete. The zones among them are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad.

executionResults.description: One result for each input element, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that passes every check made before deleting (it exists, its layer is not locked, it is editable) gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

example.description: Creates a wall and deletes it again with DeleteElements, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall and deletes it again with DeleteElements, first as a dry run that deletes nothing."""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls, 'dryRun': True}))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: DeleteSelectedElements
commands.description: Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true and lists the selected elements, with wouldDelete when there is at least one, or fails when one of them cannot be edited (Archicad then deletes none of them).

outputSchema.description: The result of the execution. A real run answers success, with error when it failed; a dry run also answers dryRun, and the elements it would delete.

wouldDelete.description: Only on a dry run that passed the checks: true when at least one element is selected.

elements.description: Only on a dry run: the selected elements (for a marquee, the ones it touches). A real run deletes them, together with the other members of their groups when Suspend Groups is off and the elements linked to them (labels, dimensions, ...).

example.description: Creates a wall, selects only it and deletes it with DeleteSelectedElements, the same as pressing the Delete key. The original selection is restored at the end. Run it with the floor plan open.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall, selects only it and deletes it with DeleteSelectedElements, the same as pressing the Delete key.

The original selection is restored at the end. Run it with the floor plan open.
"""
import aclib

originalSelection = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSelectedElements', {})['elements']
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeselectAll', {})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeSelectionOfElements', {'addElementsToSelection': walls})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteSelectedElements', {}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeSelectionOfElements', {'addElementsToSelection': originalSelection})

commands.name: LockElements
commands.description: Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

example.description: Locks a wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with LockElements, then unlocks it again. Needs at least one editable Wall.
example.code:
"""Locks a wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with LockElements, then unlocks it again.

Needs at least one editable Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')
wallId = walls[0]['elementId']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('LockElements', {'elements': walls}))
print ('Editable while locked: {}'.format (len (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FilterElements', {'elements': walls, 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements']) > 0))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UnlockElements', {'elements': walls})

commands.name: UnlockElements
commands.description: Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

example.description: Unlocks a locked wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with UnlockElements. Locks the first editable Wall first, so it is unchanged at the end.
example.code:
"""Unlocks a locked wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with UnlockElements.

Locks the first editable Wall first, so it is unchanged at the end.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')
wallId = walls[0]['elementId']

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('LockElements', {'elements': walls})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UnlockElements', {'elements': walls}))
print ('Editable after unlocking: {}'.format (len (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FilterElements', {'elements': walls, 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements']) > 0))

commands.name: RefreshElements
commands.description: Refreshes (rebuilds) the given elements, for example placed Objects, Windows and Doors that still show the old geometry after their library part's script or embedded file changed. Set force to true to run the parameter script of GDL-based elements too. The elements are looked up in the current database (floor plan, section or detail window). Returns an execution result for each input element. The refresh cannot be undone.

force.description: Forces the rebuild of GDL-based elements, which runs their parameter script. The default is false.

example.description: Rebuilds the placed objects, windows and doors of the current database with RefreshElements. force True also runs their parameter script. The refresh cannot be undone.

commands.name: GetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements.

example.description: Lists the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of a placed object with GetGDLParametersOfElements. Needs at least one Object.
example.code:
"""Lists the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of a placed object with GetGDLParametersOfElements.

Needs at least one Object.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

parameters = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetGDLParametersOfElements', {'elements': objects})['gdlParametersOfElements'][0]['parameters']
for parameter in parameters:
    print ('{} ({}): {}'.format (parameter['name'], parameter['type'], parameter['value']))

commands.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. On a Curtain Wall Frame, A, B, ac_frameWidth and ac_frameDepth mirror the frame's contour, which Archicad derives from the frame's settings, so they are rejected instead of reporting a change that does not take effect; a frame without a library part (an invisible Boundary frame, for example) has no GDL parameters. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution result naming it. With dryRun true no element is changed and no undo step is created: the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before changing it gets wouldChange, listing the parameters a real run would change (the given ones and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them) with their old and new values.

elementsWithGDLParameters.description: The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementsWithGDLParameters, in the order of the input. On a dry run the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, but the element is not changed. An element that passes every check made before changing it (the element and its parameters exist, every value is valid for its parameter, the element is editable) gets wouldChange: oldValue and newValue list the parameters a real run would change - the ones given and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them - before and after, each with name, index, type and value as GetGDLParametersOfElements gives them. Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

example.description: Widens a placed object by 0.1 m through its GDL parameter A with SetGDLParametersOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Object.

commands.name: GetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns.

markerParametersOfElements.description: The marker of each given element, in the order of the input, or an error for an element that is not a window or a door.

libPart.description: The library part of the marker. Absent when it could not be read.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the marker.

example.description: Reads the marker (the stamp next to the opening on the floor plan) library part and parameters of the first windows and doors with GetMarkerParametersOfElements. Needs at least one Window or Door.
example.code:
"""Reads the marker (the stamp next to the opening on the floor plan) library part and parameters of the first windows and doors with GetMarkerParametersOfElements.

Needs at least one Window or Door.
"""
import aclib

openings = []
for elementType in ['Window', 'Door']:
    openings += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': elementType})['elements']
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No window or door in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': openings[:3]}))

commands.name: SetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are.

elementsWithMarkerParameters.description: The elements with the marker parameters to change.

markerParameters.description: The marker parameters to change, each given by name or by index. The other marker parameters and the opening's own settings are left as they are.

name.description: The name of the marker parameter.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter: a number for the numeric types (Integer, Length, Angle, RealNumber, PenColor, LineType, Material, FillPattern, BuildingMaterial, Profile, RGBColor, Intensity), a string for String and Title, true/false for Boolean and 'On'/'Off' for LightSwitch. Array parameters are not supported.

index.description: The index of the marker parameter, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements reports it.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter, see the value given with a name.

example.description: Changes one marker parameter of a window or door with SetMarkerParametersOfElements, then restores it. Needs at least one Window or Door whose marker has a String parameter.
example.code:
"""Changes one marker parameter of a window or door with SetMarkerParametersOfElements, then restores it.

Needs at least one Window or Door whose marker has a String parameter.
"""
import aclib

openings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Window'})['elements']
openings += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Door'})['elements']
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No window or door in the project.')

opening = openings[0]
marker = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': [opening]})['markerParametersOfElements'][0]
stringParameters = [p for p in marker.get ('parameters', []) if p['type'] == 'String' and 'value' in p and 'dimension1' not in p]
if not stringParameters:
    raise SystemExit ('The marker of the first opening has no String parameter.')

parameter = stringParameters[0]
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elementsWithMarkerParameters': [{
    'elementId': opening['elementId'],
    'markerParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': 'Tapir'}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': [opening]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elementsWithMarkerParameters': [{
    'elementId': opening['elementId'],
    'markerParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': parameter['value']}]
}]}))

commands.name: GetURLReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA.

urlReferences.description: The web link of each given element, or an error. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA.

oneOf.title: URLReference
oneOf.description: The web link of an element.

url.description: The URL of the link, e.g. https://www.graphisoft.com.

description.description: The description of the link, e.g. GRAPHISOFT Home Page.

example.description: Prints the web link (URL and description) of every wall with GetURLReferencesOfElements. Walls without a link get an APIERR_NOUSERDATA error item.
example.code:
"""Prints the web link (URL and description) of every wall with GetURLReferencesOfElements.

Walls without a link get an APIERR_NOUSERDATA error item.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: SetURLReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. Fails with APIERR_MOREUSER for an element that already holds a link.

elementsWithURLReferences.description: The elements and the web link to set on each.

url.description: The URL of the link, e.g. https://www.graphisoft.com. At most 511 bytes in UTF-8.

description.description: The description of the link, e.g. GRAPHISOFT Home Page. At most 255 bytes in UTF-8. Empty when omitted.

example.description: Gives the first wall without a web link a link with SetURLReferencesOfElements and reads it back. Needs a Wall without a link. The link stays on the wall: this command cannot replace or remove an existing link.
example.code:
"""Gives the first wall without a web link a link with SetURLReferencesOfElements and reads it back.

Needs a Wall without a link. The link stays on the wall: this command cannot replace or remove an
existing link.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

links = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elements': walls})['urlReferences']
wallsWithoutLink = [wall for wall, link in zip (walls, links) if 'error' in link]
if not wallsWithoutLink:
    raise SystemExit ('Every wall has a link already.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elementsWithURLReferences': [{
    'elementId': wallsWithoutLink[0]['elementId'],
    'url': 'https://www.graphisoft.com',
    'description': 'GRAPHISOFT Home Page'
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elements': wallsWithoutLink[:1]})

commands.name: ChangeLibraryPartOfElements
commands.description: Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type, given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B).

elementsWithLibraryPart.description: The elements with the library part to change them to. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects.

libraryPart.description: The new library part, given by one of name, index or guid. It has to be a placeable library part of the element's type in the loaded libraries.

name.description: The name of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it in documentName.

index.description: The index of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it.

guid.description: The main guid of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it in guid.

keepParameters.description: Copies the values of the element's GDL parameters to the parameters of the new library part that have the same name, type and array dimensions; the other parameters get the new part's defaults. Default: true.

keepSize.description: Keeps the size (A and B) of the element; when false, the element gets the new part's default size. Default: true.

example.description: Sets the first object to the library part it already uses with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Giving the part it already has leaves the project unchanged; give the name of another library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it.
example.code:
"""Sets the first object to the library part it already uses with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.

Needs at least one Object. Giving the part it already has leaves the project unchanged; give the name
of another library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': objects})['detailsOfElements'][0]
libraryPartName = details['details']['libPart']['name']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeLibraryPartOfElements', {'elementsWithLibraryPart': [{
    'elementId': objects[0]['elementId'],
    'libraryPart': {'name': libraryPartName},
    'keepParameters': True,
    'keepSize': True
}]}))

commands.name: GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements
commands.description: Gets the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Curtain Wall Frame, Panel, Junction and Accessory elements as Archicad calculated them for their place in the curtain wall. GetGDLParametersOfElements returns the parameters the sub-element was set up with instead.

calculatedParametersOfElements.description: The calculated parameters of each given element, in the order of the input, or an error for an element that is not a curtain wall frame, panel, junction or accessory.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the sub-element as Archicad calculated them for its place in the curtain wall.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

displayName.description: The display name of the parameter.

index.description: The index of the parameter.

type.description: The type of the parameter.

dimension1.description: The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).

dimension2.description: The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).

value.description: The value of the parameter.

valueDescription.description: The value description for numeric parameter.

itemDescriptions.description: Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter, one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.

example.description: Prints the GDL parameters of the first curtain wall panel as Archicad calculated them, with GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements. Needs at least one Curtain Wall.
example.code:
"""Prints the GDL parameters of the first curtain wall panel as Archicad calculated them, with GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements.

Needs at least one Curtain Wall.
"""
import aclib

panels = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'CurtainWallPanel'})['elements'][:1]
if not panels:
    raise SystemExit ('No curtain wall panel in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements', {'elements': panels}))

commands.name: GetHotspotsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the 2D hotspots of the given library part instances (Objects, Lamps, Windows, Doors, Skylights, Zones, Curtain Wall parts, etc.), e.g. to dimension to them.

hotspotsOfElements.description: The hotspots of the given library part instances, in the order of the input.

hotspots.description: The 2D hotspots of the placed library part instance, as Archicad returns them.

example.description: Prints the 2D hotspots of the first object with GetHotspotsOfElements. Needs at least one Object.
example.code:
"""Prints the 2D hotspots of the first object with GetHotspotsOfElements.

Needs at least one Object.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotspotsOfElements', {'elements': objects}))

commands.name: SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements
commands.description: Changes which library part the marker of the given Window and Door elements uses, given by its name (find the available ones with GetAvailableLibraryParts); only a marker library part for the opening's type is accepted. The marker gets the new library part's default parameters, which SetMarkerParametersOfElements can change afterwards; the opening's own settings are left as they are.

elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart.description: The elements with the library part their marker should use.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the library part the marker should use, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements and GetAvailableLibraryParts report it. It has to be a marker library part: Archicad's marker parent for windows or doors, or a library part derived from it. Any other library part is refused.

example.description: Sets the marker of the first window or door to the library part it already uses with SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements. Needs at least one Window or Door. Give the name of another marker library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it. The marker gets the library part's default parameters.
example.code:
"""Sets the marker of the first window or door to the library part it already uses with SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements.

Needs at least one Window or Door. Give the name of another marker library part (see
GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it. The marker gets the library part's default parameters.
"""
import aclib

openings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Window'})['elements']
openings += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Door'})['elements']
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No window or door in the project.')

marker = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': openings[:1]})['markerParametersOfElements'][0]
if 'libPart' not in marker:
    raise SystemExit ('The first opening has no marker.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements', {'elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'libraryPartName': marker['libPart']['name']
}]}))

commands.name: RunParameterScriptOfElements
commands.description: Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements.

example.description: Runs the parameter script of every object with RunParameterScriptOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Parameters that depend on other parameters are recalculated.
example.code:
"""Runs the parameter script of every object with RunParameterScriptOfElements.

Needs at least one Object. Parameters that depend on other parameters are recalculated.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements']
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RunParameterScriptOfElements', {'elements': objects}))

commands.name: CreateColumns
commands.description: Creates Column elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyColumns, besides the position, size, slant, cross section and veneer; settings not given come from the Column tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the column segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.

columnsData.description: Array of data to create Columns.

items.description: The parameters of the new Column.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

height.description: Optional column height.

axisRotationAngle.description: Optional column rotation angle in radians.

slantAngle.description: Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

slantDirectionAngle.description: Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

veneer.description: Veneer of the column (type, thickness, building material); the fields not given come from the tool defaults or favoriteName, thickness 0 creates the column without veneer. Applied to all segments.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the column in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

example.description: Creates two columns with CreateColumns: one with the Column tool defaults and one round, 3 m high column with its own cut fill pens. Coordinates are in meters; z is the elevation of the column base. CreateColumns takes the same cut fill pens (written from Archicad 27) and cover fill as ModifyColumns.

commands.name: CreateWalls
commands.description: Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls, applied by the same code, except geometryType and profileType, which the new wall takes from the favorite or the Wall tool defaults (its plan outline is always Straight), and bottomOffset, which comes from zCoordinate. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

floorIndex.description: Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.

height.description: Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.

thickness.description: Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

offset.description: Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

referenceLineLocation.description: Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.

flipped.description: Optional. True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped). When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's side is kept, which for a Profile wall mirrors its whole cross section.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' for the same wall: whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

visibility.description: Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.

cutFillPen.description: Pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Background pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

structureType.description: Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

linkToSettings.description: When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

example.description: Creates a straight and a curved wall with CreateWalls. Fields not given (structure, top link, ...) come from the Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName. CreateWalls takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls: the second wall also sets how it relates to zones and overrides the surface of its reference side.
example.code:
"""Creates a straight and a curved wall with CreateWalls.

Fields not given (structure, top link, ...) come from the Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
CreateWalls takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls: the second wall also sets how it relates
to zones and overrides the surface of its reference side.
"""
import aclib
import math

surfaces = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Surface'})['attributes']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {
        'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'height': 3.0,
        'thickness': 0.3
    },
    {
        'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 8.0, 'y': 4.0},
        'arcAngle': math.pi / 4,
        'height': 3.0,
        'zoneRel': 'ReduceArea',
        'referenceMaterial': {'overridden': True, 'attributeId': surfaces[0]['attributeId']}
    }
]}))

commands.name: CreateBeams
commands.description: Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyBeams, besides the position, shape, slant and cross section; settings not given come from the Beam tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the beam's reference line. Which point of the cross section lies on the reference line is set by anchorPoint: with a Top anchor the beam hangs below zCoordinate, so zCoordinate 10 and height 0.1 span 9.9 to 10; MiddleLeft, Center and MiddleRight center it on zCoordinate; Bottom anchors stand it on top. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given.

offset.description: Horizontal distance of the beam from its reference line, in meters; positive moves the beam to the left of the line, looking from begCoordinate to endCoordinate.

slantAngle.description: Slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also switches the beam to slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

profileAngle.description: Rotation angle of the profile around the beam's center line, in radians.

arcAngle.description: Optional arc angle in radians. A non-zero value makes a horizontally curved beam.

verticalCurveHeight.description: Optional rise of a vertically curved beam. A non-zero value makes a vertically curved beam; it wins over arcAngle.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

anchorPoint.description: The point of the cross section that lies on the reference line (begCoordinate to endCoordinate at zCoordinate). Top anchors hang the beam below zCoordinate, Bottom anchors stand it on top, MiddleLeft, Center and MiddleRight center it. Left and Right anchors put the line on the beam's left or right edge, looking from begCoordinate to endCoordinate; TopCenter, Center and BottomCenter keep it on the beam's axis.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the beam in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

example.description: Creates a 6 m long beam at 3 m height with its own cut fill pen with CreateBeams. With the TopCenter anchor the beam hangs below its reference line at zCoordinate. CreateBeams takes the same cut fill pens (written from Archicad 27) and cover fill as ModifyBeams.
example.code:
"""Creates a 6 m long beam at 3 m height with its own cut fill pen with CreateBeams.

With the TopCenter anchor the beam hangs below its reference line at zCoordinate. CreateBeams takes the same
cut fill pens (written from Archicad 27) and cover fill as ModifyBeams.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateBeams', {'beamsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'zCoordinate': 3.0,
    'width': 0.3,
    'height': 0.5,
    'isWidthAndHeightLinked': False,
    'anchorPoint': 'TopCenter',
    'cutFillPen': {'overridden': True, 'penIndex': 5}
}]}))

commands.name: CreateStairs
commands.description: Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters, optionally with the segment type of each baseline edge and the turn at each baseline point (landings and winders). Accepts the same settings as ModifyStairs: the step values with their locks, the finish and structure visibility, the extra treads, the walking line, the numbering, the walking direction, and the tread, riser and structure settings of the flights and the landings; settings not given come from the Stair tool defaults or the favorite.

stairsData.description: Array of data to create Stair elements.

items.description: The parameters of the new Stair.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates of the stair baseline polyline. Whether the baseline runs along the left edge, the right edge or the center of the flight is the Stair tool's baseline position, taken from baselinePosition, or else from the tool defaults or favoriteName: with the baseline on the left edge, the flight lies to the right of it, looking from the first point to the last. The first point is kept; the length of the flight comes from the riser count and going, so the flight does not necessarily end at the last point given. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

baselinePosition.description: Optional. Where the baseline runs on the flight, looking from the first point to the last. Left: along the left edge, the flight lies to the right of the baseline. Right: along the right edge, the flight lies to the left of it. Center: along the middle of the flight. Without it the baseline position of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is used.

baselineOffset.description: Optional. The offset of the baseline from the flight edge that baselinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center. Without it the offset of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is kept.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

stepNum.description: Number of risers (steps). Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not have this many risers.

riserHeight.description: Height of each riser. Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not use this riser height.

treadDepth.description: Depth (going) of each tread. Pinned as a fixed going in the stair rules, so the run length follows from the number of treads; the standard's combined riser/going rules (2R+G, R+G, R/G) are not applied to this stair.

baseLineEdges.description: Optional. The segment type of each baseline edge, one item per edge (baseLinePoints.length - 1 items; edge i runs from point i to point i + 1). A U-shaped stair with a half landing is Flight, Landing, Flight with landing turns at both inner points. When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineVertices is given, every edge is a flight. Combinations Archicad cannot build fail like any other invalid stair.

segmentType.description: Flight: steps. Landing: a landing segment, the edge between two landing turns of a U-shaped stair. DividedLanding: a divided landing segment.

baseLineVertices.description: Optional. The turn at each baseline point, one item per point (baseLinePoints.length items). When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineEdges is given, the first and last points get no turn and every other point a landing turn. Winders use Archicad's default winder settings.

turnType.description: The turn at this point. The first and last points take None.

minLandingStartEdgeOffset.description: Optional, 0 by default. The minimal lead edge offset of a landing turn: makes the landing longer before the turn. Archicad calculates the actual offset, at least this much, to fit the steps (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as landingStartEdgeOffset).

minLandingEndEdgeOffset.description: Optional, 0 by default. The minimal trail edge offset of a landing turn: makes the landing longer after the turn. Archicad calculates the actual offset, at least this much (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as landingEndEdgeOffset).

treadDepthLocked.description: Whether the going lengths are locked.

totalHeightLocked.description: Whether the total height is locked.

finishVisible.description: Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.

extraTopTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.

extraBottomTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.

walkingLinePosition.description: Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).

walkingLineOffset.description: The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.

numberingType.description: Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.

inputDirection.description: The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).

uniformFinish.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.

uniformMonolithAttributes.description: Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.

uniformDrainings.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.

structureVisibility.description: Whether the structure of the stair is shown.

treads.description: The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the treads.

nosingType.description: Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).

nosingSlant.description: The slant of the nosing in radians.

risers.description: The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the risers.

crossSection.description: The cross section of the risers.

angle.description: The angle of a slanted riser in radians.

position.description: Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

structures.description: The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

structureType.description: The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.

bottomType.description: The shape of the underside of the structure.

horizontalThickness.description: The horizontal thickness of the structure.

example.description: Creates a straight stair and a U-shaped stair with a half landing with CreateStairs. Two baseline points make a straight stair; more points make an L- or U-shaped one. The straight stair's baseline runs along the middle of its flight (baselinePosition), and its treads and structure are set with the same tread, riser and structure settings ModifyStairs accepts. Fields not given come from the Stair tool defaults.
example.code:
"""Creates a straight stair and a U-shaped stair with a half landing with CreateStairs.

Two baseline points make a straight stair; more points make an L- or U-shaped one. The straight
stair's baseline runs along the middle of its flight (baselinePosition), and its treads and structure
are set with the same tread, riser and structure settings ModifyStairs accepts. Fields not given come
from the Stair tool defaults.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateStairs', {'stairsData': [
    {
        'baseLinePoints': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}],
        'baselinePosition': 'Center',
        'zCoordinate': 0.0,
        'totalHeight': 3.0,
        'flightWidth': 1.2,
        'treadDepth': 0.28,
        'extraTopTread': False,
        'numberingType': 'Treads',
        'treads': [{'role': 'Run', 'thickness': 0.04, 'nosingType': 'ByValue', 'nosingValue': 0.02}],
        'structures': [{'role': 'Run', 'side': 'UnderSide', 'visible': True, 'structureType': 'Monolith', 'bottomType': 'Smooth', 'thickness': 0.18}]
    },
    {
        'baseLinePoints': [{'x': 10.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 13.455, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 13.455, 'y': 1.39}, {'x': 10.0, 'y': 1.39}],
        'zCoordinate': 0.0,
        'totalHeight': 2.7684,
        'riserHeight': 0.1538,
        'treadDepth': 0.24,
        'flightWidth': 1.15,
        'baseLineEdges': [{'segmentType': 'Flight'}, {'segmentType': 'Landing'}, {'segmentType': 'Flight'}],
        'baseLineVertices': [{'turnType': 'None'}, {'turnType': 'Landing'}, {'turnType': 'Landing'}, {'turnType': 'None'}]
    }
]}))

commands.name: SolveStairBaseline
commands.description: Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27.

stairsData.description: Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.

solutions.description: The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

example.description: Checks an L-shaped stair baseline with SolveStairBaseline, without creating a stair. Prints whether the baseline is Correct, Solved (with the solved baseline) or NotSolved. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Checks an L-shaped stair baseline with SolveStairBaseline, without creating a stair.

Prints whether the baseline is Correct, Solved (with the solved baseline) or NotSolved.
Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SolveStairBaseline', {'stairsData': [{
    'baseLinePoints': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 3.0}, {'x': 3.0, 'y': 3.0}],
    'zCoordinate': 0.0,
    'totalHeight': 3.0,
    'flightWidth': 1.2
}]}))

commands.name: CreateSlabs
commands.description: Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same surfaces (top, side, bottom), cut fill pens and floor fill as ModifySlabs, besides the outline, holes, level and structure; settings not given come from the Slab tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surface of a single edge, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27; of the floor fill orientation Archicad applies only the type through the API.

slabsData.description: Array of data to create Slabs.

items.description: The parameters of the new Slab.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

level.description: The Z coordinate value of the reference line of the slab.

thickness.description: Optional slab thickness. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType, buildingMaterialId or compositeId the new slab keeps the structure of the slab tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

structureType.description: Optional structure of the slab. If omitted, derived from buildingMaterialId or compositeId when one is given, otherwise the slab tool default (or the favorite) is kept.

example.description: Flips a Boolean parameter of the cut symbol of the first opening with SetOpeningSymbolParameters, then restores it. Needs an Opening (made with the Opening tool) with a cut symbol that has a Boolean parameter. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Flips a Boolean parameter of the cut symbol of the first opening with SetOpeningSymbolParameters, then restores it.

Needs an Opening (made with the Opening tool) with a cut symbol that has a Boolean parameter.
Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

openings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Opening'})['elements'][:1]
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No opening in the project.')

symbol = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': openings})['openings'][0]
booleans = [p for p in symbol.get ('cutSymbolParameters', []) if p['type'] == 'Boolean' and 'dimension1' not in p]
if not booleans:
    raise SystemExit ('The first opening has no cut symbol with a Boolean parameter.')

parameter = booleans[0]
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'cutSymbolParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': not parameter['value']}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': openings})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'cutSymbolParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': parameter['value']}]
}]}))
