height.description: The opening's height. See linkedStatus.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

example.description: Moves the first opening 0.5 m along X with SetOpeningDetails, reads it back, then moves it back. Needs at least one Opening (made with the Opening tool). The transformation is a 3x4 matrix, row by row, with the translation in the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Moves the first opening 0.5 m along X with SetOpeningDetails, reads it back, then moves it back.

Needs at least one Opening (made with the Opening tool). The transformation is a 3x4 matrix, row by
row, with the translation in the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

openings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Opening'})['elements'][:1]
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No opening in the project.')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningDetails', {'elements': openings})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetOpeningDetails', {'openingsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'transformation': [1, 0, 0, 0.5,
                       0, 1, 0, 0,
                       0, 0, 1, 0]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningDetails', {'elements': openings})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetOpeningDetails', {'openingsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'transformation': [1, 0, 0, -0.5,
                       0, 1, 0, 0,
                       0, 0, 1, 0]
}]}))

commands.name: CreateMorphs
commands.description: Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions or arbitrary bodies. Each item may name a favorite (favoriteName) to start from, a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id); the given geometry and floor are kept.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Morph favorite to base the new morph on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. The geometry (basePoint, size or body, axes) and the floor always come from this item, not from the favorite.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

size.description: Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.

body.description: Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.

topExpansion.description: Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

example.description: Creates a 2 m box morph and a tetrahedron morph from vertices and faces with CreateMorphs. A body's vertices are local to the morph's basePoint; each face lists vertex indices counterclockwise as seen from outside. An item may also name a Morph favorite to start from (favoriteName), a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id), as the box does with its id.

commands.name: CreateRoofs
commands.description: Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

pivotLine.description: If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.

angle.description: Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.

example.description: Creates a multi-plane roof and a single-plane roof with CreateRoofs. A pivotLine makes a single-plane roof that rises on the left of the line; angles are in radians.

commands.name: CreateShells
commands.description: Creates extruded, revolved and ruled Shell elements from profile polylines, with thickness, structure, an optional clipping contour and holes.

shellsData.description: Array of data to create Shells.

items.description: The parameters of the new Shell.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Shell favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

shellClass.description: Extruded: 'profile' swept along 'extrusionVector'. Revolved: 'profile' turned around 'axis'. Ruled: a surface ruled between 'profile' and 'secondProfile'.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the shell. Without it the shell is placed on the story of the Shell tool defaults.

basePlane.description: Base plane of the shell, in project coordinates; the profiles, the extrusion, the axis and the contour and hole polygons are given in it. The project axes by default, except for a Revolved shell, whose default base plane stands upright (its Y axis is the project Z axis), so the profile's x is the radius and its y the height.

profile.description: The profile polyline. Extruded: in the plane across the extrusion, x horizontal and y up. Revolved: in the base plane's XY plane. Ruled: in the XY plane of 'profilePlane'.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic shell; a Composite shell takes its thickness from the composite.

isFlipped.description: Applies the thickness to the other side of the reference surface.

extrusionVector.description: Extruded only, required: the direction and length of the extrusion, in base plane coordinates.

extrusionStart.description: Extruded only: the point the extrusion starts from, in base plane coordinates.

shapePlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the profile's plane, in radians.

begPlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the start plane of the extrusion, in radians.

endPlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the end plane of the extrusion, in radians.

slantAngle.description: Extruded and Revolved: slant of the extrusion vector or of the profile, in radians.

axis.description: Revolved only: the coordinate system whose Z axis the profile is turned around, in base plane coordinates. By default the base plane's Y axis.

revolutionAngle.description: Revolved only: the angle the profile is turned through, in radians. 2*pi (a full turn) by default.

beginAngle.description: Revolved only: the angle the revolution starts at, in radians.

distortionAngle.description: Revolved only: shear of the revolution, in radians. pi/2 (no shear) by default.

segmentsByCircle.description: Revolved only: the number of segments a full circle is resolved into.

secondProfile.description: Ruled only, required: the second profile polyline, in the XY plane of 'secondProfilePlane'.

profilePlane.description: Ruled only, required: the plane of 'profile', in base plane coordinates.

secondProfilePlane.description: Ruled only, required: the plane of 'secondProfile', in base plane coordinates.

morphingRule.description: Ruled only: how the two profiles are joined, segment by segment (Paired) or smoothly.

contour.description: Optional clipping contour: only the part of the shell inside this polygon, seen along the Z axis of its plane, is kept. Its 'depth' is ignored.

holes.description: Optional holes, each requiring 'depth' to extrude its cutting polygon along the Z axis of its plane.

begShapeEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the profile's edges at the start of the shell (the start plane of an extrusion, the begin angle of a revolution, the first profile of a ruled shell). Perpendicular at pi/2 by default, as the Shell tool draws it, also when favoriteName is given.

endShapeEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the profile's edges at the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

begSideEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the edge that the profile's first point sweeps from the start to the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

endSideEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the edge that the profile's last point sweeps. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

example.description: Creates an extruded barrel vault, a revolved dome and a ruled shell with CreateShells. The vault has a square opening, and the dome has a circular oculus. Profiles, placement planes and cutting polygons define the three shells.

commands.name: CreateSkylights
commands.description: Creates Skylight elements with a roof or shell owner and a floor plan anchor position. It takes the same settings as ModifySkylights (anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display, pens, line types, section fill, surface and the library part flags) and optionally a library part; the settings not given come from the Skylight tool defaults or a favorite. Surface placement is handled by Archicad and has not yet been verified for this command.

skylightsData.description: Array of data to create Skylights.

items.description: The parameters of the new Skylight. The settings not given are the Skylight tool defaults' or the favorite's.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Skylight favorite to base the new element on.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

ownerId.description: The roof (single- or multi-plane) or shell the skylight is placed in.

libraryPartName.description: Optional localized name of a skylight library part to place instead of the tool default's.

anchorPosition.description: Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point (API_SkylightType::anchorPosition). Archicad places the skylight on its owner roof or shell at this point; moving it onto another plane of a multi-plane roof has not been verified.

anchorPoint.description: Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places (API_SkylightType::anchorPoint).

fixMode.description: What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes (API_SkylightType::fixMode).

azimuthAngle.description: Rotation angle of the skylight in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians (API_SkylightType::azimuthAngle).

elevationAngle.description: Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.

pen.description: Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines.

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the skylight.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines.

surfaceId.description: Surface of the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectMaterials.description: Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

example.description: Requests three skylights in single-plane and multi-plane roof owners. Creates the roofs first, then uses their IDs and global XY anchor positions. Automatic surface placement still needs verification in a running Archicad.

commands.name: ModifySkylights
commands.description: Modifies Skylight elements: anchor position and anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display option, pens, line types, section fill and pens, surface and the use-the-library-part's-settings flags - the same settings CreateSkylights takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given settings change. Not written by this command: the owner roof or shell, the anchor level and the vertical link (Archicad places the skylight on its owner), the plane of a multi-plane roof it sits on, the dimension marker (a separate element) and the library part's own parameters (use SetGDLParametersOfElements). Archicad may set the elevation angle again from the owner.

skylightsWithDetails.description: The skylights to modify, each with the settings to change. The settings not given stay as they are.

anchorPosition.description: Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point (API_SkylightType::anchorPosition). Archicad places the skylight on its owner roof or shell at this point; moving it onto another plane of a multi-plane roof has not been verified.

anchorPoint.description: Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places (API_SkylightType::anchorPoint).

fixMode.description: What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes (API_SkylightType::fixMode).

azimuthAngle.description: Rotation angle of the skylight in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians (API_SkylightType::azimuthAngle).

elevationAngle.description: Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.

pen.description: Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines.

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the skylight.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines.

surfaceId.description: Surface of the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectMaterials.description: Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

example.description: Changes the size, rotation and floor plan display of the skylights with ModifySkylights. Needs at least one Skylight. Only the settings given change; CreateSkylights takes the same keys, and GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.
example.code:
"""Changes the size, rotation and floor plan display of the skylights with ModifySkylights.

Needs at least one Skylight. Only the settings given change; CreateSkylights takes the same keys,
and GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.
"""
import aclib

skylights = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Skylight'})['elements']
if not skylights:
    raise SystemExit ('Place a Skylight first.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand (
    'ModifySkylights', {
        'skylightsWithDetails': [
            {
                'elementId': skylight['elementId'],
                'width': 1.0,
                'height': 1.2,
                'azimuthAngle': 0.0,
                'displayOption': 'OutLinesOnly',
                'pen': 7
            } for skylight in skylights
        ]
    }))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': skylights}))

commands.name: CreateRailings
commands.description: Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite, from an existing railing (templateElementId) or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices.

railingsData.description: Array of data to create Railings.

items.description: The parameters of the new Railing. Everything not given here - the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters - comes from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults of the open project. Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices from them.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

templateElementId.description: Optional existing Railing whose settings the new railing takes instead of the tool defaults (or the favorite): its node and segment settings, from which the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters are generated, its story visibility, pens, bottom offset, layer and home story. floorIndex, bottomOffset and height given here override them. The reference line of a railing cannot be changed through the Archicad API, so a railing is given a new reference line by creating it again with itself as templateElementId and deleting the old one.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the railing on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.

bottomOffset.description: Optional base height of the railing relative to the floor level. When omitted, the value of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

height.description: Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

example.description: Creates a 1.1 m high railing along three edges of a balcony with CreateRailings, then a second one with its settings. The posts, rails, handrails and infill come from the Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName. The second railing takes every setting of the first through templateElementId; the reference line of a railing cannot be changed, so this is also how a railing gets a new one (create it again with itself as the template, then delete the old one).

commands.name: CreateRailingsFromPolyline
commands.description: Creates Railing elements along a 3D reference polyline: each node has its own elevation and segments can be arcs. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults.

railingsData.description: Array of data to create Railings.

items.description: The parameters of the new Railing. Everything not given here - the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters - comes from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults of the open project. Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices from them.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.

polylineCoordinates.description: The nodes of the reference line of the railing. z is the elevation of the node relative to the floor level of the home story, so the railing can climb or descend along its segments.

polylineArcs.description: Optional arc segments of the reference line. begIndex and endIndex are indices into polylineCoordinates and must be consecutive (endIndex = begIndex + 1).

height.description: Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

example.description: Creates a railing that climbs 1 m along its second segment and ends in a quarter arc with CreateRailingsFromPolyline. z of each node is its elevation above the home story. The posts, rails and infill come from the Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
example.code:
"""Creates a railing that climbs 1 m along its second segment and ends in a quarter arc with CreateRailingsFromPolyline.

z of each node is its elevation above the home story. The posts, rails and infill come from the
Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
"""
import aclib
import math

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRailingsFromPolyline', {'railingsData': [{
    'polylineCoordinates': [
        {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0},
        {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0},
        {'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 1.0},
        {'x': 10.0, 'y': 2.0, 'z': 1.0}
    ],
    'polylineArcs': [{'begIndex': 2, 'endIndex': 3, 'arcAngle': math.pi / 2}],
    'floorIndex': 0,
    'height': 1.1
}]}))

commands.name: CreateCurtainWalls
commands.description: Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

curtainWallsData.description: Array of data to create Curtain Walls.

items.description: The parameters of the new Curtain Wall. Everything not given here - the frame and panel classes, the surfaces, the boundary and corner frames, the pattern - comes from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults of the open project.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.

zCoordinate.description: Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. When omitted, derived from zCoordinate if that is given, otherwise the current story.

height.description: Optional height of the curtain wall. When omitted, the height of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) is kept.

primaryPattern.description: Optional column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segment (the primary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

secondaryPattern.description: Optional row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

cells.description: Optional assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. A cell not listed here keeps the assignment of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) when the pattern is unchanged, otherwise the assignment of the first default cell.

example.description: Creates a 6 m long, 3 m high curtain wall with 1.5 m wide columns and two rows with CreateCurtainWalls. The frame and panel classes come from the Curtain Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
example.code:
"""Creates a 6 m long, 3 m high curtain wall with 1.5 m wide columns and two rows with CreateCurtainWalls.

The frame and panel classes come from the Curtain Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateCurtainWalls', {'curtainWallsData': [{
    'coordinates': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0}],
    'zCoordinate': 0.0,
    'height': 3.0,
    'primaryPattern': {'sizes': [1.5], 'logic': 'FixedSizes'},
    'secondaryPattern': {'sizes': [1.0, 2.0], 'logic': 'FixedSizes'}
}]}))

commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensions
commands.description: Creates associative dimensions from explicit witness point references: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance). A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textFrame.description: Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.

appearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.

elevationOrigin.description: Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.

linePen.description: Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.

marker.description: Optional marker at the witness points; give the type, the pen or both. Its size is not written: the size the API reports did not match the marker size of the Dimension Settings for linear dimensions.

type.description: The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.

pen.description: The pen of the marker.

defaultWitnessForm.description: Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.

defaultWitnessVal.description: Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.

example.description: Creates a wall and dimensions its length with CreateAssociativeDimensions. The dimension follows the wall: inIndex 1 and 2 are the end points of the wall's reference line. A witness point given only by a coordinate is static. direction is the direction of the dimension line.

commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection
commands.description: Creates associative dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column, door and window presets: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance), e.g. level marks. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds. For Opening tool elements, which Archicad does not associate with dimensions, the OpeningEdges preset places fixed points at their edges instead.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).

textFrame.description: Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.

appearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.

elevationOrigin.description: Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.

linePen.description: Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.

marker.description: Optional marker at the witness points; give the type, the pen or both. Its size is not written: the size the API reports did not match the marker size of the Dimension Settings for linear dimensions.

type.description: The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.

pen.description: The pen of the marker.

defaultWitnessForm.description: Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.

defaultWitnessVal.description: Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of a single section element. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

sectionElementIds.description: A list of section elements whose preset points are merged into one continuous dimension chain. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

preset.description: OpeningEdges puts fixed points, not associated ones, at the edges of an Opening tool element as the section draws it: left and right for a horizontal direction, bottom and top for a vertical one. Archicad does not associate dimensions with openings in sections.

example.description: Dimensions the composite faces of the first wall in the current section with CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection. Run it with a section window as the current window that shows at least one Wall. The dimension is placed in that section.
example.code:
"""Dimensions the composite faces of the first wall in the current section with CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection.

Run it with a section window as the current window that shows at least one Wall. The dimension is
placed in that section.
"""
import aclib

sectionElements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSectionElements', {})['sectionElements']
walls = [s for s in sectionElements if s.get ('ownerElementType') == 'Wall']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the current section window.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'sectionElementId': walls[0]['sectionElementId'],
    'referencePoint': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'preset': 'WallCompositeFaces'
}]}))

commands.name: CreateWallThicknessDimensions
commands.description: Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. example.description: Creates a linear dimension, then changes its pens, marker, texts and witness lines with ModifyAssociativeDimensions. The keys are the ones the dimension creation commands take, and GetDetailsOfElements returns them, so the settings read from one dimension can be written to others. The text and witness line settings are applied to every witness point. Run it with a floor plan window active.
example.code:
"""Creates a linear dimension, then changes its pens, marker, texts and witness lines with ModifyAssociativeDimensions.

The keys are the ones the dimension creation commands take, and GetDetailsOfElements returns them,
so the settings read from one dimension can be written to others. The text and witness line
settings are applied to every witness point. Run it with a floor plan window active.
"""
import aclib

dimension = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateAssociativeDimensions', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'referencePoint': {'x': 0.0, 'y': -1.0},
    'direction': {'x': 1.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'witnessPoints': [{'coordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}}, {'coordinate': {'x': 3.0, 'y': 0.0}}]
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyAssociativeDimensions', {'dimensionsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': dimension['elementId'],
    'linePen': 3,
    'marker': {'type': 'FullArrow30', 'pen': 3},
    'textHeight': 3.5,
    'textPen': 5,
    'textFrame': True,
    'defaultWitnessForm': 'Fix',
    'defaultWitnessVal': 0.5
}]}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [dimension]}))

commands.name: GetOpeningTransformations
commands.description: Gets the placement of Opening elements, Windows, Doors and Skylights without changing them: a global-to-local transformation matrix, its inverse, and the origin and axes in world coordinates derived from the inverse. For Windows, Doors and Skylights the local-to-global matrix is the one Archicad returns, and mirrored ones give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). For Opening elements it is built from the opening geometry (Archicad 29 and later): origin at the anchor point, the X and Y axes of the opening and Z = X × Y, which points against the extrusion direction. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

openingTransformations.description: The transformation of each given Opening, or an error, in the order of the input elements.

globalToLocal.description: The global-to-local matrix (API_Tranmat), the inverse of localToGlobal: the 12 values of a 3x4 matrix, row by row, so x' = m[0]*x + m[1]*y + m[2]*z + m[3], y' = m[4]*x + ... + m[7], z' = m[8]*x + ... + m[11].

localToGlobal.description: The local-to-global matrix, in the same layout: the matrix ACAPI_Element_GetOpeningTransformation returns for a Window, Door or Skylight, or the one built from the geometry of an Opening element.

origin.description: The origin of the opening's local coordinate system in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. For an Opening element this is its anchor point.

xAxis.description: The local X axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal.

yAxis.description: The local Y axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal.

zAxis.description: The local Z axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. For an Opening element it is X × Y, which points against its extrusion direction.

determinant.description: The determinant of the 3x3 part of localToGlobal: 1, or -1 for a mirrored Window, Door or Skylight.

isMirrored.description: True when the matrix is left-handed (negative determinant), which Archicad returns for a mirrored opening.

example.description: Prints the placement (transformation matrices, origin and axes) of every window with GetOpeningTransformations. Needs at least one Window; Doors, Skylights and Openings work the same way (Openings from Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the placement (transformation matrices, origin and axes) of every window with GetOpeningTransformations.

Needs at least one Window; Doors, Skylights and Openings work the same way (Openings from Archicad 29).
Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

windows = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Window'})['elements']
if not windows:
    raise SystemExit ('No window in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningTransformations', {'elements': windows}))

commands.name: CreateZones
commands.description: Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same zone settings as ModifyZones (name, number, category, zone stamp, levels, contour line and cover fill), applied by the same helpers; the polygon or reference point is only set here. An item whose area would overlap an existing Zone on the same story fails with an error naming that Zone instead of opening Archicad's modal overlap warning, unless its allowOverlap is true.

zonesData.description: Array of data to create Zones.

items.description: The parameters of the new Zone.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the new zone. An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) is found around its reference point on this story, which is made active in the floor plan while the zone is created; the previously active story is restored afterwards.

name.description: Name of the zone.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

stampAngle.description: Optional zone stamp rotation angle in radians.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

contourLine.description: Optional contour line of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.

coverFill.description: Optional cover fill of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.

allowOverlap.description: Optional, defaults to false. Archicad answers a new zone whose area overlaps an existing zone on the same story with a modal warning dialog that blocks the API until it is dismissed, so by default such an item fails with an error naming the overlapping zone and no element is created for it. Set it to true to skip this check and create the zone anyway; the dialog may then appear. Zones that only touch (a shared edge or corner) do not overlap; curved edges are checked by their chords, and an automatic zone counts as overlapping when its referencePosition lies inside an existing zone.

height.description: Optional height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height); when omitted, the height and top link of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults are kept. Do not combine with relativeTopStory.

bottomOffset.description: Optional base level of the zone relative to its home story level.

topOffset.description: Optional offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Optional top link: non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not combine with height.

floorThickness.description: Optional thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

example.description: Creates a 6 m x 5 m zone named Office from its outline with CreateZones, with its contour line drawn. A zone that would overlap an existing zone on the same story fails with an error instead (unless allowOverlap is true). Give 'geometry': {'referencePosition': {'x': ..., 'y': ...}} instead to create an automatic zone in the room around that point. contourLine and coverFill take the same keys in ModifyZones; fields left out keep the Zone tool defaults.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

parameters.description: Optional GDL parameters to set by name, after dimensions. The value is a number, a boolean or a string; array parameters are not supported. A or B also set the size. An unknown name or a value of the wrong type fails the item, and nothing is created for it.

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

databaseId.description: Optional database to place the elements in, e.g. a worksheet or a detail (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), for a legend of symbols. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are placed in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

example.description: Places the first Lamp library part of the loaded libraries 2.5 m above the floor, switched on, with CreateLamps. Give any loaded lamp library part name in libraryPartName, e.g. one listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts. The lamp starts from the library part's own default size and parameters; GDL 'parameters' given by name override them, and 'layerIndex' puts it on a layer (here the first layer of the project). A top-level 'databaseId' (e.g. the one CreateWorksheets returns) places the lamps in that database instead of the current one, as in the CreateObjects example.
example.code:
"""Places the first Lamp library part of the loaded libraries 2.5 m above the floor, switched on, with CreateLamps.

Give any loaded lamp library part name in libraryPartName, e.g. one listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.
The lamp starts from the library part's own default size and parameters; GDL 'parameters' given by
name override them, and 'layerIndex' puts it on a layer (here the first layer of the project).
A top-level 'databaseId' (e.g. the one CreateWorksheets returns) places the lamps in that database
instead of the current one, as in the CreateObjects example.
"""
import aclib

libraryParts = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAvailableLibraryParts', {'filterByTypeId': 'Lamp'})['libraryParts']
if not libraryParts:
    raise SystemExit ('No Lamp library part in the loaded libraries.')
layers = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Layer'})['attributes']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLamps', {'lampsData': [{
    'libraryPartName': libraryParts[0]['documentName'],
    'coordinates': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 2.5},
    'lightIsOn': True,
    'lightColor': {'red': 1.0, 'green': 0.9, 'blue': 0.8},
    'parameters': [{'name': 'A', 'value': 0.5}],
    'layerIndex': layers[0]['index']
}]}))

commands.name: CreateGridElements
commands.description: Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

begCoordinate.description: Start point of the grid line (the object's insertion point).

endCoordinate.description: End point of the grid line. Sets the direction and, unless lengthMode is 'none', the length.

lengthMode.description: How the line length is applied. length (default): to the GDL parameter AC_Length when the library part has it, as the Grid Tool's grid marker does; otherwise to the object's A size, converted to xRatio as CreateObjects does. none: the length is left to 'parameters'.

floorIndex.description: Home story index. Default: the tool default.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index. Only a positive index takes effect. Default: the tool default.

parameters.description: GDL parameters to set by name (read the names with GetGridElementDefaults). The value is a number, a boolean or a string. Unknown names and wrong value types are reported in warnings and skipped. The tool defaults can look different from a grid drawn with the Grid Tool (for example a short line with a leader to the bubble); to get the same look, copy the parameters of such a grid (GetGridElements with includeParameters).

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

warnings.description: Parameters that were not set, prefixed with the index of the grid element.

example.description: Creates two crossing 20 m long grid lines with CreateGridElements. The library part comes from the Grid Tool defaults; parameters sets GDL parameters by name (see GetGridElementDefaults). Requires Archicad 26 or later.

commands.name: CreateLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements based on the given parameters.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create Labels.

items.description: The parameters of the new Label.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

parentElementId.description: The parent element if the label is an associative label.

labelClass.description: Optional; if omitted, inherits the current Label tool default (which may silently resolve to either class - explicitly setting this avoids ambiguity). 'Symbol' needs a symbol library part, which only the Label tool default or the favorite given in favoriteName can provide: when those are a Text label, the item fails instead of placing a label without content.

text.description: The text content if the label is a text label. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

runs.description: Multi-style text content for a text label: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

begCoordinate.description: The begin coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter, but either begCoordinate or parentElementId must be provided. Unless midCoordinate and endCoordinate are both given too, the label is created at its default position relative to the parent element (Archicad's 'createAtDefaultPosition'), so the label may not end up at begCoordinate - read it back with GetDetailsOfElements after creation.

midCoordinate.description: The mid coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with endCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

endCoordinate.description: The end coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with midCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor or the floor of the parent element is used.

databaseId.description: Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

example.description: Labels the first wall with a text label with CreateLabels. Needs at least one Wall. Without parentElementId the label stands on its own at begCoordinate.
example.code:
"""Labels the first wall with a text label with CreateLabels.

Needs at least one Wall. Without parentElementId the label stands on its own at begCoordinate.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLabels', {'labelsData': [{
    'parentElementId': walls[0]['elementId'],
    'labelClass': 'Text',
    'text': 'Exterior wall'
}]}))

commands.name: CreateTexts

textsData.description: Array of data to create Texts.
