commands.name: CreateLevelDimensions
commands.description: Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes.

levelDimensionsData.description: Array of data to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan).

items.description: The parameters of the new Level Dimension.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Level Dimension favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (marker, format, text style, layer, pen) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

position.description: The location of the marker on the floor plan. With a parentElementId it must lie on that element, the measured level is the parent's height at this point. Outside the parent's outline Archicad still creates the dimension, but without a height (GetDetailsOfElements reads a level of -110000000).

parentElementId.description: Optional element the level dimension is associated with (Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Beam, Column, Wall, Object, Stair ...). The dimension then shows the element's height at the position and follows the element when it changes. Without it the dimension measures the floor level, or the given static level.

level.description: Optional fixed level value in meters (absolute, from the project zero). Only used without parentElementId; the dimension then shows this value instead of the floor level.

floorIndex.description: The index of the floor to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the floor of the parent element, otherwise the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the layer of the favorite or the Level Dimension tool default is used.

pen.description: Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.

textHeight.description: Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size), applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

textPen.description: Pen index of the dimension text, applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

dimForm.description: Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.

needPlus.description: Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.

markerSize.description: Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.

origin.description: The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

example.description: Creates a slab and puts an associative level dimension on it with CreateLevelDimensions, plus one showing a fixed level. The associative one shows the slab's level at its position and follows the slab when it changes; level (in meters, from the project zero) is only used without parentElementId.

commands.name: ModifyLevelDimensions
commands.description: Changes existing Level Dimension elements: the position of the marker and the settings CreateLevelDimensions takes (pen, text height and pen, marker type and size, plus sign, angle, origin), with the same keys. Not written: the parent element and the static level (delete and recreate the dimension to change them), the text content and the hide-with-base-element setting.

levelDimensionsWithDetails.description: The Level Dimensions to change, each with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed.

position.description: The new location of the marker on the floor plan. An associative level dimension then shows the height of its element at the new position. Optional parameter.

pen.description: Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.

textHeight.description: Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size), applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

textPen.description: Pen index of the dimension text, applied to both texts of the marker. Optional parameter.

dimForm.description: Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.

needPlus.description: Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.

markerSize.description: Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.

origin.description: The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

example.description: Creates a level dimension showing a fixed level, then moves it and changes its marker and texts with ModifyLevelDimensions. The settings have the keys CreateLevelDimensions takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns; only the given ones are changed.
example.code:
"""Creates a level dimension showing a fixed level, then moves it and changes its marker and texts with ModifyLevelDimensions.

The settings have the keys CreateLevelDimensions takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns; only the
given ones are changed.
"""
import aclib

levelDimension = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLevelDimensions', {'levelDimensionsData': [
    {'position': {'x': 2.0, 'y': 2.0}, 'level': 0.5}
]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyLevelDimensions', {'levelDimensionsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': levelDimension['elementId'],
    'position': {'x': 3.0, 'y': 2.0},
    'pen': 3,
    'textHeight': 3.0,
    'textPen': 5,
    'markerSize': 4.0,
    'needPlus': True
}]}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [levelDimension]}))

commands.name: ModifyWalls
commands.description: Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as CreateWalls, applied by the same code, plus geometryType (Straight or Trapezoid), profileType and bottomOffset. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'.

geometryType.description: Polygonal is not settable here; it is read-only via GetDetailsOfElements. This is unrelated to slantAlpha/slantBeta - see profileType for the cross section shape those depend on.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero makes the wall curved (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch such a wall first.

flipped.description: True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped).

profileType.description: slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is set to Slanted.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' for the same wall: whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

visibility.description: Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.

cutFillPen.description: Pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Background pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen. Not inheritable/overridable like cutFillPen, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field regardless of structureType.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

example.description: Creates a wall, then makes it longer, higher and thicker with ModifyWalls, and stops it reducing zone areas. Only the given fields change. A new thickness only takes effect on a Basic wall. ModifyWalls takes the same wall settings as CreateWalls, plus geometryType, profileType and bottomOffset.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall, then makes it longer, higher and thicker with ModifyWalls, and stops it reducing zone areas.

Only the given fields change. A new thickness only takes effect on a Basic wall. ModifyWalls takes
the same wall settings as CreateWalls, plus geometryType, profileType and bottomOffset.
"""
import aclib

wall = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'height': 3.0
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyWalls', {'wallsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': wall['elementId'],
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'height': 3.5,
    'structureType': 'Basic',
    'thickness': 0.4,
    'zoneRel': 'None'
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [wall], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyBeams
commands.description: Modifies Beam elements based on the given parameters. CreateBeams takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill, and the same absolute zCoordinate of the reference line (with an optional floorIndex). Not written: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the beam's reference line, as in CreateBeams. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; level, when given too, is applied after it.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story (combine with level to set the offset relative to it).

level.description: Elevation of the reference line relative to the home story.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the beam to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

holes.description: Replaces all holes currently placed on the beam.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the beam in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

example.description: Creates a beam, then changes its cross section and adds a round hole with ModifyBeams, and moves it: a new reference line and its absolute elevation (zCoordinate, as in CreateBeams). Only the given fields change; holes replaces every hole of the beam.
example.code:
"""Creates a beam, then changes its cross section and adds a round hole with ModifyBeams,
and moves it: a new reference line and its absolute elevation (zCoordinate, as in CreateBeams).

Only the given fields change; holes replaces every hole of the beam.
"""
import aclib

beam = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateBeams', {'beamsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'zCoordinate': 3.0
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyBeams', {'beamsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': beam['elementId'],
    'isWidthAndHeightLinked': False,
    'width': 0.3,
    'height': 0.6,
    'holes': [{'type': 'Circular', 'centerX': 3.0, 'centerZ': 0.3, 'width': 0.15}]
}]}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyBeams', {'beamsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': beam['elementId'],
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 1.0, 'y': 2.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 7.0, 'y': 2.0},
    'zCoordinate': 2.5
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [beam], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifySlabs
commands.description: Modifies Slab elements based on the given parameters. CreateSlabs takes the same surfaces, cut fill pens and floor fill. Not written: the surface of a single edge, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Of the cover fill orientation, Archicad applies only the type to a Slab through the API; a given origin or distortion matrix that did not stick gets a failed execution result, while the other details are applied.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the slab's reference level. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative level.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite slab first.

polygonOutline.description: Replaces the slab's entire polygon, including its holes - resend the holes field too to keep them, otherwise they are removed.

holes.description: Can be given on its own, without polygonOutline, to add/remove/clear holes in place (an empty array clears all holes) - the slab's current outline is reused unchanged.

topMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the top of the slab.

sideMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the sides of the slab.

bottomMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the bottom of the slab.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

floorFill.description: The cover fill of the slab in the floor plan. Only the given fields change; of the orientation Archicad applies only its type through the API, read it back with GetDetailsOfElements.

example.description: Creates a slab, then raises it, makes it thicker and replaces its outline with ModifySlabs. Only the given fields change; polygonOutline replaces the whole polygon, holes included.
example.code:
"""Creates a slab, then raises it, makes it thicker and replaces its outline with ModifySlabs.

Only the given fields change; polygonOutline replaces the whole polygon, holes included.
"""
import aclib

slab = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateSlabs', {'slabsData': [{
    'level': 0.0,
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0}]
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifySlabs', {'slabsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': slab['elementId'],
    'zCoordinate': 0.5,
    'structureType': 'Basic',
    'thickness': 0.3,
    'polygonOutline': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [slab], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyColumns
commands.description: Modifies Column elements based on the given parameters. CreateColumns takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill. Not written: the surfaces of the column segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the column's bottom. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative bottomOffset.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story (combine with bottomOffset to set the offset relative to it).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - see the note on relativeTopStory below.

isFlipped.description: Has no visible effect on a circular column (circleBased cross section) - Archicad ignores it there.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the column's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the column to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

veneer.description: Veneer of the column (type, thickness, building material); only the given fields change, thickness 0 removes it. Applied to all segments.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

coverFill.description: The cover fill of the column in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

example.description: Creates a column, then moves it, rotates it by 45 degrees and makes it 0.5 m x 0.3 m with ModifyColumns. Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
example.code:
"""Creates a column, then moves it, rotates it by 45 degrees and makes it 0.5 m x 0.3 m with ModifyColumns.

Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
"""
import aclib
import math

column = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateColumns', {'columnsData': [{
    'coordinates': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0}
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyColumns', {'columnsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': column['elementId'],
    'origin': {'x': 2.0, 'y': 1.0},
    'axisRotationAngle': math.radians (45),
    'circleBased': False,
    'isWidthAndHeightLinked': False,
    'width': 0.5,
    'depth': 0.3
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [column], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyWindows
commands.description: Modifies Window elements based on the given parameters.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

pen.description: Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the opening.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

example.description: Creates a wall with a window, then makes the window wider and moves it along the wall with ModifyWindows. Only the given fields change. centerOffset is measured along the wall from its begin point.

commands.name: ModifyDoors
commands.description: Modifies Door elements based on the given parameters.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

pen.description: Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the opening.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

example.description: Creates a wall with a door, then mirrors the door and moves it along the wall with ModifyDoors. Only the given fields change. centerOffset is measured along the wall from its begin point.

commands.name: ModifyOpenings
commands.description: Modifies Opening elements: the width, the height and the base point CreateOpenings takes. Needs Archicad 28 or earlier; in Archicad 29 and later every item fails with a message pointing to SetOpeningDetails, which changes the size and the position of an opening there.

basePoint.description: New base point of the opening: its bottom left corner in world space, the same point CreateOpenings takes.

width.description: New width of the opening.

height.description: New height of the opening. The bottom edge stays where it is, the opening grows or shrinks upwards.

example.description: Creates a wall with an opening, then resizes and moves the opening with ModifyOpenings. Requires Archicad 28 or earlier; from Archicad 29 use SetOpeningDetails instead.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall with an opening, then resizes and moves the opening with ModifyOpenings.

Requires Archicad 28 or earlier; from Archicad 29 use SetOpeningDetails instead.
"""
import aclib

wall = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'height': 3.0
}]})['elements'][0]

opening = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateOpenings', {'openingsData': [{
    'ownerElementId': wall['elementId'],
    'basePoint': {'x': 2.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 1.0},
    'width': 0.8,
    'height': 0.8
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyOpenings', {'openingsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': opening['elementId'],
    'basePoint': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.5},
    'width': 1.2,
    'height': 1.5
}]}))

commands.name: ModifyMorphs
commands.description: Modifies Morph elements based on the given parameters.

rotationDegreesZ.description: Turns the Morph about the vertical axis through its origin, counterclockwise seen from above, in degrees. Added to the current rotation.

body.description: When given, discards the Morph's ENTIRE existing geometry and rebuilds it from this (mirrors CreateProfiles' replaceSkins) - not a partial edit.

xAxis.description: Replaces the rotation part of the placement transform outright. Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together. If rotationDegreesZ is also given in the same call, it is applied first and this then overwrites its result.

example.description: Creates a box morph, then moves it 3 m along X and turns it by 30 degrees with ModifyMorphs. rotationDegreesZ is in degrees and is added to the current rotation.

commands.name: ModifyRoofs
commands.description: Modifies single-plane and multi-plane Roof elements based on the given parameters. The plan outline, level, thickness and structure apply to both; angle, pivotLine and edgeTrims (the cut of each polygon edge) only to single-plane roofs; levels, eavesOverhang and pivotEdges only to multi-plane roofs.

level.description: Absolute elevation of the roof's pivot line (the zCoordinate GetDetailsOfElements returns). The roof is put on the story floorIndex when given, else on the story at this elevation.

floorIndex.description: Home story of the roof. With level, the roof gets this home story at the absolute elevation level; without level, it moves to this story and keeps its offset from the story.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite roof first.

angle.description: Single-plane roofs only: the angle of the plane to the XY plane.

pivotLine.description: Single-plane roofs only: the line the plane rises from. The ends are named begCoordinate and endCoordinate as in CreateRoofs, or begin and end as GetDetailsOfElements reports them.

edgeTrims.description: Single-plane roofs only: the cut of each edge of the roof's polygon, one item per edge in the order GetDetailsOfElements reports them in edgeTrims (the outline, then each hole). Only the given fields change; an empty item keeps its edge. Cannot be combined with polygonOutline.

trimType.description: Vertical, Perpendicular to the roof plane, Horizontal, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle).

angle.description: The angle of the edge cut in radians, as GetDetailsOfElements reports it. Only CustomAngle uses it.

pivotEdges.description: Multi-plane roofs only: the roof planes of each edge of the pivot polygon, one item per edge in the order GetDetailsOfElements reports them (the outline, then each hole). Only the given fields change; an item without levels keeps its edge. Cannot be combined with polygonOutline.

levels.description: The roof plane of the edge on each level, from the pivot polygon upwards; at most as many as the roof has levels.

angle.description: Angle of the plane to the XY plane.

eavesOverhang.description: Extension of the eaves outside the pivot polygon.

angleType.description: Gable for a vertical gable plane, Sloped otherwise.

example.description: Creates a multi-plane and a single-plane roof, then changes both with ModifyRoofs. The multi-plane roof is raised and gets a new slope and eaves overhang. The single-plane roof gets a steeper angle, a new pivot line and a wider outline. Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
example.code:
"""Creates a multi-plane and a single-plane roof, then changes both with ModifyRoofs.

The multi-plane roof is raised and gets a new slope and eaves overhang. The single-plane roof gets a
steeper angle, a new pivot line and a wider outline. Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
"""
import aclib
import math

roofs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRoofs', {'roofsData': [{
    'level': 3.0,
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 8.0, 'y': 6.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 6.0}],
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (30)}]
}, {
    'level': 3.0,
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 12.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 12.0, 'y': 4.0}],
    'pivotLine': {'begCoordinate': {'x': 12.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 18.0, 'y': 0.0}},
    'angle': math.radians (15)
}]})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyRoofs', {'roofsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': roofs[0]['elementId'],
    'level': 3.5,
    'eavesOverhang': 0.5,
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (40)}]
}, {
    'elementId': roofs[1]['elementId'],
    'angle': math.radians (25),
    'pivotLine': {'begCoordinate': {'x': 12.0, 'y': -1.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 18.0, 'y': -1.0}},
    'polygonOutline': [{'x': 12.0, 'y': -1.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': -1.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': 5.0}, {'x': 12.0, 'y': 5.0}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': roofs, 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyShells
commands.description: Modifies the structure (Basic or Composite, building material or composite) of Shell elements based on the given parameters.

example.description: Makes the first shell a Basic shell of the first building material with ModifyShells, reads it back, then restores its structure. Needs at least one Shell.

commands.name: ModifyMeshes
commands.description: Modifies the attributes of Mesh elements based on the given parameters.

example.description: Creates a flat mesh, then gives it a skirt and a raised corner with ModifyMeshes. Only the fields given in meshData change; polygonCoordinates replaces the whole outline, z being the height of each point above level.

commands.name: ModifyRailings
commands.description: Modifies Railing elements in place: the height of their segments, the bottom offset and the home story. The reference line, the nodes and segments, and the posts, rails and panels stay as they are. Each railing is read back after the change, and a value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result.

height.description: The new height of the railing segments (the height GetDetailsOfElements returns), applied to every segment of the railing.

bottomOffset.description: The new base height of the railing relative to its home story.

floorIndex.description: The new home story index (as returned by GetStories). The bottom offset is kept, or set from bottomOffset when that is given too, so the railing moves with the story.

example.description: Creates a railing, then makes it 1.2 m high and raises it by 0.15 m with ModifyRailings. Only the given fields change; the reference line, posts, rails and panels stay as they are. GetDetailsOfElements reads the new height, bottomOffset and segmentHeights back.

commands.name: ModifyObjects
commands.description: Modifies Object elements based on the given parameters.

objectsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

example.description: Places an object, then moves it, turns it by 90 degrees and mirrors it with ModifyObjects. The object is the first Object library part of the loaded libraries. Angles are in radians.

commands.name: ModifyLamps
commands.description: Modifies Lamp elements based on the given parameters.

lampsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

lightColor.description: Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.

example.description: Places a lamp, then raises it, switches it off and makes its light blue with ModifyLamps. The lamp is the first Lamp library part of the loaded libraries. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1.

commands.name: ModifyTexts
commands.description: Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

textsWithDetails.description: Array of Text elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run text applies that style to every run; a text that wraps keeps its wrap width through the rebuild unless the same item gives a width. The other style fields and a width leave the content as it is.

coordinate.description: The new placement position. As in CreateTexts, the z value selects the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

floorIndex.description: Optional. Moves the text to this floor; when omitted and a coordinate is given, the floor is derived from its z value.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

width.description: Optional box width in mm (paper size, like height). Greater than 0 turns word wrap on: the text wraps within this width ('Wrap Text' in the Text settings, nonBreaking false). 0 turns word wrap off: the text is auto-width and grows with its content; on a wrapped text this rebuilds the content, so like a pen change it is refused for content with an autotext run. Given alone it leaves the content and its runs (and any autotext in them) as they are. When the content is rebuilt in the same item, the width is applied after the rebuild. When omitted, the current wrap setting is kept, also through a rebuild of the content. Read back by GetDetailsOfElements as style.boxWidth, with style.nonBreaking false.

example.description: Creates a text, then replaces its content, makes it bold and 5 mm high, and moves it with ModifyTexts. Then it gives the text a fixed width of 20 mm, so it wraps, without changing its content. Only the given fields change; text replaces the whole content (see ChangeTextContent to change a part). A text that wraps keeps its wrap width when its content or style is rebuilt; width 0 turns word wrap off.

commands.name: ModifyLabels
commands.description: Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters.

labelsWithDetails.description: Array of Label elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. The label's class (Text/Symbol) cannot be changed after creation. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the label's text auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run label applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

example.description: Creates a wall with a text label, then changes the label's text, frame and arrow with ModifyLabels. Only the given fields change.

commands.name: ModifyCurtainWalls
commands.description: Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls.

curtainWallsWithDetails.description: Array of Curtain Wall elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the others, and the frames and panels not affected by them, are left as they are. The fields are those of CreateCurtainWalls, so a curtain wall can be changed in place instead of being deleted and recreated, keeping its GUID, properties and classifications.

coordinates.description: The new 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates is one straight segment, so the number of coordinates must be the current number of segments plus one: the segments can be moved and resized, but not added or removed (a curved segment becomes straight).

zCoordinate.description: The new Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given too.

floorIndex.description: The new home story index. On its own it moves the curtain wall to that story, keeping its bottom offset from the story; with zCoordinate it pins the story the bottom elevation is measured from.

height.description: The new height of the curtain wall. It is applied before the other fields and read back: when Archicad does not apply it, the item fails and the curtain wall is left unchanged.

primaryPattern.description: The new column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segments (the primary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.

secondaryPattern.description: The new row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.

cells.description: Assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit of every segment, as in CreateCurtainWalls. Without a pattern change, a cell not listed here keeps its current assignment; with one, it takes the assignment of the first current cell.

example.description: Creates a curtain wall, then makes it 4 m high with 1 m wide columns with ModifyCurtainWalls. The curtain wall keeps its GUID, properties and classifications.

commands.name: ModifyCurtainWallFrames
commands.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Modifies single Curtain Wall Frames by their GUID: the frame contour (a1, a2, b1, b2), the frame class and the frame type. ACAPI_Element_Change does not take a frame on its own, so the change is written through the memo of the owner curtain wall, and read back to check that Archicad applied it.

framesWithDetails.description: Curtain Wall Frames to modify (the GUIDs from GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements), with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed. EXPERIMENTAL.

frameContour.description: The contour of the frame, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it. Only the given keys are changed.

classIndex.description: The frame class (classID) of the frame: 0 to 3 for the built-in classes, 4 and up for the frame classes of the owner curtain wall.

type.description: The type of the frame (API_CWFrameObjectTypeID).

example.description: EXPERIMENTAL: changes the contour and the type of the first frame of a new curtain wall with ModifyCurtainWallFrames. The frame is found by its GUID, which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements returns.
example.code:
"""EXPERIMENTAL: changes the contour and the type of the first frame of a new curtain wall with ModifyCurtainWallFrames.

The frame is found by its GUID, which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements returns.
"""
import aclib

curtainWall = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateCurtainWalls', {'curtainWallsData': [{
    'coordinates': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0}],
    'zCoordinate': 0.0,
    'height': 3.0,
    'primaryPattern': {'sizes': [1.5]}
}]})['elements'][0]

subelements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements', {'elements': [curtainWall]})
frame = subelements['subelements'][0]['cWallFrames'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyCurtainWallFrames', {'framesWithDetails': [{
    'frameId': frame['elementId'],
    'frameContour': {'a1': 0.01, 'a2': 0.01, 'b1': 0.0, 'b2': 0.10},
    'type': 'GDL'
}]}))

commands.name: ModifyStairs
commands.description: Modifies Stair elements in place, keeping their baseline and position: the flight width, total height, number of steps, riser height and going with their locks, the finish and structure visibility, the extra top and bottom treads, the walking line position and offset, the step numbering, the walking direction, the uniform finish, monolith and draining settings, and for the flights and the landings the tread and riser settings (presence, thickness, offset, nosing, riser cross section and position) and the structure of each side (presence, type, underside shape and thickness). CreateStairs accepts the same settings. Only the given settings are changed. Archicad solves the stair again within its baseline, so it may adjust the step values; read them back with GetDetailsOfElements. Not written by this command: the baseline with its landings and winders, the top link, the floor plan display (symbol and marker layout), the headroom and the stair rules; the subelements (treads, risers, structures) take the per-part settings above and cannot be written one by one through the API.

stairsWithDetails.description: Array of Stair elements to modify, with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed; the baseline, the position and the omitted settings are kept.

totalHeight.description: The height of the stair relative to its bottom.

treadDepthLocked.description: Whether the going lengths are locked.

totalHeightLocked.description: Whether the total height is locked.

finishVisible.description: Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.

extraTopTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.

extraBottomTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.

walkingLinePosition.description: Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).

walkingLineOffset.description: The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.

numberingType.description: Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.

inputDirection.description: The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).

uniformFinish.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.

uniformMonolithAttributes.description: Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.

uniformDrainings.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.

structureVisibility.description: Whether the structure of the stair is shown.

treads.description: The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the treads.

nosingType.description: Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).

nosingSlant.description: The slant of the nosing in radians.

risers.description: The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the risers.

crossSection.description: The cross section of the risers.

angle.description: The angle of a slanted riser in radians.

position.description: Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

structures.description: The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

structureType.description: The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.

bottomType.description: The shape of the underside of the structure.

horizontalThickness.description: The horizontal thickness of the structure.

example.description: Creates a straight stair, then changes its width, its walking line, its tread thickness and its structure with ModifyStairs. Makes the flights monolithic with a smooth underside and numbers the steps on the risers, reads the stair back with GetDetailsOfElements, then deletes the stair it created.
example.code:
"""Creates a straight stair, then changes its width, its walking line, its tread thickness and its structure with ModifyStairs.

Makes the flights monolithic with a smooth underside and numbers the steps on the risers, reads the
stair back with GetDetailsOfElements, then deletes the stair it created.
"""
import aclib

stairs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateStairs', {'stairsData': [{
    'baseLinePoints': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}],
    'zCoordinate': 0.0,
    'totalHeight': 3.0,
    'flightWidth': 1.2
}]})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyStairs', {'stairsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': stairs[0]['elementId'],
    'flightWidth': 1.4,
    'walkingLinePosition': 'Center',
    'numberingType': 'Risers',
    'treads': [{'role': 'Run', 'visible': True, 'thickness': 0.04}],
    'structures': [{'role': 'Run', 'side': 'UnderSide', 'visible': True, 'structureType': 'Monolith', 'bottomType': 'Smooth', 'thickness': 0.18}]
}]}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': stairs}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': stairs})

commands.name: ChangeTextContent
commands.description: Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content.

contentChanges.description: The content changes, applied in order (several changes of one element see the content as the previous one left it). Unlike ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels, the rest of the content is not rebuilt: the other runs, their styles and any autotext in them stay as they are, and the inserted piece takes the style of the character at 'from'.

example.description: Creates the text 'Hello World', then replaces 'World' with 'Tapir' with ChangeTextContent. from is the character position, range the number of characters replaced (0 inserts). The styles of the rest of the content and the autotexts in it are kept. A range must stay within one line.
example.code:
"""Creates the text 'Hello World', then replaces 'World' with 'Tapir' with ChangeTextContent.

from is the character position, range the number of characters replaced (0 inserts). The styles of
the rest of the content and the autotexts in it are kept. A range must stay within one line.
"""
import aclib

text = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateTexts', {'textsData': [{
    'coordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0},
    'text': 'Hello World'
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeTextContent', {'contentChanges': [{
    'elementId': text['elementId'],
    'from': len ('Hello '),
    'range': len ('World'),
    'content': 'Tapir'
}]}))

commands.name: ModifyZones
commands.description: Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, height, base offset, top link, floor thickness, contour line and cover fill - the same settings as CreateZones, applied by the same helpers. Only the given fields are changed. The polygon of a manual zone cannot be changed here (the change takes no polygon memo), nor the reference point of an automatic one (SetDetailsOfElements moves it).

zonesWithDetails.description: Array of Zone elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon and the omitted fields are kept. The same fields as the ZoneSettings of SetDetailsOfElements.

name.description: Name of the zone.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

stampAngle.description: Rotation angle of the zone stamp in radians.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

height.description: Height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height), so do not combine it with relativeTopStory in the same call: whichever is applied last wins.

bottomOffset.description: Base level of the zone relative to its home story level.

topOffset.description: Offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not set together with height in the same call, see the note on height.

floorThickness.description: Thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

contourLine.description: Contour line of the zone. Only the given fields are changed.

coverFill.description: Cover fill of the zone. Only the given fields are changed.

example.description: Renames and renumbers the first zone and changes its contour line pen with ModifyZones, reads it back, then restores them. Needs at least one Zone. Only the given fields change; the polygon is kept. ModifyZones takes the same settings as CreateZones, contourLine and coverFill included.

commands.name: MeasureTexts
commands.description: Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.

texts.description: The texts to measure, each with the font, style and height it would be placed with. Nothing is created.

text.description: The text to measure. Newlines separate lines, each measured on its own; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are treated as LF.

fontIndex.description: The index of the font, as GetDetailsOfElements and GetFontsByName report it in fontIndex. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

fontName.description: Name of the font as Archicad's font list carries it (GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontName), which is not always the operating system's font name; GetFontsByName tells whether a name is found. Resolved to the font's index (exact match first, then case-insensitive, then Archicad's font search as GetFontsByName does, so a family name such as 'Arial' finds 'Arial Western'); the text fails when no loaded font has the name. Takes precedence over fontIndex if both are given. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

height.description: The character height in millimetres, as a Text's height.

slant.description: The slant angle of the characters in radians; pi/2 (the default) is upright text.

inModelUnits.description: When true, Archicad applies the drawing scale correction and the lengths are model distances at the current drawing scale; when false (the default), they are lengths on paper in millimetres.

measurements.description: One item per input text, in the same order. The measurement takes no width factor or character spacing into account.

example.description: Measures the length of each line of a two-line text in Arial 2.5 mm, on paper and in the model, with MeasureTexts. Creates nothing. Model lengths use the drawing scale of the current window.
example.code:
"""Measures the length of each line of a two-line text in Arial 2.5 mm, on paper and in the model, with MeasureTexts.

Creates nothing. Model lengths use the drawing scale of the current window.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MeasureTexts', {'texts': [
    {'text': 'Living Room\n24.5 m2', 'fontName': 'Arial', 'height': 2.5},
    {'text': 'Living Room\n24.5 m2', 'fontName': 'Arial', 'height': 2.5, 'bold': True, 'inModelUnits': True}
]}))

commands.name: GetElementPreviewImage
commands.description: Returns the preview image of the given element.

imageType.description: The type of the preview image. Default is 3D.

format.description: The image format. Default is png.

width.description: The width of the preview image in pixels. Default is 128.

height.description: The height of the preview image in pixels. Default is 128.

example.description: Saves the 3D preview image of the first wall as a PNG file in the temp folder with GetElementPreviewImage. Needs at least one Wall. The image comes base64 encoded.
example.code:
"""Saves the 3D preview image of the first wall as a PNG file in the temp folder with GetElementPreviewImage.

Needs at least one Wall. The image comes base64 encoded.
"""
import aclib
import base64
import os
import tempfile

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementPreviewImage', {
    'elementId': walls[0]['elementId'],
    'imageType': '3D',
    'format': 'png',
    'width': 256,
    'height': 256
})

path = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'wall_preview.png')
with open (path, 'wb') as file:
    file.write (base64.b64decode (response['previewImage']))
print ('Saved ' + path)

commands.name: GetModelExtent
commands.description: Returns the 3D extent (xMin, yMin, zMin, xMax, yMax, zMax) of the current database, the region Archicad's Fit in Window would show.

example.description: Prints the model extent with GetModelExtent: the region Fit in Window would show in the current database, vertical range included. A stray element far from the building makes it much larger than expected.
example.code:
"""Prints the model extent with GetModelExtent: the region Fit in Window would show in the current database, vertical range included.

A stray element far from the building makes it much larger than expected.
"""
import aclib

extent = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetModelExtent')

if extent is None or 'error' in extent:
    print ('Failed to get the model extent.')
    raise SystemExit (1)

width = extent['xMax'] - extent['xMin']
depth = extent['yMax'] - extent['yMin']
height = extent['zMax'] - extent['zMin']
print ('x: {0:.2f} .. {1:.2f}'.format (extent['xMin'], extent['xMax']))
print ('y: {0:.2f} .. {1:.2f}'.format (extent['yMin'], extent['yMax']))
print ('z: {0:.2f} .. {1:.2f}'.format (extent['zMin'], extent['zMax']))
print ('The model spans {0:.2f} x {1:.2f} x {2:.2f} m'.format (width, depth, height))

commands.name: SetElementNotificationClient
commands.description: Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.

host.description: The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.

port.description: The port number of the notification client.

notifyOnNewElement.description: Notify on creation of a new element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnModificationOfAnElement.description: Notify on modification/deletion of an element. The observed elements are the ones ACAPI_Element_GetElemList returns, for API_ZombieElemID or, with elementTypesToObserve, for each of those types, when the first client asking for these notifications of them is registered, and every element of the observed types created after that. Archicad does not report the changes made by Tapir's own commands, so Tapir reports them itself for SetDetailsOfElements, SetPropertyValuesOfElements, MoveElements, RotateElements, MirrorElements (not for the copies they make, which are new elements), DeleteElements, DeleteSelectedElements, the Modify<Tool> commands (ModifyWalls, ModifyBeams, ModifySlabs, ModifyColumns, ModifyWindows, ModifyDoors, ModifyOpenings, ModifyMorphs, ModifyRoofs, ModifyShells, ModifyMeshes, ModifyObjects, ModifyLamps, ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels, ModifyCurtainWalls, ModifyCurtainWallFrames, ModifyZones, ModifySections, ModifyDetailMarkers, ModifyRailings, ModifyStairs), ChangeTextContent, SetGDLParametersOfElements, RunParameterScriptOfElements (only when the script changed the element), SetMarkerParametersOfElements, SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements, ChangeLibraryPartOfElements, SetClassificationsOfElements, SetCategoryValuesOfElements, ModifyPropertyValueOfElements, SetElementInfoStrings, SetURLReferencesOfElements, SetIFCAttributesOfElements, SetIFCPropertiesOfElements, RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements, SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, LockElements, UnlockElements, SetOpeningDetails, SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, SetOpeningSymbolParameters, CreateGroups and UngroupElements (the grouped elements), MoveElementsToDesignOptions, CreateSolidElementLinks, RemoveSolidElementLinks, CreateSolidOperations (the target and operator when the operation changed or deleted them; the results are new elements), TrimElements, RemoveElementTrims, MergeElements, UnmergeElements, ModifyMEPRoutingElements, ModifyMEPPorts (the element owning the port), ConnectMEPElements, ModifyMEPElements, SetMEPRoutingParameters, ModifyElectricalPanels, ModifyElectricalDevices and ConnectToElectricalCircuits. Of the elements these commands change, only the given ones are reported: an element deleted together with its owner (a door or window of a deleted wall) is not. UpdateZones is not reported by Tapir, because Archicad updates the Zones after the command has returned. When the user moves, rotates, mirrors, elevates, resizes or stretches elements in Archicad, each of their changedElements items also has a transformation: {"type": ..., ...}, where type is "Drag" (with displacement: {"x", "y", "z"}), "Elevate" (with displacement, only z is not 0), "Rotate" (with origin: {"x", "y"} and angle, in radians, counterclockwise), "Mirror" (with origin, a point of the mirror axis, and axisDirection: {"x", "y"}, its unit vector), "Resize" (with origin and ratio), "Stretch", "VerticalStretch", "PreservedHeightStretch", "PreservedDirectionStretch" or "General"; the changes made by Tapir's own commands and by undo or redo have no transformation. Optional parameter, by default true. Archicad attaches an observer to each element to observe (see elementTypesToObserve) when the first client asks for this, and detaches them when the last one stops, and it is blocked meanwhile: the time grows faster than the number of elements, from seconds for a few hundred elements to many minutes for a few thousand. Count the elements first (GetAllElements with IncludeSubElemObjects, or GetElementsByType) and limit the types on large projects.

elementTypesToObserve.description: Only modifications/deletions of elements of these types are observed and notified to this client. Optional parameter, by default every element (including the parts of curtain walls, stairs and railings, which are most of the elements of large projects). Registering the same client again with other types changes them; only the elements of types no client observed before get an observer then. Does not limit the other notifications.

notifyOnReservationChanges.description: Notify on reservation changes of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnSelectionChange.description: Notify when the selection changes. The message is {"selectedElements": [...]}: the whole current selection, each item an elementId as in the response of GetSelectedElements, an empty list when nothing is selected. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnWindowChange.description: Notify when the current (active) window changes or the user switches to another story. The message is {"windowChanged": {"event": "Window" or "Floor", "windowType": ..., "databaseId": ..., "storyIndex": ...}}: windowType and databaseId describe the new current window as in the response of GetCurrentWindowType (databaseId is missing when that response has none), storyIndex is the active story, missing when it cannot be read. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnProjectEvents.description: Notify on project events. The message is {"projectEvent": ...}, one of "New", "NewAndReset", "Open", "Close", "Quit", "SendChanges" (a Teamwork send is about to start) and "ReceiveChanges" (Teamwork changes were received). The client stays registered when the project is closed or another one is opened. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnAttributeReplacement.description: Notify when attributes are deleted and replaced by other attributes of the same type (for example Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager). The message is {"replacedAttributes": [{"attributeType": ..., "oldIndex": ..., "newIndex": ..., "newAttributeId": ...}, ...]}: attributeType is one of the type names of GetAttributesByType ("Layer", "Line", "Fill", "Composite", "Surface", "LayerCombination", "ZoneCategory", "Profile", "PenTable", "MEPSystem", "OperationProfile", "BuildingMaterial", or "Unknown"), oldIndex is the index of the replaced attribute and newIndex the index of the attribute that replaces it, newAttributeId is the attributeId of that attribute, missing when it cannot be found. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnToolChange.description: Notify when the user switches to another tool in the Toolbox. The message is {"toolChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type of the new tool, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), "None" for the Arrow and the Marquee, and "Unknown" for a tool Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnViewEvents.description: Notify when an item of the Project Navigator or the Organizer is inserted (for example a view is saved or a layout is created), modified (for example renamed), deleted or opened. The message is {"viewEvent": {"event": ..., "navigatorMapId": ..., "navigatorItemId": {"guid": ...}}}: event is one of "Inserted", "Modified", "Deleted" and "Opened", navigatorMapId is the navigator map of the item, one of "ProjectMap", "PublicViewMap", "MyViewMap", "LayoutBook" and "PublisherSets" (as navigatorMapId of GetNavigatorItemTree), and navigatorItemId is the guid of the navigator item, as in the response of GetNavigatorItemTree (a deleted item no longer exists). Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnLockableReservationChanges.description: Notify when a Teamwork lockable object set (the non-element things Teamwork reserves: the attributes of a type, favorites, model view options, project info, project preferences, ...) is reserved or released, by anyone, including the current user. The message is {"lockableReservationChanged": {"event": ..., "objectSetId": {"guid": ...}, "objectSetName": ..., "reservedBy": ..., "reservedByUserId": ...}}: event is "Reserved" or "Released", objectSetId is the guid of the object set, objectSetName its name as objectSetName of ReserveLockableObjectSet (for example "Composites", "LayerSettingsDialog" or "Favorites"), missing when it is not one of the documented sets, and reservedBy and reservedByUserId are the name and the Teamwork user id of the member who reserved it, only for "Reserved". Element reservations are notified by notifyOnReservationChanges. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnToolDefaultChanges.description: Notify when the default settings of a tool change (for example the user changes the settings of the Wall tool with no wall selected), so a client can read the new defaults. The message is {"toolDefaultsChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type whose defaults changed, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), and "Unknown" for a type Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnAttributeChanges.description: Notify when attributes (layers, fills, composites, surfaces, building materials, ...) are created, modified or deleted. The message is {"attributesChanged": {"event": ..., "attributeIds": [{"attributeId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and attributeIds are the attributes, as in the response of GetAttributesByType (a deleted attribute no longer exists). Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnClassificationChanges.description: Notify when classification systems or classification items are created, modified or deleted. The messages are {"classificationSystemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationSystemIds": [{"classificationSystemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"classificationItemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationItemIds": [{"classificationItemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllClassificationSystems and GetAllClassificationsInSystem. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnPropertyDefinitionChanges.description: Notify when property groups or property definitions are created, modified or deleted (property values of elements are notified as changedElements by notifyOnModificationOfAnElement). The messages are {"propertyGroupsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyGroupIds": [{"propertyGroupId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"propertyDefinitionsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllProperties. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnMarqueeChange.description: Notify when the marquee is drawn, changed or removed. The message is {"marqueeChanged": {"type": ..., "multiStory": ...}}: type is "rectangle", "rotatedRectangle", "polygon" or, when the marquee was removed, "none", as type of GetMarquee, which returns the shape of the marquee; multiStory is missing for "none". Available from Archicad 27: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOn3DSettingsChanges.description: Notify when the settings of the 3D window change (projection, Filter and Cut Elements in 3D, 3D window settings). The message is {"view3DSettingsChanged": {}}; read the new settings with the commands of the 3D window. The changes made while navigating in 3D are not notified. Available from Archicad 30: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

example.description: Prints the element events Archicad sends to a local HTTP server registered with SetElementNotificationClient. Creates a column to trigger a notification, then removes the client again. Archicad posts each event as JSON to http://<host>:<port>/element_notification. Modifications are observed only for columns here (elementTypesToObserve): attaching an observer to every element blocks Archicad for minutes on a project with thousands of elements.
example.code:
"""Prints the element events Archicad sends to a local HTTP server registered with SetElementNotificationClient.

Creates a column to trigger a notification, then removes the client again. Archicad posts each event
as JSON to http://<host>:<port>/element_notification.

Modifications are observed only for columns here (elementTypesToObserve): attaching an observer to
every element blocks Archicad for minutes on a project with thousands of elements.
"""
import aclib
import json
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

HOST = 'localhost'
PORT = 12345

class NotificationHandler (BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST (self):
        length = self.headers.get ('Content-Length')
        body = self.rfile.read (int (length)) if length else self.rfile.readline ()
        print (json.dumps (json.loads (body), indent = 4))
        self.send_response (200)
        self.end_headers ()

server = HTTPServer ((HOST, PORT), NotificationHandler)
threading.Thread (target = server.serve_forever, daemon = True).start ()

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetElementNotificationClient', {
    'host': HOST,
    'port': PORT,
    'notifyOnNewElement': True,
    'notifyOnModificationOfAnElement': True,
    'elementTypesToObserve': ['Column'],
    'notifyOnReservationChanges': False
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateColumns', {'columnsData': [{'coordinates': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0}}]})
time.sleep (2)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RemoveElementNotificationClient', {'host': HOST, 'port': PORT})
server.shutdown ()

host and port name the client given to SetElementNotificationClient.

commands.name: RegularizePolygons
commands.description: Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.

polygons.description: The polygons to regularize, in the format of CreateSlabs (polygonCoordinates, polygonArcs, holes). For CreateHatches, pass the outline of a result as its coordinates and arcs.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every vertex and edge of the results which input vertex or edge it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polygon, in the order of the request.

example.description: Regularizes a self-intersecting (bow tie) outline with a repeated point with RegularizePolygons. The results are in the format of CreateSlabs; nothing is created.

commands.name: RegularizePolylines
commands.description: Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.

polylines.description: The polylines to regularize, in the format of CreatePolylines.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every point and segment of the results which input point or segment it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polyline, in the order of the request.

example.description: Removes the repeated points of a polyline with RegularizePolylines, and reports which input point each result point came from. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines; nothing is created.

commands.name: GetSplineMaxDistances
commands.description: Measures how far the given 2D coordinates are from a segment of a Spline element, between two of its fit points, with its own Bezier handles: returns the largest distance, for example to check how well a polyline follows the spline. The output is aligned with the input array. Changes nothing in the project.

splines.description: The spline segments to measure and the coordinates to measure from them.

elementId.description: A Spline element.

segmentIndex.description: The segment of the spline between its fit points segmentIndex and segmentIndex + 1, from 0 to the number of fit points - 2 (the fit points are the coordinates GetDetailsOfElements returns for the spline).

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates to measure from the segment.

results.description: The result of each input item, in the same order, or an error.

maxDistance.description: The largest distance of the given coordinates from the spline segment.

example.description: GetSplineMaxDistances measures how far coordinates are from a segment of a Spline element (between its fit points segmentIndex and segmentIndex + 1), with the spline's own Bezier handles, and returns the largest distance. Here a spline is created and the midpoint of the straight line between its first two fit points is measured from its first segment.

commands.name: SetUserDataOfGroups
commands.description: Stores string values under keys in the user data of groups, for scripts to keep their own state on a group. The given pairs are merged into what each group already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. }))
