commands.name: ImportFavorites
commands.description: Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project. From Archicad 29 they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or the given fileNames) or from a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format), with the conflict policies Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting and RenameNew. In a Teamwork project the Favorites lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet).

path.description: Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: a Favorites file (.prefs) or folder. With the xml format: the folder of Favorite files, as ExportFavorites writes it. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file.

fileNames.description: Only with the xml format: the names of the Favorite files in the folder to import. Default: every Favorite file of the folder.

targetFolder.description: Folder hierarchy under which to import. Empty = root. With the xml and legacyPRF formats the folder must exist, and omitting it keeps the folders stored with the Favorites.

importFolders.description: Only with the prefs format: if true and `path` is a folder, the folder structure is preserved.

firstConflictName.description: Set when conflictPolicy=Error and a name collided; absent otherwise.

example.description: Imports a Favorite from a .prefs file with ImportFavorites. Needs at least one Wall. The script creates the Favorite 'Tapir Example Wall' from the first wall, exports it to a temporary file, deletes it, imports it again from the file and finally deletes it.
example.code:
"""Imports a Favorite from a .prefs file with ImportFavorites.

Needs at least one Wall. The script creates the Favorite 'Tapir Example Wall' from the first wall, exports it to a
temporary file, deletes it, imports it again from the file and finally deletes it.
"""
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

favoriteName = 'Tapir Example Wall'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateFavoritesFromElements', {
    'favoritesFromElements': [{'elementId': walls[0]['elementId'], 'favorite': favoriteName}]
})

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory () as tempDir:
    favoritesFile = os.path.join (tempDir, 'TapirExample.prefs')
    aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ExportFavorites', {'path': favoritesFile, 'names': [favoriteName]})
    aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteFavorites', {'favorites': [favoriteName]})

    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportFavorites', {
        'path': favoritesFile,
        'format': 'prefs',
        'conflictPolicy': 'Skip'
    }))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetFavoritesByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteFavorites', {'favorites': [favoriteName]})

commands.name: ExportFavorites
commands.description: Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format). With overwrite false an export to a single file refuses to replace an existing file.

path.description: Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: if extension matches the Favorite binary format (.prefs), writes a single file; otherwise treats as folder. With the xml format: the folder to write the Favorite files to. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file to write.

names.description: Optional subset of Favorites to export. Default: export all.

format.description: prefs (the default) works in every Archicad version. xml exports each Favorite to its own file in the folder, and legacyPRF exports to a Favorites file of earlier Archicad versions; these two require Archicad 29 or newer.

It needs an export to a single file (prefs format with a .prefs path, or legacyPRF format); with an export to a folder it is an error, as the names of the files written there are Archicad's.

Needs a Wall Favorite. The file is written into a new temporary folder.

commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements
commands.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes. With favorite instead of favoritesToApply, one Favorite is read once and applied to the given elements, or to every element of its type that matches the filter.

favoritesToApply.description: The elements and the Favorite to apply to each. Give this or favorite.

favorite.description: The name of one Favorite to apply to many elements, instead of favoritesToApply: to the given elements, or without elements to every element of the Favorite's type that matches the filter. The Favorite is read only once. Needs elements or filter.

elements.description: The elements to apply the single favorite to, one execution result each, in the same order. Only with favorite.

filter.description: Server-side element filter for the single favorite. Without elements the favorite is applied to every element of its type that matches it; an element of elements that does not match it gets a failed execution result. Only with favorite.

applySettings.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc.). Geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is never applied - the element stays on its own home story - except that a Window or Door takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included, while keeping its wall, marker and placement. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. A Dimension's text size, text pen and text frame are not changed (tested in Archicad 28): the dimension creation commands take textHeight, textPen and textFrame for them. Default is true.

applyClassifications.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's classifications. Default is true.

applyCategories.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.

applyProperties.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's property values. Default is true.

keepFields.description: Fields of the target element to keep: after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width', 'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column; 'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height', 'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a story. Default: nothing is kept.

example.description: Applies the first Wall Favorite to a new wall with ApplyFavoritesToElements, keeping the wall's height. Needs a Wall Favorite. The wall is created by the script and deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Applies the first Wall Favorite to a new wall with ApplyFavoritesToElements, keeping the wall's height.

Needs a Wall Favorite. The wall is created by the script and deleted at the end.
"""
import aclib

wallFavorites = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetFavoritesByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['favorites']
if not wallFavorites:
    raise SystemExit ('The project has no Wall Favorite.')

wall = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ApplyFavoritesToElements', {
    'favoritesToApply': [{'elementId': wall['elementId'], 'favorite': wallFavorites[0]}],
    'applySettings': True,
    'applyClassifications': True,
    'applyCategories': True,
    'applyProperties': False,
    'keepFields': ['height', 'topOffset', 'relativeTopStory']
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': [wall]})

commands.name: GetPropertyValuesOfElements
commands.description: Returns the property values of the elements for the given property. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With includeAvailability it also tells whether each property is available for the element.

includeAvailability.description: Adds isAvailable to each property value or error, telling whether the property is available for the element (for example by its classification). Default is false.

commands.name: SetPropertyValuesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the property values of elements. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With valueStatus an element's value can also be reset to the default value of the property (Default) or made undefined (UserUndefined, from 1.8.1). With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value now (oldValue) and the value a real run would write (newValue), both as GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives them.

elementPropertyValues.description: A single real value accepts '.' or ',' as the decimal separator, so the value strings GetPropertyValuesOfElements returns can be written back: when both appear the last one is the decimal separator, a separator that appears more than once groups thousands, and a single separator is the decimal one. Unitless real and integer lists accept semicolon-separated numbers; an empty string sets an empty list. Invalid items reject the entire property write.

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementPropertyValues, in the order of the input. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the property values of the element can be read, the value is editable for the element and converts to the property's type) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value now as GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives it (left out when the property is not available or not evaluated for the element), newValue the value that would be written in the same format (left out for valueStatus Default). Archicad can still refuse a value that passes them.

commands.name: GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes

commands.description: Sets built-in property values of attributes, writing the values of each attribute together. Custom properties are refused; set them with SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes. Returns one execution result per value.

attributes.description: The attributes and the built-in property values to set on each.

commands.name: SetPropertyValueOfAttributes
commands.description: Sets one property value on several attributes (for example Building Materials) in one undo step. If the property is not available for any of the given attributes, no attribute is changed.

attributeIds.description: The attributes to set the value on. The property must be available for every one of them.

example.description: Sets one value of a custom text property on every Building Material that has it with SetPropertyValueOfAttributes, then restores the values. Needs Building Materials that have an editable, not expression based, custom text property.
example.code:
"""Sets one value of a custom text property on every Building Material that has it with SetPropertyValueOfAttributes, then restores the values.

Needs Building Materials that have an editable, not expression based, custom text property.
"""
import aclib

buildingMaterials = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes']
attributeIds = [{'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']} for buildingMaterial in buildingMaterials]
definitions = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds})['propertyDefinitionsOfAttributes']
textPropertyIds = [p['propertyId'] for p in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['properties']
                   if p['propertyValueType'] == 'String' and p['propertyCollectionType'] == 'Single' and p['propertyIsEditable'] and not p['isExpressionBased']]
propertyId = next ((p['propertyId'] for d in definitions for p in d.get ('propertyIds', []) if p['propertyId'] in textPropertyIds), None)
if propertyId is None:
    raise SystemExit ('No Building Material has an editable custom text property.')
attributeIds = [a for a, d in zip (attributeIds, definitions) if {'propertyId': propertyId} in d.get ('propertyIds', [])]

def ReadValues ():
    return [values['propertyValues'][0]['propertyValue']['value'] for values in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes', {
        'attributeIds': attributeIds,
        'properties': [{'propertyId': propertyId}]
    })['propertyValuesForAttributes']]

oldValues = ReadValues ()

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetPropertyValueOfAttributes', {
    'propertyId': propertyId,
    'propertyValue': {'value': 'Set by Tapir'},
    'attributeIds': attributeIds
}))
print ('Values after the change:', ReadValues ())

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes', {
    'attributePropertyValues': [{'attributeId': a['attributeId'], 'propertyId': propertyId, 'propertyValue': {'value': v}} for a, v in zip (attributeIds, oldValues)]
})

commands.name: AddPropertyToAttributes

"""Makes a custom property available for the first Building Material with AddPropertyToAttributes, then removes it again.

Needs a custom property that the Building Material does not have yet. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.
"""
import aclib

buildingMaterial = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes'][0]
attributeIds = [{'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']}]
ownPropertyIds = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds})['propertyDefinitionsOfAttributes'][0].get ('propertyIds', [])
customProperties = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['properties']

With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and wouldDelete when the property and every attribute exist.

attributeIds.description: The attributes (for example Building Materials) to make the property unavailable for.

outputSchema.description: The result of the execution: success, with error when it failed. A dry run also answers dryRun, and wouldDelete when the property and every attribute exist.

example.description: Makes a custom property unavailable for the first Building Material with RemovePropertyFromAttributes. The script first makes a property available that the Building Material does not have yet, so the project ends as it was. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.
example.code:
"""Makes a custom property unavailable for the first Building Material with RemovePropertyFromAttributes.

The script first makes a property available that the Building Material does not have yet, so the project
ends as it was. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.
"""
import aclib

buildingMaterial = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes'][0]
attributeIds = [{'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']}]
ownPropertyIds = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds})['propertyDefinitionsOfAttributes'][0].get ('propertyIds', [])
customProperties = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['properties']
propertyId = next ((p['propertyId'] for p in customProperties if {'propertyId': p['propertyId']} not in ownPropertyIds), None)
if propertyId is None:
    raise SystemExit ('No custom property that the Building Material does not have.')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddPropertyToAttributes', {'propertyId': propertyId, 'attributeIds': attributeIds})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RemovePropertyFromAttributes', {'propertyId': propertyId, 'attributeIds': attributeIds}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds, 'properties': [{'propertyId': propertyId}]})

commands.name: ImportPropertiesXml
commands.description: Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed.

xml.description: A Property Manager export (XML) to import.

example.description: Imports a group with one text property from Property Manager XML with ImportPropertiesXml, then deletes them. conflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a property whose name already exists in its group.
example.code:
"""Imports a group with one text property from Property Manager XML with ImportPropertiesXml, then deletes them.

conflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a property whose name already exists in its group.
"""
import aclib

group = 'Tapir Example Import'
xml = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no" ?>
<BuildingInformation>
    <PropertyDefinitionGroups>
        <PropertyDefinitionGroup>
            <Name>{group}</Name>
            <Description/>
            <PropertyDefinitions>
                <PropertyDefinition>
                    <Name>Imported Text</Name>
                    <Description/>
                    <ValueDescriptor Type="SingleValueDescriptor">
                        <ValueType>String</ValueType>
                    </ValueDescriptor>
                    <MeasureType>Default</MeasureType>
                    <DefaultValue>
                        <DefaultValueType>Basic</DefaultValueType>
                        <Variant Type="StringVariant">
                            <Status>Normal</Status>
                            <Value>-</Value>
                        </Variant>
                    </DefaultValue>
                    <ClassificationIDs/>
                </PropertyDefinition>
            </PropertyDefinitions>
        </PropertyDefinitionGroup>
    </PropertyDefinitionGroups>
</BuildingInformation>
'''.format (group = group)

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportPropertiesXml', {'xml': xml, 'conflictPolicy': 'skip'})
aclib.PrintJson (result)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeletePropertyDefinitions', {'propertyIds': [{'propertyId': p} for p in result.get ('created', [])]})
groups = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['propertyGroups']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeletePropertyGroups', {'propertyGroupIds': [{'propertyGroupId': g['propertyGroupId']} for g in groups if g['name'] == group]})

results.description: One item for each value, in the order of the input: whether it is acceptable, or an error if the property was not found.

commands.name: GetPropertyEditability
commands.description: Tells whether the values of the given properties can be modified, and whether the properties are visible, for the given elements. Also tells whether they can be modified in the tool defaults of element types (from Archicad 26) and in the default values of the property definitions themselves. Unknown elements, element types and properties are reported as errors, not as locked properties.

elements.description: Checks whether the value of each property can be modified for these elements, and whether each property is visible for them.

elementTypes.description: Checks whether the value of each property can be modified in the tool default of these element types.

propertyDefinitionDefaults.description: When true, checks whether the default value of each property definition can be modified. This is the default value of the property definition itself, not the tool default of an element type.

outputSchema.description: Only the lists that were asked for are present.

editabilityOfElements.description: Present when elements were given. The order of the outer list is that of the given elements. The order of the inner lists are that of the given properties.

editable.description: Whether the value of the property can be modified for the element. False for example for read-only properties or expressions with cyclic references.

visible.description: Whether the property is visible for the element.

editabilityOfElementTypeDefaults.description: Present when elementTypes were given. The order of the outer list is that of the given element types. The order of the inner lists are that of the given properties.

editable.description: Whether the value of the property can be modified in the tool default of the element type.

editabilityOfPropertyDefinitionDefaults.description: Present when propertyDefinitionDefaults is true. The order is that of the given properties.

editable.description: Whether the default value of the property definition can be modified.

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByClassification', {'classificationItemIds': itemIds}))

commands.name: SetClassificationsOfElements
commands.description: Sets the classifications of elements. In order to set the classification of an element to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's classification in the system now (oldValue) and the one a real run would set (newValue).

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementClassifications, in the order of the input. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the classification item and its system exist, the element's classification in that system can be read) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's classificationId in the system now and newValue the one a real run would set, both as GetClassificationsOfElements gives them (without classificationItemId when the element is or would be unclassified in the system). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them.

example.description: Classifies the first Wall with the first item of the first classification system with SetClassificationsOfElements, then restores its classification. Needs at least one Wall and a classification system with an item.

commands.name: GetClassificationsOfAttributes

Uses the first child of the first item of the first classification system, or that item when it has no child.

commands.name: ImportClassificationsXml
commands.description: Imports a Classification Manager XML export, with the given policies for systems and items that already exist. Returns the systems and items it created and removed.

xml.description: A Classification Manager export (XML) to import.

example.description: Imports a small classification system from Classification Manager XML with ImportClassificationsXml, then deletes it. systemConflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a system whose name already exists.
example.code:
"""Imports a small classification system from Classification Manager XML with ImportClassificationsXml, then deletes it.

systemConflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a system whose name already exists.
"""
import aclib

system = 'Tapir Example Import System'
xml = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no" ?>
<BuildingInformation>
    <Classification>
        <System>
            <Name>{system}</Name>
            <EditionVersion>1</EditionVersion>
            <EditionDate>
                <Year>2026</Year>
                <Month>1</Month>
                <Day>1</Day>
            </EditionDate>
            <Description/>
            <Source/>
            <Items>
                <Item>
                    <ID>10</ID>
                    <Name>Walls</Name>
                    <Description/>
                    <Children>
                        <Item>
                            <ID>10.1</ID>
                            <Name>External walls</Name>
                            <Description/>
                            <Children/>
                        </Item>
                    </Children>
                </Item>
            </Items>
        </System>
    </Classification>
</BuildingInformation>
'''.format (system = system)

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportClassificationsXml', {
    'xml': xml,
    'systemConflictPolicy': 'skip',
    'itemConflictPolicy': 'skip'
}))

systems = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllClassificationSystems')['classificationSystems']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteClassificationSystems', {
    'classificationSystemIds': [{'classificationSystemId': s['classificationSystemId']} for s in systems if s['name'] == system]
})

commands.name: GetClassificationItemVisibility
commands.description: Tells whether the given classification items are visible (offered) for the given elements, element tool defaults and attributes, such as building materials. Non-existing targets and classification items are reported as errors. Visibility does not tell whether the target is classified with the item, and an item can be visible even if its parent item is not.

targets.description: The elements, element tool defaults and attributes to check the classification items for.

elementType.description: The tool default of this element type is checked.

classificationItemVisibilities.description: One entry per target, in the order of the input. A non-existing element or attribute, or an invalid element type, is represented by an error object.

example.description: Tells whether the first item of the first classification system is offered for the first Wall, the Wall tool default and the first Building Material with GetClassificationItemVisibility. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Tells whether the first item of the first classification system is offered for the first Wall, the Wall tool default and the first Building Material with GetClassificationItemVisibility.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
buildingMaterial = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes'][0]
systemId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllClassificationSystems')['classificationSystems'][0]['classificationSystemId']
item = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetAllClassificationsInSystem', {'classificationSystemId': systemId})['classificationItems'][0]['classificationItem']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetClassificationItemVisibility', {
    'targets': [
        {'elementId': walls[0]['elementId']},
        {'elementType': 'Wall'},
        {'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']}
    ],
    'classificationItemIds': [{'classificationItemId': item['classificationItemId']}]
}))

commands.name: GetAttributesByType
commands.description: Returns the details of every attribute of the given type, including the path of the attribute folder holding it (Archicad 26 and newer). commands.name: GetAttributeIndexes
commands.description: Reports for each given attribute type how many attributes there are, the first valid and the highest index in use, and the free indexes between them (for example those of deleted attributes). Available from Archicad 27.

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to report the indexes of.

attributeIndexes.description: One item per requested attribute type, in the order of attributeTypes.

count.description: The number of attributes of the type.

firstIndex.description: The index of the first valid attribute of the type, as Archicad reports it. Left out when the type has no attribute.

lastIndex.description: The highest index in use. Left out when the type has no attribute.

freeIndexes.description: The indexes between firstIndex and lastIndex that no attribute uses, for example those of deleted attributes, in ascending order. Archicad 29 gives a new Layer the lowest free index.

example.description: Prints how the indexes of a few attribute types are used, with GetAttributeIndexes. For each type: the number of attributes, the first valid and the highest index, and how many indexes between them are free (for example those of deleted attributes). Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: GetAttributesFromProject
commands.description: Reads the attributes of the given types from another project or template file without opening it, for example to compare them with the attributes of the open project. Nothing is imported into the open project. The names are the legacy 8-bit names, so non-ASCII characters may not come through. Archicad does not read Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem attributes from a file that is not open: these types get an error item instead of an empty list. Available from Archicad 27.

projectFilePath.description: The absolute path of the project or template file (for example .pln or .tpl) to read the attributes from.

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to read. Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem cannot be read from a file that is not open; they get an error item.

example.description: Reads the line types and fills of another project or template file with GetAttributesFromProject, without opening it. Set the TAPIR_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE environment variable to the absolute path of a .pln or .tpl file. Nothing is imported into the open project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: DeleteAttributes
commands.description: Deletes the given attributes. Returns an execution result for each input item. With dryRun true nothing is deleted: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks made before deleting (valid attribute type, attribute exists) gets wouldDelete.

executionResults.description: One result for each input attribute, in the order of the input. On a dry run an attribute that passes the checks made before deleting (valid attributeType, attribute found) gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete an attribute that passes them.

example.description: Creates a temporary Layer and deletes it again with DeleteAttributes, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.

commands.name: ImportAttributesFromProject
commands.description: Imports Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and LayerCombination attributes from another project or template file into the open project, with their complete definition (symbol and percent fills included), like Append or Overwrite by name in Archicad's Attribute Manager. The lines and fills a composite or profile uses are matched by name; its building materials and surfaces, and the layers of a layer combination, keep their index only with referencesByIndex, since Archicad does not read these types from a closed file. An attribute with a reference that cannot be mapped is not imported. A new attribute gets a new guid: Archicad does not hand out the guids stored in the source file. An attribute whose name already exists is skipped, or overwritten in place with overwriteExisting. dryRun reports what would happen without changing anything. The names are the legacy 8-bit names of the source file. Available from Archicad 27.

projectFilePath.description: The absolute path of the project or template file (for example .pln or .tpl) to import the attributes from.

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to import, in this order. Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and LayerCombination can be imported. Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem fail with an error item: Archicad does not read them from a closed file. A Composite, Profile or LayerCombination refers to other attributes, see referencesByIndex; list Line and Fill before them to import the lines and fills they use.

attributeNames.description: Import only the attributes with these names. All attributes of the given types are imported when it is omitted.

overwriteExisting.description: What happens to an attribute whose name already exists in the open project. false (default): it is skipped and the existing attribute is kept. true: the existing attribute is overwritten with the imported definition and keeps its index and guid.

dryRun.description: If true, nothing is changed: the response reports what an import would do.

referencesByIndex.description: How the BuildingMaterial, Surface and Layer references of an imported Composite, Profile or LayerCombination are mapped. Archicad does not read these attributes from a closed file, so their names are unknown and they cannot be matched by name. false (default): an attribute with such a reference is not imported (result failed). true: the reference keeps its index and refers to the attribute with that index in the open project, which is right only when both files share these attributes at the same indexes, for example because they come from the same template. Line and Fill references are always matched by name.

attributesByType.description: One item per requested attribute type, in the order of attributeTypes.

attributes.description: One item per imported (or, with dryRun, importable) attribute of the source file.

name.description: The name of the attribute in the source file.

sourceIndex.description: The index of the attribute in the source file. Archicad hands out a new guid for the attributes of another file on every read, so they are identified by name and index.

result.description: created: new in the open project. overwritten: an attribute of the same name was overwritten. skipped: an attribute of the same name exists and overwriteExisting is false. failed: see error, for example a reference that cannot be mapped. With dryRun the result is what an import would do.

attributeId.description: The attribute in the open project. Missing when it was not created (failed, or created with dryRun).

references.description: For a Composite, Profile or LayerCombination that is created or overwritten (or would be, with dryRun): the attributes it refers to, each once, and how they were mapped to the open project.

attributeType.description: The type of the attribute referred to.

sourceIndex.description: Its index in the source file.

sourceName.description: Its name in the source file. Only for Line and Fill: Archicad does not read the other types from a closed file.

mappedBy.description: name: an attribute of the open project with the same name. index: the attribute of the open project with the same index (referencesByIndex). none: not mapped, so the attribute was not imported.

attributeId.description: The attribute of the open project referred to after the import. Missing when not mapped, or when it is created by the same dry run.

example.description: Imports the line types of another project or template file with ImportAttributesFromProject, first as a dry run. Set the TAPIR_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE environment variable to the absolute path of a .pln or .tpl file. Line types whose name already exists in the open project are kept as they are; the others are added. The dry run also shows how the composites of the file would map their line types and building materials. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Imports the line types of another project or template file with ImportAttributesFromProject, first as a dry run.

Set the TAPIR_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE environment variable to the absolute path of a .pln or .tpl file.
Line types whose name already exists in the open project are kept as they are; the others are added.
The dry run also shows how the composites of the file would map their line types and building materials.
Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import os
import aclib

projectFilePath = os.environ.get ('TAPIR_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE', '')
if not os.path.isfile (projectFilePath):
    raise SystemExit ('Set TAPIR_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE to the path of a project or template file.')

parameters = {
    'projectFilePath': projectFilePath,
    'attributeTypes': ['Line'],
    'overwriteExisting': False
}

# Building materials keep their index only with referencesByIndex, so without it a composite that
# uses one is reported as failed, with its references.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportAttributesFromProject', dict (parameters, attributeTypes = ['Line', 'Composite'], dryRun = True)))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportAttributesFromProject', parameters))

commands.name: RenameAttributeFolders
commands.description: Renames attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, to the given new names. The root folder cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 26.

commands.name: MoveAttributesAndFolders
commands.description: Moves attributes and attribute folders (with their contents) into the target folder, which must be of the same attribute type; an empty target path is the root folder. Returns one execution result per attribute and per folder; an attribute or folder that is already directly in the target folder counts as moved. Available from Archicad 26.

attributeIds.description: The attributes to move. They must have the attribute type of the target folder.

attributeFolders.description: The folders to move, with their contents. They must have the attribute type of the target folder.

targetFolder.description: The folder to move the attributes and folders into. An empty path is the root folder.

attributeExecutionResults.description: One result per item of attributeIds, in the same order.

commands.name: ReindexLayers
commands.description: Moves layers to new indices. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so each layer is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary layers, which are deleted again), gets the old layer's state in every layer combination, and then every element of the old layer is moved to it, in the floor plan and in every view and layout database, with the tool defaults on that layer. Only when the old layer is empty everywhere is it deleted, and the new layer gets its name, flags and folder. If an element cannot be moved (it is locked, not reserved in Teamwork, or comes from a hotlinked module), that layer is left as it was. The new layer has a new attribute id; Favorites that use the layer are not updated. Archicad keeps the shown, locked and wireframe state of a layer per open window: the new layer gets the old one's state in the current window and in every layer combination, and starts shown and unlocked in the other open windows. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show of the layer come back on the new layer when those views are rebuilt (listed as viewsToRebuild). dryRun lists the elements and tool defaults on each layer without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Available from Archicad 27.

layers.description: The layers to move to a new index, handled in the given order.

attributeId.description: The layer to move.

newIndex.description: The index the layer gets. It must not be used by another layer. Index 1 (the Archicad Layer) cannot be used or moved.

dryRun.description: Only list what would change (the elements on each layer, the tools whose default layer it is, the elements that block the move) without changing anything. The default is false.

maxPlaceholders.description: Every free index below newIndex is filled with a temporary layer first (about 20 ms each), so a newIndex far above the highest index in use takes long. A layer that needs more temporary layers than this is not moved. The default is 1000.

layers.description: One item per requested layer, in the same order.

attributeId.description: The layer at its new index. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute in place, so this is a new attribute with a new id; with dryRun it is the layer's current id.

elements.description: The elements on the layer, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout. Moved to the new layer unless dryRun is true. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show are not listed (see viewsToRebuild).

blockedElements.description: Only with dryRun: elements on the layer that cannot be moved, because they come from a hotlinked module. Without dryRun such a layer is not moved.

toolDefaults.description: The element types whose tool default is on this layer. They are set to the new layer unless dryRun is true.

placeholders.description: The number of temporary layers needed for the free indices below newIndex.

warnings.description: What did not work after the layer was moved: its name and flags, or the move into its attribute folder.

viewsToRebuild.description: The sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents that show elements of the layer. The model elements they show are deleted with the old layer and come back on the new layer when the view is rebuilt: Archicad does that when the view is opened, unless it is set to be rebuilt manually. To rebuild one at once, call ChangeWindow with its databaseId and then RebuildCurrentDatabase.

example.description: Creates a temporary Layer and moves it to the next free index with ReindexLayers, first as a dry run. The layer gets a new attribute id at its new index; the script deletes it at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a temporary Layer and moves it to the next free index with ReindexLayers, first as a dry run.

The layer gets a new attribute id at its new index; the script deletes it at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

name = 'Tapir Example Layer To Reindex'
layerId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLayers', {'layerDataArray': [{'name': name}]})['attributeIds'][0]
if 'error' in layerId:
    raise SystemExit ('Could not create the layer: ' + layerId['error']['message'])

layers = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Layer'})['attributes']
newIndex = int (max (layer['index'] for layer in layers)) + 1

parameters = {'layers': [{'attributeId': layerId['attributeId'], 'newIndex': newIndex}]}
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReindexLayers', dict (parameters, dryRun = True)))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReindexLayers', parameters))

layers = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Layer'})['attributes']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteAttributes', {
    'attributesToDelete': [{'attributeType': 'Layer', 'attributeId': {'attributeId': layer['attributeId']}} for layer in layers if layer['name'] == name]
})

commands.name: ReindexAttributes
commands.description: Moves fills, line types, surfaces, building materials and zone categories to new indices, the way ReindexLayers moves layers. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so the attribute is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary attributes, which are deleted again) and every reference to the old index is rewritten to the new one: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, the memo data of roofs, slabs, meshes, morphs, curtain walls, beams, columns, stairs and interior elevations, the tool defaults, the Favorites (with their sub-elements: a curtain wall's frame and panel classes, a stair's structures), the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Only then is the old attribute deleted. The new attribute has a new attribute id (Archicad does not keep a given id); its name, definition and attribute folder are the old ones. Elements on a hidden or locked layer cannot be changed, so their layers are shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards (in the current window, as Archicad keeps these flags per window). If an element still cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not moved. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed; their module file has to be reindexed on its own. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the old index (Archicad does not take them from ACAPI_Favorite_Change, so such Favorites are left as they are and named in the warnings). dryRun lists every reference without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Pens, layers (see ReindexLayers) and the other attribute types are not supported. Available from Archicad 27.

attributeType.description: The type of the attributes to move. Layers are moved by ReindexLayers; pens and the other attribute types cannot be moved.

attributes.description: The attributes to move to a new index, handled in the given order.

attributeId.description: The attribute to move.

newIndex.description: The index the attribute gets. It must not be used by another attribute of the type.

dryRun.description: Only list every reference to each attribute (elements, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes, graphic override rules, elements from hotlinked modules) without changing anything. The default is false.

maxPlaceholders.description: Every free index below newIndex is filled with a temporary attribute first, so a newIndex far above the highest index in use takes long. An attribute that needs more temporary attributes than this is not moved. The default is 1000.

attributes.description: One item per requested attribute, in the same order.

attributeId.description: The attribute at its new index. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute in place, so this is a new attribute with a new id; with dryRun it is the attribute's current id.

placeholders.description: The number of temporary attributes needed for the free indices below newIndex.

elements.description: The elements that refer to the attribute, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout: in their own fields, their library part parameters or their memo data (side surfaces, roof levels, morph faces, cutting planes). Rewritten to the new index unless dryRun is true.

hotlinkElements.description: Elements from hotlinked modules that refer to the attribute. They cannot be changed and keep the old index until their module file is reindexed.

toolDefaults.description: The element types whose tool default refers to the attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

favorites.description: The names of the Favorites that refer to the attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

attributes.description: The other attributes that refer to the attribute: composites (skins and separators), building materials (cut fill, cut surface), surfaces (hatching fill), MEP systems (fill) and profiles (skins and edges). Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

overrideRules.description: The names of the graphic override rules that refer to the attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

layersShown.description: The hidden or locked layers of the elements that were shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards. Not present with dryRun.

warnings.description: What keeps the old index or did not work after the attribute was moved: elements from hotlinked modules, a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule that could not be written, the name or the attribute folder.

example.description: Creates a temporary Line type and moves it to the next free index with ReindexAttributes, first as a dry run. The line type gets a new attribute id at its new index; the script deletes it at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a temporary Line type and moves it to the next free index with ReindexAttributes, first as a dry run.

The line type gets a new attribute id at its new index; the script deletes it at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

name = 'Tapir Example Line To Reindex'
lineId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLines', {'lineDataArray': [{'name': name}]})['attributeIds'][0]
if 'error' in lineId:
    raise SystemExit ('Could not create the line type: ' + lineId['error']['message'])

lines = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Line'})['attributes']
newIndex = int (max (line['index'] for line in lines)) + 1

parameters = {
    'attributeType': 'Line',
    'attributes': [{'attributeId': lineId['attributeId'], 'newIndex': newIndex}]
}
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReindexAttributes', dict (parameters, dryRun = True)))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReindexAttributes', parameters))

lines = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Line'})['attributes']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteAttributes', {
    'attributesToDelete': [{'attributeType': 'Line', 'attributeId': {'attributeId': line['attributeId']}} for line in lines if line['name'] == name]
})

commands.name: DeleteAndReplaceAttributes
commands.description: Deletes fills, line types, surfaces or building materials and replaces each by another attribute of the same type wherever it was used, like Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager. Every reference is rewritten to the replacement, the way ReindexAttributes rewrites them: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, their memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Elements on a hidden or locked layer are changed too: their layers are shown and unlocked for the change and put back afterwards (in the current window). If an element cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not deleted. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the deleted attribute (named in the warnings). If a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule cannot be rewritten to the replacement, it keeps a copy of the deleted attribute with its name and a new attribute id, named in the warnings. The whole call is one undo step. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks gets wouldDelete and lists every reference a real run would rewrite (elements, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes, graphic override rules, elements from hotlinked modules). Available from Archicad 27.

attributeType.description: The type of the attributes to delete and of their replacements.

attributes.description: The attributes to delete, each with the attribute that takes its place, handled in the given order.

attributeId.description: The attribute to delete.

replacementAttributeId.description: The attribute of the same type that replaces it wherever it is used. It must be another attribute than the one to delete.

attributes.description: One item per requested attribute, in the same order.

attributeId.description: The deleted attribute (with dryRun, the attribute that would be deleted).

replacementAttributeId.description: The attribute that took its place.

wouldDelete.description: Only on a dry run: the attribute and its replacement passed the checks, and a real run would delete the attribute and rewrite the references listed here to the replacement.

elements.description: The elements that referred to the deleted attribute, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout: in their own fields, their library part parameters or their memo data (side surfaces, roof levels, morph faces, cutting planes). They refer to the replacement now, unless dryRun is true.

hotlinkElements.description: Elements from hotlinked modules that refer to the deleted attribute. They cannot be changed; replace the attribute in their module file.

toolDefaults.description: The element types whose tool default referred to the deleted attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

favorites.description: The names of the Favorites that referred to the deleted attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

attributes.description: The other attributes that referred to the deleted attribute: composites (skins and separators), building materials (cut fill, cut surface), surfaces (hatching fill), MEP systems (fill) and profiles (skins and edges). Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

overrideRules.description: The names of the graphic override rules that referred to the deleted attribute. Rewritten unless dryRun is true.

layersShown.description: The hidden or locked layers of the elements that were shown and unlocked for the change and put back afterwards. Not present with dryRun.

warnings.description: What still refers to the deleted attribute: elements from hotlinked modules, a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule that could not be written. What could not be rewritten to the replacement keeps a copy of the deleted attribute, whose attribute id the last warning names.

example.description: Creates two temporary Line types and deletes the first with DeleteAndReplaceAttributes, replaced by the second, first as a dry run. The script deletes the second line type at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: GetUnusedAttributes
commands.description: Lists the unused layers, fills, surfaces, building materials, composites, profiles, line types, pen tables and zone categories (index, id and name), for the given types or all of them. The Archicad API has no function that tells which attributes are unused (only how many per type), so every reference is collected: the elements of the floor plan and of every view and layout (hotlinked ones too), with their library part parameters and memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules, the way ReindexAttributes finds them; for layers the layer of each element, tool default and Favorite; for composites and profiles the walls, slabs, roofs, shells, column and beam segments whose structure type uses them; for pen tables the current pen table and the drawings set to a pen table of their own. An attribute that only an unused attribute refers to counts as used. Indices typed into GDL scripts and the pen tables saved with views are not found. Each type also reports Archicad's own count of the attributes in use (archicadUsedCount, see GetUsedAttributes), so a difference shows. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.

types.description: The attribute types to check. All of them when omitted.

attributeTypes.description: One item per checked attribute type, in the order layer, fill, surface, buildingMaterial, composite, profile, lineType, penTable, zoneCategory.

unusedAttributes.description: The attributes of this type that no reference found by the command points at.

attributeCount.description: The number of attributes of this type in the project.

archicadUsedCount.description: The number of attributes of this type in use as Archicad itself counts them, from the usedAttributes JSON query (see GetUsedAttributes). When it differs from usedCount, Archicad counts references this command does not see, or the other way round, so check the list before deleting. Missing when Archicad's report does not name the type.

archicadReport.description: Archicad's usedAttributes report as it came, e.g. 'Layer: 16, LineType: 9, Fill: 17'. Missing when the query failed.

warnings.description: What could not be checked. Missing when everything was checked.

example.description: Lists the unused fills, line types and surfaces of the project with GetUnusedAttributes, and how many of each type Archicad itself counts as used. Leave out 'types' to check every attribute type. Nothing is changed. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Lists the unused fills, line types and surfaces of the project with GetUnusedAttributes, and how many of each type Archicad itself counts as used.

Leave out 'types' to check every attribute type. Nothing is changed. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetUnusedAttributes', {'types': ['fill', 'lineType', 'surface']})
aclib.PrintJson (result)

for attributeType in result['attributeTypes']:
    names = [attribute['name'] for attribute in attributeType['unusedAttributes']]
    print (f"{attributeType['type']}: {len (names)} of {attributeType['attributeCount']} unused, Archicad counts {attributeType.get ('archicadUsedCount', '?')} as used")

commands.name: GetMissingAttributes
commands.description: Lists the references of placed elements to layers, fills, surfaces, building materials, composites, profiles, line types, pen tables and zone categories that do not exist in the project, for the given types or all of them, and of the tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options combinations and attributes: the structured counterpart of the missing attributes report of Archicad's GDL palette. Every element of the floor plan and of every view and layout (hotlinked ones too) is checked, and so is every tool default and Favorite (with its sub-elements): its layer, its attribute fields and memo data as ReindexAttributes finds them, its composite or profile when its structure type uses one, a drawing's own pen table, and its library part parameters of attribute types; of every graphic override rule the line type, fill and surface it overrides with; of every Model View Options combination the surfaces and line types of the stair and railing schemes and the library part settings' GDL parameters of attribute types; of every composite the building materials of its skins and the line types of its separators, of every building material its cut fill and cut surface, of every surface the fill of its vectorial hatching, of every MEP system its fill, center line type and surfaces, and of every profile the building material, surface or fill of each skin and its contour, cut end and edge line types. The sources input limits the check to elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options or attributes. Each item names the source; for an element the element (and the element it is part of, for a curtain wall frame, a column segment, ...) and the story or view it sits on, for a tool default the tool, for a Favorite its name and tool, for a graphic override rule its guid and name, for a Model View Options combination its guid and name (and the library part option set), for an attribute its type, guid and name; then the attribute type, the missing index and the field or GDL parameter that holds it. Index 0 counts as no attribute. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.

attributeTypes.description: The attribute types to check. All of them when omitted.

sources.description: What to check: the placed elements (element), the tool default settings (toolDefault), the Favorites (favorite), the graphic override rules (overrideRule), the Model View Options combinations (modelViewOption) and the attributes that refer to other attributes (attribute: composites, building materials, surfaces, MEP systems and profiles). All of them when omitted.

missingAttributes.description: One item per reference to an attribute index that has no attribute in the project: first the placed elements in the order they were found (the floor plan first, then the views and layouts), then the tool defaults, then the Favorites, then the graphic override rules, then the Model View Options combinations, then the attributes that refer to other attributes.

source.description: What refers to the missing attribute: a placed element, the default settings of a tool, a Favorite, a graphic override rule, a Model View Options combination, or another attribute.

elementId.description: The placed element. Only for source element.

elementType.description: The element's type, as GetElementsByType names it: for a tool default or a Favorite the type of its tool. Missing for a graphic override rule, a Model View Options combination and an attribute.

overrideRuleId.description: The graphic override rule. Only for source overrideRule.

overrideRuleName.description: The name of the graphic override rule. Only for source overrideRule.

modelViewOptionId.description: The Model View Options combination, the id GetModelViewOptionDetails returns. Only for source modelViewOption.

modelViewOptionName.description: The name of the Model View Options combination. Only for source modelViewOption.

gdlOptionsName.description: When the reference is a GDL parameter of the library part settings of a Model View Options combination, the name of that option set (the gdlOptions name GetModelViewOptionDetails returns). Missing otherwise.

ownerAttributeType.description: The type of the attribute that refers to the missing one. Only for source attribute.

ownerAttributeId.description: The attribute that refers to the missing one. Only for source attribute.

ownerAttributeName.description: The name of that attribute. Only for source attribute.

favoriteName.description: The name of the Favorite. Only for source favorite.

subElementType.description: When the reference is in a sub-element the Favorite keeps apart (e.g. a stair's structure), the type of that sub-element. Missing otherwise.

parentElementId.description: The element this one is part of (the curtain wall of a frame, the column of a segment, ...). Missing for an element that is not part of another one.

databaseId.description: The database the element is in, the same id GetDatabases returns. Only for source element.

databaseType.description: The type of that database, e.g. FloorPlan, Worksheet, Details, Section, Layout. Only for source element.

storyIndex.description: The element's home story. Only for elements of the floor plan.

storyName.description: The name of that story. Only for elements of the floor plan.

databaseName.description: The name of the view or layout (e.g. the worksheet) the element is in. Missing for the floor plan.

databaseReference.description: The reference id of that view or layout. Missing when it has none.

inHotlinkedModule.description: True when the element comes from a hotlinked module: it has to be fixed in the module's file. Missing otherwise.

index.description: The attribute index the element, tool default, Favorite, graphic override rule, Model View Options combination or attribute refers to, which no attribute of attributeType has.

field.description: The element's setting that holds the index, named as in the Archicad API (e.g. layer, contLtype, cWallFrameDefaults.material); for a graphic override rule lineType, fillOverride or surfaceOverride; for a Model View Options combination the field as GetModelViewOptionDetails names it (e.g. stair.stairSchemeSurfaceIndex); for an attribute the field as GetComposites, GetBuildingMaterials, GetSurfaces, GetMEPSystems or GetProfiles names it (e.g. skins[0].buildingMaterialId, cutFillIndex). Missing when gdlParameter is given.

gdlParameter.description: The library part parameter that holds the index, with the cell for an array parameter (e.g. gs_frame_mat, matArray[2][1]). Missing when field is given.

checkedElementCount.description: The number of placed elements checked; 0 when the elements were not checked.

checkedToolDefaultCount.description: The number of tool defaults checked. Missing when the tool defaults were not checked.

checkedFavoriteCount.description: The number of Favorites checked. Missing when the Favorites were not checked.

checkedOverrideRuleCount.description: The number of graphic override rules checked. Missing when the rules were not checked or could not be listed.

checkedModelViewOptionCount.description: The number of Model View Options combinations checked. Missing when they were not checked.

checkedAttributeCount.description: The number of composites, building materials, surfaces, MEP systems and profiles checked for references to other attributes. Missing when they were not checked.

warnings.description: What could not be checked. Missing when everything was checked.

example.description: Lists the references of placed elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options and attributes to attributes that are not in the project with GetMissingAttributes, one line per reference, like the missing attributes report of the GDL palette. Leave out 'attributeTypes' to check every attribute type, and 'sources' to check elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options and the attributes that refer to other attributes (composites, building materials, surfaces, MEP systems, profiles). Nothing is changed. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Lists the references of placed elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options and attributes to attributes that are not in the project with GetMissingAttributes, one line per reference, like the missing attributes report of the GDL palette.

Leave out 'attributeTypes' to check every attribute type, and 'sources' to check elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options and the attributes that refer to other attributes (composites, building materials, surfaces, MEP systems, profiles). Nothing is changed. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMissingAttributes', {})
aclib.PrintJson (result)

print (f"{len (result['missingAttributes'])} missing references in {result['checkedElementCount']} elements, "
       f"{result.get ('checkedToolDefaultCount', 0)} tool defaults, {result.get ('checkedFavoriteCount', 0)} Favorites, "
       f"{result.get ('checkedOverrideRuleCount', 0)} graphic override rules, "
       f"{result.get ('checkedModelViewOptionCount', 0)} Model View Options combinations "
       f"and {result.get ('checkedAttributeCount', 0)} attributes")
for missing in result['missingAttributes']:
    usedBy = missing.get ('field') or missing.get ('gdlParameter')
    if missing['source'] == 'element':
        where = missing.get ('storyName') or missing.get ('databaseName') or missing['databaseType']
        what = f"{missing['elementType']} {missing['elementId']['guid']} | {where}"
    elif missing['source'] == 'favorite':
        what = f"Favorite '{missing['favoriteName']}' ({missing['elementType']})"
    elif missing['source'] == 'overrideRule':
        what = f"Graphic override rule '{missing['overrideRuleName']}'"
    elif missing['source'] == 'modelViewOption':
        what = f"Model View Options '{missing['modelViewOptionName']}'"
        if 'gdlOptionsName' in missing:
            what += f" ({missing['gdlOptionsName']})"
    elif missing['source'] == 'attribute':
        what = f"{missing['ownerAttributeType']} '{missing['ownerAttributeName']}'"
    else:
        what = f"Tool default of {missing['elementType']}"
    print (f"{what} | {missing['attributeType']} {missing['index']} ({usedBy})")

commands.name: CreateLayers
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Layer attributes based on the given parameters.

layerDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Layers.

items.description: Data to create a Layer.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Layer to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Layer to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Layer with the given name will be overwritten.

intersectionGroupNr.description: Intersection group. Elements on layers having the same group will be intersected.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Layer if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

example.description: Creates a locked Layer in intersection group 2 with CreateLayers. Overwrites the layer of the same name when the script is run again.
example.code:
"""Creates a locked Layer in intersection group 2 with CreateLayers.

Overwrites the layer of the same name when the script is run again.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLayers', {
    'layerDataArray': [{
        'name': 'Tapir Example Layer',
        'isHidden': False,
        'isLocked': True,
        'isWireframe': False,
        'intersectionGroupNr': 2
    }],
    'overwriteExisting': True
}))

commands.name: CreateLayerCombinations
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Layer Combination attributes based on the given parameters.

layerCombinationDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Layer Combinations.

items.description: Data to create a Layer Combination.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Layer Combination to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Layer Combination to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Layer Combination with the given name will be overwritten.

layers.description: Layer states to set. Layers not listed keep their current state when overwriting an existing Layer Combination (or get the default visible/unlocked state for a new one), so this can be omitted to e.g. only rename an existing Layer Combination.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Layer Combination if exists with the same guid/index/name. The default is false.

example.description: Creates a Layer Combination that shows and unlocks every layer with CreateLayerCombinations. Overwrites the layer combination of the same name when the script is run again.

commands.name: CreateLines
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Line attributes based on the given parameters.

lineDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Lines.

items.description: Data to create a Line.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Line to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Line to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Line with the given name will be overwritten.

scaleWithPlan.description: If true, the line type parameters are defined in meters at the given defineScale and scale on printout with the actual plan scale. If false (default), the parameters are fixed values in millimeters as the line will appear on the printout.

defineScale.description: The floor plan scale the line type is defined with. Only used if scaleWithPlan is true.

lineType.description: Solid, Dashed, or Symbol. Defaults to Solid.

period.description: The length of one period (Dashed and Symbol line types).

height.description: The height of the symbol line (Symbol line type only).

dashItems.description: Dash-gap pairs describing one period (Dashed line type only).

lineItems.description: Symbol items describing one period (Symbol line type only).

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Line if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

example.description: Creates a dashed Line type (3 mm dash, 1.5 mm gap on the printout) with CreateLines. Overwrites the line type of the same name when the script is run again.
example.code:
"""Creates a dashed Line type (3 mm dash, 1.5 mm gap on the printout) with CreateLines.

Overwrites the line type of the same name when the script is run again.

commands.name: CreateProfiles
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters.

profileDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Profiles.

items.description: Data to create or modify a Profile. Its geometry (the cross-section shape) comes from sourceAttributeId (an existing Profile's geometry, copied), from newSkins (AC27+ only, caller-supplied polygon geometry), or both combined. When creating a brand-new Profile (overwriteExisting false, or true but no existing match), at least one of the two must be given. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, both are optional - the existing Profile's own current geometry is preserved by default (e.g. to change only wallType, or to add newSkins on top of the unchanged existing shape). skinOverrides and newSkins' edgeOverrides target skins/edges by the identifiers/indices GetProfiles reports.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Profile with the given name will be overwritten.

sourceAttributeId.description: Identifier of an existing Profile whose geometry (cross-section shape) will be copied as the starting point. Optional if newSkins is given: omit it to build the Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins instead of copying anything (AC27+ only).

wallType.description: Profile available for walls. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

beamType.description: Profile available for beams. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

coluType.description: Profile available for columns. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

handrailType.description: Profile available for handrails. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

otherGDLObjectType.description: Profile available for other GDL based objects. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

skinOverrides.description: Modifications to apply to specific skins of the copied geometry, e.g. to change a skin's building material without rebuilding the profile's shape. Each skinId comes from a prior GetProfiles call's skins[].skinId on the source Profile (or, when overwriteExisting is true, on the Profile being overwritten).

skinId.description: Identifies which skin to modify, from GetProfiles' skins[].skinId.

edgeOverrides.description: Modifications to specific edges of this skin, targeted by their position (0-based) in GetProfiles' skins[].edges.

moveVertices.description: Moves vertices of the copied (or, when overwriting, the preserved existing) geometry in place, e.g. to change the height of a wall profile by moving its top band, without rebuilding its skins: the skins keep their skinIds, edges and edge settings, so the profileModifiers, the stretch zones and every edge flag are kept. Applied in order, after skinOverrides and before newSkins. Hotspots and fixed modifier anchors inside the region are moved too, and so is a stretch zone limit inside it: a vertical stretch zone limit (a height) when the region has no xMin/xMax, a horizontal one when it has no yMin/yMax.

region.description: Selects the vertices to move: those with xMin <= x <= xMax and yMin <= y <= yMax, in the coordinates GetProfiles reports in skins[].outlineCoords. Each omitted bound leaves that side open, so { "yMin": 2.5 } selects every vertex at or above 2.5. Omit region to move every vertex.

vector.description: The displacement of the selected vertices.

skinIds.description: Moves only the vertices of these skins (GetProfiles' skins[].skinId). Omit to move the vertices of every skin.

newSkins.description: AC27+ only. Adds brand-new skins built from caller-supplied polygon geometry, instead of (or in addition to) whatever was copied from sourceAttributeId. Combine with sourceAttributeId to add skins to a copied Profile, or omit sourceAttributeId to build a Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins.

replaceSkins.description: AC27+ only. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, discard every one of its existing skins (and any sourceAttributeId geometry given alongside it) before applying newSkins, instead of adding newSkins on top of the preserved existing geometry. Use this to fully replace a Profile's cross-section with a caller-authored shape while keeping its guid and scalar fields (wallType etc.) - e.g. to sync a Profile's geometry from another project, where sourceAttributeId can't be used because it only resolves within the same file. Also discards any existing profileModifiers, since those are tied to the specific geometry being replaced. Ignored when creating a brand-new Profile (there is nothing to discard yet).

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Profile if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

example.description: Creates a Profile as a copy of the first Profile of the project, usable for walls and beams, with CreateProfiles. Overwrites the Profile of the same name when the script is run again.
