commands.name: SetUserDataOfAttributes
commands.description: Stores string values under keys in the user data of attributes, for scripts to keep their own state on an attribute. The given pairs are merged into what each attribute already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it.

pairs.description: The key-value pairs to store on each attribute. A key the attribute already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

executionResults.description: One result per attribute, in the input order.

example.description: Stores a key-value pair on the first Layer with SetUserDataOfAttributes, reads it back, then removes the key. Undo does not revert user data changes.
example.code:
"""Stores a key-value pair on the first Layer with SetUserDataOfAttributes, reads it back, then removes the key.

Undo does not revert user data changes.
"""
import aclib

layer = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'Layer'})['attributes'][0]
attributeIds = [{'attributeId': layer['attributeId']}]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetUserDataOfAttributes', {
    'attributeIds': attributeIds,
    'pairs': [{'key': 'tapirExample.note', 'value': 'Checked by a Tapir example'}]
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetUserDataOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetUserDataOfAttributes', {
    'attributeIds': attributeIds,
    'keysToDelete': ['tapirExample.note']
}))

commands.name: DeleteUserDataOfAttributes
commands.description: Removes the user data of attributes, every key at once. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it. With dryRun true nothing is removed: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that exists gets wouldDelete.

executionResults.description: One result per attribute, in the input order. On a dry run an attribute that exists gets wouldDelete.

example.description: Creates a temporary Layer with user data and removes all its user data with DeleteUserDataOfAttributes. DeleteUserDataOfAttributes removes every key, also those of other scripts, and Undo does not revert it, so the script works on a layer it creates and deletes.

"""Creates a temporary Layer with user data and removes all its user data with DeleteUserDataOfAttributes.

DeleteUserDataOfAttributes removes every key, also those of other scripts, and Undo does not revert it,
so the script works on a layer it creates and deletes.
"""
import aclib

layerId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLayers', {'layerDataArray': [{'name': 'Tapir Example User Data Layer'}]})['attributeIds'][0]

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetUserDataOfAttributes', {
    'attributeIds': [layerId],
    'pairs': [{'key': 'tapirExample.note', 'value': 'To be deleted'}]
})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteUserDataOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': [layerId]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetUserDataOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': [layerId]})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteAttributes', {'attributesToDelete': [{'attributeType': 'Layer', 'attributeId': layerId}]})

commands.name: IFCFileOperation
commands.description: Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use, a merge the story the IFC file's first storey is placed on. With overwrite false a save refuses to replace an existing file.

method.description: The file operation method to use.

ifcFilePath.description: The target IFC file to use. The save method overwrites an existing file, unless overwrite is false.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. Only for the save method: false refuses to save when a file already exists at ifcFilePath, and writes nothing.

fileType.description: The type of the IFC file. The default is 'ifc'.

translatorName.description: Only for the save method: the name of the IFC export translator to save with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them. Without it the save runs with the translator Archicad would offer in its own Save dialog. Needs a fileType of ifc or ifczip (ifc or ifcxml on Archicad 25 and 26).

elementsToExport.description: Only for the save method, and only together with translatorName. The default is VisibleElementsOnAllStories.

storyIndex.description: Only for the merge method: the story the first storey of the IFC file is placed on, the IFC's other storeys follow on the stories above it. Without it Archicad uses the active story of the floor plan. The active story and the current window are restored after the merge. See GetStories for the valid story indices.

example.description: Saves the project as an IFC file with IFCFileOperation, using the first IFC export translator of the project. The file is written into a new temporary folder. The open and merge methods take the same ifcFilePath; open replaces the open project.
example.code:
"""Saves the project as an IFC file with IFCFileOperation, using the first IFC export translator of the project.

The file is written into a new temporary folder. The open and merge methods take the same ifcFilePath; open replaces
the open project.
"""
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

translators = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCExportTranslators')['translators']
ifcFilePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'Project.ifc')

parameters = {
    'method': 'save',
    'ifcFilePath': ifcFilePath,
    'fileType': 'ifc'
}
if translators:
    parameters['translatorName'] = translators[0]['name']
    parameters['elementsToExport'] = 'EntireProject'

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('IFCFileOperation', parameters))
print ('IFC file saved to', ifcFilePath)

commands.name: AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary
commands.description: Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

overwriteExisting.description: Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is deleted first, so the newly added file replaces the loaded library part. By default false: the existing loaded part stays in use. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

example.description: Adds a small PNG file to the embedded library with AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary. The image is written to a temporary folder first and deleted from the embedded library at the end (the deletion requires Archicad 27 or later).
example.code:
"""Adds a small PNG file to the embedded library with AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.

The image is written to a temporary folder first and deleted from the embedded library at the end
(the deletion requires Archicad 27 or later).
"""
import base64
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

PNG_1X1 = base64.b64decode ('iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==')
outputPath = 'TapirExamples/tapir_example.png'

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory () as tempDir:
    inputPath = os.path.join (tempDir, 'tapir_example.png')
    with open (inputPath, 'wb') as pngFile:
        pngFile.write (PNG_1X1)

    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary', {
        'files': [{'inputPath': inputPath, 'outputPath': outputPath, 'type': 'Pict'}],
        'overwriteExisting': True
    }))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems', {'embeddedLibraryItems': [{'path': outputPath}]})

commands.name: DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems
commands.description: Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27.

embeddedLibraryItems.description: A list of embedded library items to delete.

example.description: Adds a small PNG file to the embedded library, then deletes it again with DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Adds a small PNG file to the embedded library, then deletes it again with DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems.

Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import base64
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

PNG_1X1 = base64.b64decode ('iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==')
outputPath = 'TapirExamples/tapir_example.png'

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory () as tempDir:
    inputPath = os.path.join (tempDir, 'tapir_example.png')
    with open (inputPath, 'wb') as pngFile:
        pngFile.write (PNG_1X1)
    aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary', {
        'files': [{'inputPath': inputPath, 'outputPath': outputPath}],
        'overwriteExisting': True
    })

# The path is the same relative path AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary took as outputPath.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems', {
    'embeddedLibraryItems': [{'path': outputPath}]
}))

commands.name: CreateLibraryParts
commands.description: Creates GDL library parts in the embedded library from their scripts (master, 2D, 3D, parameter, interface, properties) and parameter definitions, under the given parent subtype. The new parts are placeable right away, e.g. with CreateObjects. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new part is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

libraryParts.description: The library parts to create in the embedded library.

overwriteExisting.description: Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new library part is deleted first, so the new one replaces the loaded library part. By default false: creating on an existing path fails. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

libraryParts.description: The created library parts, in the order of the input, or the error of each one that could not be created.

example.description: Creates a GDL box object in the embedded library with CreateLibraryParts, then deletes it again. The parent subtype is the 'General GDL Object' of the loaded Archicad Library. Deleting the part at the end requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a GDL box object in the embedded library with CreateLibraryParts, then deletes it again.

The parent subtype is the 'General GDL Object' of the loaded Archicad Library. Deleting the part at the
end requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLibraryParts', {
    'libraryParts': [{
        'name': 'Tapir Example Box',
        'parentName': 'General GDL Object',
        'path': 'TapirExamples/Tapir Example Box.gsm',
        'a': 0.6,
        'b': 0.4,
        'parameters': [
            {'name': 'boxHeight', 'type': 'Length', 'value': 0.5, 'description': 'Box Height'},
            {'name': 'boxLabel', 'type': 'String', 'value': 'Tapir', 'description': 'Label'}
        ],
        'script2D': 'RECT2 0, 0, A, B\nTEXT2 A / 2, B / 2, boxLabel',
        'script3D': 'BLOCK A, B, boxHeight',
        'parameterScript': 'VALUES "boxHeight" RANGE [0.1, 3.0]'
    }],
    'overwriteExisting': True
})
aclib.PrintJson (response)
createdPart = response['libraryParts'][0]
if 'error' in createdPart:
    raise SystemExit (createdPart['error']['message'])

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems', {'embeddedLibraryItems': [{'path': createdPart['path']}]})

commands.name: CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary
commands.description: Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.

files.description: The files to copy. Each keeps its file name inside the target folder.

targetFolder.description: Optional. The folder relative to the embedded library to copy the files into, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing folders are created. By default the root of the embedded library.

overwriteIfExists.description: Optional. When true, an item with the same name in the target folder is replaced. By default false.

example.description: Copies two PNG files into a folder of the embedded library with CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary. The files are written to a temporary folder first; the copies are deleted from the embedded library at the end (the deletion requires Archicad 27 or later).
example.code:
"""Copies two PNG files into a folder of the embedded library with CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary.

The files are written to a temporary folder first; the copies are deleted from the embedded library at the end
(the deletion requires Archicad 27 or later).
"""
import base64
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

PNG_1X1 = base64.b64decode ('iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==')
targetFolder = 'TapirExamples/Copied'
fileNames = ['tapir_example_a.png', 'tapir_example_b.png']

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory () as tempDir:
    files = []
    for fileName in fileNames:
        path = os.path.join (tempDir, fileName)
        with open (path, 'wb') as pngFile:
            pngFile.write (PNG_1X1)
        files.append ({'path': path})

    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary', {
        'files': files,
        'targetFolder': targetFolder,
        'overwriteIfExists': True
    }))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems', {
    'embeddedLibraryItems': [{'path': targetFolder + '/' + fileName} for fileName in fileNames]
})

commands.name: IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf
commands.description: Checks for each of the given library parts whether the given ancestor is anywhere up its subtype hierarchy (e.g. whether a part is a kind of furniture), independent of its name. A library part is not a subtype of itself. With matchAncestorByMainId any revision of the ancestor matches.

libraryParts.description: The library parts to check.

ancestor.description: The subtype to check against. Given by unId, it is used as it is, without checking that such a library part is loaded.

matchAncestorByMainId.description: Optional, false by default. When true, only the main GUID of the ancestor's unique ID is compared, so any revision of the ancestor matches; when false, the full unique ID (main and revision GUID) must match.

ancestorUnId.description: The full unique ID of the ancestor the library parts were checked against.

results.description: One result for each library part, in the order of the input.

unId.description: The full unique ID of the checked library part.

isSubtypeOf.description: True if the ancestor is anywhere up the subtype hierarchy of the library part. False for the ancestor itself: a library part is not a subtype of itself.

example.description: Checks with IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf which of a few object library parts are subtypes of the direct parent of the first one. Needs a loaded library with at least one object. Any revision of the parent matches.
example.code:
"""Checks with IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf which of a few object library parts are subtypes of the direct parent of the first one.

Needs a loaded library with at least one object. Any revision of the parent matches.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAvailableLibraryParts', {'filterByTypeId': 'Object'})['libraryParts'][:10]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object library part is loaded.')
libraryParts = [{'index': libraryPart['index']} for libraryPart in objects]

first = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLibraryPartTypeDetails', {'libraryParts': libraryParts[:1]})['libraryParts'][0]

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf', {
    'libraryParts': libraryParts,
    'ancestor': {'unId': first['parentUnId']},
    'matchAncestorByMainId': True
})
aclib.PrintJson (response)

To read a part by its file name, as SetLibraryPartParameters writes it, use GetLibraryPartParameterValues.

libraryParts.description: The library parts to read the default GDL parameters of.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the library part, the same name CreateObjects, CreateLamps, CreateWindows and CreateDoors take as libraryPartName.

gdlParametersOfLibraryParts.description: The default GDL parameters of each given library part, in the order of the input, or an error for a name that no loaded library part has.

libPart.description: The library part found by the name. Absent when it could not be read.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the library part with their default values as stored in the library part (its Parameter Script is not run). The description of each parameter is the displayName of the same entry.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

displayName.description: The display name (description) of the parameter.

index.description: The index of the parameter.

type.description: The type of the parameter.

dimension1.description: The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).

example.description: Lists the default GDL parameters of an object library part, by name, with GetGDLParametersOfLibraryParts. Nothing is placed and no defaults change. Needs a loaded library with at least one object.

commands.name: GetUnusedLibraryParts
commands.description: Lists the loaded library parts that no element of the project is placed from. Read only. The Archicad API does not tell which library parts are used, so every element of the floor plan and of every view and layout is checked: objects, lamps, doors, windows, skylights, zone stamps, symbol labels, drawing titles, curtain wall parts, and the markers of doors, windows, skylights, sections, elevations, details and worksheets. A library part used only in another way (called as a macro, linked as a property object, as an interior elevation marker, in stairs and railings, in the tool defaults or in Favorites) is listed as unused. Library parts that cannot be placed (e.g. macros) are only listed with includeNotPlaceable.

filterByTypeId.description: Optional. Only list the unused library parts of this type (the typeId of GetAvailableLibraryParts).

includeNotPlaceable.description: Also list the library parts that cannot be placed (macros, pictures, property objects, list schemes and the like), which are never placed on their own. Default: false.

unusedLibraryParts.description: The loaded library parts that no element of the project is placed from, in index order.

usedLibraryPartCount.description: The number of different loaded library parts that are placed in the project.

scannedElementCount.description: The number of elements checked, in the floor plan and every view and layout database.

complete.description: False when a view or layout database or a library part could not be read (see warnings): then a listed library part may still be used.

example.description: Lists the loaded library parts that are not placed in the project with GetUnusedLibraryParts. Read only: nothing is changed. A part used only by other GDL scripts, as a property object or in the Favorites is listed too.
example.code:
"""Lists the loaded library parts that are not placed in the project with GetUnusedLibraryParts.

Read only: nothing is changed. A part used only by other GDL scripts, as a property object or in the Favorites is listed too.
"""
import aclib

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetUnusedLibraryParts', {})
for libraryPart in response['unusedLibraryParts']:
    print (libraryPart['index'], libraryPart['typeId'], libraryPart['fileName'])
print ('Unused:', len (response['unusedLibraryParts']), 'Used:', response['usedLibraryPartCount'])
print ('Elements checked:', response['scannedElementCount'], 'Complete:', response['complete'])
for warning in response['warnings']:
    print ('Warning:', warning)

commands.name: SetLibraryPartCustomSection
commands.description: Creates, replaces or deletes a custom section of a loaded library part. The content is given as base64. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

sectionId.description: The type identifier of the custom section. A four-character code is given as its integer value, the first character in the highest byte (e.g. 'ABCD' is 1094861636).

index.description: Optional. The index of the section among the sections with the same identifier. By default 0.

dataVersion.description: Optional. The data version stored with the section. By default 0. Only used with data.

data.description: The new content of the section, base64 encoded. The section is created when it does not exist, otherwise replaced. Give either data or delete.

delete.description: When true, the section is deleted. Give either data or delete.

example.description: Writes a custom section into a library part with SetLibraryPartCustomSection, reads it back and deletes it. The library part is created in the embedded library by the script and deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Writes a custom section into a library part with SetLibraryPartCustomSection, reads it back and deletes it.

The library part is created in the embedded library by the script and deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import base64

import aclib

# A library part of the embedded library, created by this script and deleted at the end.
createdPart = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLibraryParts', {
    'libraryParts': [{
        'name': 'Tapir Example Box',
        'parentName': 'General GDL Object',
        'path': 'TapirExamples/Tapir Example Box.gsm',
        'script3D': 'BLOCK A, B, 1'
    }],
    'overwriteExisting': True
})['libraryParts'][0]
if 'error' in createdPart:
    raise SystemExit (createdPart['error']['message'])
libraryPartName = 'Tapir Example Box.gsm'

# A four-character section code is given as its integer value, the first character in the highest byte.
sectionId = int.from_bytes (b'TAPR', 'big')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetLibraryPartCustomSection', {
    'name': libraryPartName,
    'sectionId': sectionId,
    'dataVersion': 1,
    'data': base64.b64encode (b'Data stored by Tapir').decode ('ascii')
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLibraryPartCustomSection', {'name': libraryPartName, 'sectionId': sectionId})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetLibraryPartCustomSection', {'name': libraryPartName, 'sectionId': sectionId, 'delete': True}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems', {'embeddedLibraryItems': [{'path': createdPart['path']}]})

"""Creates a new .gsm file of the 'General GDL Object' subtype with CreateLibraryPart.

The copy gets a new unique ID unless the main GUID is kept. An existing file is never overwritten. The libraries are reloaded once afterwards, so the copies can be found by name. """Copies the library part of the first object in the project into a temporary folder with CopyLibraryParts.

Needs at least one Object. The copy gets a new unique ID; the temporary folder is deleted at the
end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import shutil
import tempfile

import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

targetFolder = tempfile.mkdtemp ()
try:
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CopyLibraryParts', {
        'libraryParts': [{
            'elementId': objects[0]['elementId'],
            'newName': 'Tapir example copy.gsm',
            'targetFolder': targetFolder
        }]
    }))
finally:
    shutil.rmtree (targetFolder, ignore_errors = True)

folder.description: Optional. The folder of the new .gsm file, relative to the embedded library (or to libraryFolder), created when missing. By default the embedded library (or libraryFolder) itself.

libraryFolder.description: Optional. The absolute path of a local library folder to create the library part in instead of the embedded library. A folder that is not one of the loaded libraries yet is added to them first, and stays added.

overwrite.description: Optional. When true, a library part file of the same name in the folder is overwritten. By default false: the new library part then gets a unique name, which the response returns.

keywords.description: Optional. The keywords of the library part.

commands.name: InterpretGDLScript3D
commands.description: Runs a GDL 3D script, given as text or as the master and 3D scripts of a loaded library part with its default parameters, with the settings of the GDL editor, and returns whether it ran without a GDL error, how many 3D model elements it generated and their bounding box. The API returns no GDL error message or line number.

script.description: The GDL 3D script to run. Either script or libraryPartName is required.

libraryPartName.description: A loaded library part, by its fileName (with extension) or documentName as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns them. Its default parameters are used; without script, its master script followed by its 3D script is run.

success.description: Whether the script ran to its end. False when the GDL interpreter stopped with an error; the API gives no message or line number of the GDL error.

error.description: The error code the interpreter returned, when success is false.

elementCount.description: The number of 3D model elements the script generated, when success is true; 0 for a script that generates no 3D model.

boundingBox3D.description: The bounding box of the generated 3D model, in the local coordinates of the library part, when it has elements.

example.description: InterpretGDLScript3D runs a GDL 3D script like the GDL editor does and tells whether it ran to its end. A script that stops with a GDL error gives success False; the API gives no message or line number. The model's element count tells an empty output apart.
example.code:
"""InterpretGDLScript3D runs a GDL 3D script like the GDL editor does and tells whether it ran to its end. A
script that stops with a GDL error gives success False; the API gives no message or line number. The model's
element count tells an empty output apart.
"""
import aclib

goodScript = 'BLOCK 1, 2, 3'
response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InterpretGDLScript3D', {
    'script': goodScript
})
print ('Good script ran:', response['success'])
print ('Elements:', response.get ('elementCount'))
if 'boundingBox3D' in response:
    box = response['boundingBox3D']
    print ('Size:', round (box['xMax'] - box['xMin'], 3), round (box['yMax'] - box['yMin'], 3), round (box['zMax'] - box['zMin'], 3))

# An uninitialized array index stops the interpreter.
badScript = 'DIM arr[2]\nBLOCK arr[5], 1, 1'
response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InterpretGDLScript3D', {
    'script': badScript
})
print ('Bad script ran:', response['success'])

# With a library part: its master and 3D scripts run with its default parameters.
# Set the name to the fileName or documentName of one of your loaded objects.
libraryPartName = 'Tapir Example Symbol'
response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InterpretGDLScript3D', {
    'libraryPartName': libraryPartName
})
print (libraryPartName, 'ran:', response.get ('success'), response.get ('error', {}).get ('message', ''))

"""Reserves the first wall of the project with ReserveElements and prints the users who hold it if that fails.

Needs an open Teamwork project with at least one Wall. A wall that was free before is released again at the end.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

wasFree = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetReservationStatusOfElements', {'elements': walls})['reservationStatuses'][0].get ('status') == 'Free'

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveElements', {'elements': walls})
for conflict in response.get ('conflicts', []):
    print ('Reserved by', conflict['user']['userName'])
for notElement in response.get ('notElements', []):
    print ('Not an element, not reserved:', notElement['elementId']['guid'])

if wasFree:
    aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElements', {'elements': walls})

isShared.description: Whether the opened project is a Teamwork (BIMcloud) project.

isOnline.description: Whether there is a live connection to the Teamwork server. Always false for a project that is not shared.

users.description: The members of the shared project. Only present when the project is shared.

hotlinkCacheManagementOwner.description: The user who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Only present when somebody has reserved it.

example.description: Gets with GetTeamworkStatus whether the project is shared and online, its members and who holds the Hotlink and XRef management. In a solo project isShared and isOnline are false.

"""Gets with GetTeamworkStatus whether the project is shared and online, its members and who holds the Hotlink and XRef management.

In a solo project isShared and isOnline are false.
"""

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetTeamworkStatus'))

commands.name: GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases

owners.description: The Teamwork owner of each given database, in the order of the input. userId is 0 when nobody owns the database.

commands.name: UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud
commands.description: Uploads local library folders or container files (.lcf) to a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server, as BIMcloud libraries. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29.

libraryPaths.description: The paths of the local library folders or container files (.lcf) to upload.

serverUrl.description: The URL of the BIMcloud or Teamwork server, e.g. 'https://bimcloud.example.com:22000'.

parentPath.description: The path of the folder on the server that holds the libraries, as shown in BIMcloud Manager.

executionResults.description: One result per library, in the order of the input.

example.description: Uploads a local library folder to a folder of a BIMcloud server with UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud. Set serverUrl, parentPath and libraryPath to your own server and library before running it; the values below are placeholders. Uploads to the server. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Uploads a local library folder to a folder of a BIMcloud server with UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud.

Set serverUrl, parentPath and libraryPath to your own server and library before running it; the values below are
placeholders. Uploads to the server. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

serverUrl = 'https://bimcloud.example.com:22000'
parentPath = 'Libraries'
libraryPath = '/path/to/My Library'

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud', {
    'libraryPaths': [libraryPath],
    'serverUrl': serverUrl,
    'parentPath': parentPath
}))

commands.name: PublishPublisherSet
commands.description: Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set.

outputPath.description: Full local or LAN path for publishing. Optional, by default the path set in the settings of the publisher set will be used.

selectedNavigatorItemIds.description: Optional publisher-tree navigator items to publish instead of the whole publisher set.

example.description: Publishes the first publisher set of the project with PublishPublisherSet. Needs at least one publisher set. The output goes to a new temporary folder instead of the path saved in the publisher set.
example.code:
"""Publishes the first publisher set of the project with PublishPublisherSet.

Needs at least one publisher set. The output goes to a new temporary folder instead of the
path saved in the publisher set.
"""
import tempfile
import aclib

publisherSets = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPublisherSets')['publisherSets']
if not publisherSets:
    raise SystemExit ('No publisher set in the project.')

outputPath = tempfile.mkdtemp (prefix = 'TapirPublish_')
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('PublishPublisherSet', {
    'publisherSetName': publisherSets[0]['name'],
    'outputPath': outputPath
}))
print ('Published to', outputPath)

commands.name: CreateDetailMarkers
commands.description: Places Detail markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Detail viewpoint, like the Detail tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.

clipPolygon.description: The boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

markerCoordinate.description: Where the marker symbol is placed. Default is the first point of clipPolygon.

angle.description: Rotation of the marker symbol in radians. Default is that of the tool defaults.

name.description: Name of the new viewpoint. Default is that of the tool defaults.

id.description: Reference ID shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker. Default is that of the tool defaults.

floorIndex.description: Story of the marker when it is placed on a floor plan. Default is the current story.

example.description: Places a Detail marker on the current floor plan story with CreateDetailMarkers, then deletes it again. The marker cuts out a 4 x 3 m rectangle; Archicad creates a new Detail viewpoint for it, which is deleted together with the marker.
example.code:
"""Places a Detail marker on the current floor plan story with CreateDetailMarkers, then deletes it again.

The marker cuts out a 4 x 3 m rectangle; Archicad creates a new Detail viewpoint for it, which is deleted
together with the marker.
"""
import aclib

details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateDetailMarkers', {
    'detailMarkersData': [{
        'clipPolygon': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 3.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 3.0}],
        'name': 'Wall connection',
        'id': 'D1'
    }]
})['elements']
aclib.PrintJson (details)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': details})

commands.name: CreateWorksheetMarkers
commands.description: Places Worksheet markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Worksheet viewpoint, like the Worksheet tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.

clipPolygon.description: The boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

markerCoordinate.description: Where the marker symbol is placed. Default is the first point of clipPolygon.

angle.description: Rotation of the marker symbol in radians. Default is that of the tool defaults.

name.description: Name of the new viewpoint. Default is that of the tool defaults.

id.description: Reference ID shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker. Default is that of the tool defaults.

floorIndex.description: Story of the marker when it is placed on a floor plan. Default is the current story.

example.description: Places a Worksheet marker on the current floor plan story with CreateWorksheetMarkers, then deletes it again. The marker cuts out a 4 x 3 m rectangle; Archicad creates a new Worksheet viewpoint for it, which is deleted together with the marker.
example.code:
"""Places a Worksheet marker on the current floor plan story with CreateWorksheetMarkers, then deletes it again.

The marker cuts out a 4 x 3 m rectangle; Archicad creates a new Worksheet viewpoint for it, which is deleted
together with the marker.
"""
import aclib

worksheets = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWorksheetMarkers', {
    'worksheetMarkersData': [{
        'clipPolygon': [{'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 10.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 10.0, 'y': 3.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 3.0}],

})['elements']

commands.name: ModifyDetailMarkers
commands.description: Changes the name, the reference ID, the clip polygon, the boundary's pen and line type, the marker symbol's angle, always-horizontal setting and pen of Detail and Worksheet markers. Not written: the base point (Archicad places it at the center of the clip polygon's bounding box when the marker is created), the viewpoint the marker refers to, and the marker symbol's other settings, which are parameters of the library part placed as the marker (markerId in GetDetailsOfElements). A value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result.

elementId.description: A Detail or a Worksheet marker.

name.description: The new name of the viewpoint.

id.description: The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker.

clipPolygon.description: The new boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the new boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

penIndex.description: The new pen of the boundary (API_DetailType::pen).

lineTypeIndex.description: Attribute index of the new line type of the boundary (API_DetailType::ltypeInd).

angle.description: The new rotation of the marker symbol, in radians (API_DetailType::angle).

isHorizontalMarker.description: Whether the marker symbol is always horizontal (API_DetailType::horizontalMarker).

markerPenIndex.description: The new pen of the marker symbol, the library part placed as the marker (its markerId in GetDetailsOfElements).

example.description: Changes the ID, name, clip polygon, pens and angle of a Detail marker with ModifyDetailMarkers, reads them back, then deletes it. The script places its own Detail marker on the current floor plan story first (CreateDetailMarkers). ModifyDetailMarkers works on Worksheet markers the same way. penIndex and lineTypeIndex are the boundary's pen and line type, markerPenIndex the pen of the marker symbol; angle turns the marker symbol unless isHorizontalMarker keeps it horizontal.
example.code:
"""Changes the ID, name, clip polygon, pens and angle of a Detail marker with ModifyDetailMarkers, reads them back, then deletes it.

The script places its own Detail marker on the current floor plan story first (CreateDetailMarkers).
ModifyDetailMarkers works on Worksheet markers the same way. penIndex and lineTypeIndex are the
boundary's pen and line type, markerPenIndex the pen of the marker symbol; angle turns the marker
symbol unless isHorizontalMarker keeps it horizontal.
"""
import aclib

markers = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateDetailMarkers', {
    'detailMarkersData': [{
        'clipPolygon': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 3.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 3.0}],
        'name': 'Wall connection',
        'id': 'D1'
    }]
})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyDetailMarkers', {
    'detailMarkersWithDetails': [{
        'elementId': markers[0]['elementId'],
        'id': 'D2',
        'name': 'Corner detail',
        'clipPolygon': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 1.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 1.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0}],
        'penIndex': 3,
        'lineTypeIndex': 1,
        'markerPenIndex': 5,
        'isHorizontalMarker': False,
        'angle': 0.5
    }]
}))

details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': markers})['detailsOfElements'][0]['details']
print (details['detailIdStr'], details['detailName'], len (details['clipPolygon']), round (details['angle'], 3), details['isHorizontalMarker'])

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': markers})

commands.name: CreateLayout
commands.description: Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does. A layout that was created but could not be placed is returned with both its databaseId and the error.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: The sibling after which the new layout is placed, as in MoveNavigatorItem. It must be a child of parentNavigatorItemId (or of the Layout Book root when that is omitted). Cannot be combined with position.

position.description: Archicad inserts new layouts at the first place, which renumbers the sheets after them; "last" appends it after the existing children instead. Cannot be combined with previousNavigatorItemId.

paperWidth.description: Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.

paperHeight.description: Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.

customLayoutNumber.description: The layout's own number, used when customLayoutNumbering is true. It only replaces this layout's displayed number: the layout still counts in its subset's numbering, so the sheets after it are renumbered. Use doNotIncludeInNumbering to leave it out.

customLayoutNumbering.description: Use customLayoutNumber instead of the automatic number. Does not leave the layout out of the subset's numbering; see doNotIncludeInNumbering.

doNotIncludeInNumbering.description: Leave the new layout out of its subset's automatic numbering, so the numbers of the other sheets do not change.

oneOf.description: The layout was created, but it could not be moved to the place asked for by previousNavigatorItemId or position: it stays where Archicad put it.

example.description: Creates a layout at the end of the Layout Book with CreateLayout, then deletes it again. Needs at least one master layout.

commands.name: CreateLayoutSubset
commands.description: Creates Layout Book subsets.

example.description: Creates a Layout Book subset with its own ID prefix and numbering, using CreateLayoutSubset. The new subset stays in the Layout Book: subsets cannot be deleted through the Archicad API.

commands.name: GetLayoutSubsetSettings
commands.description: Gets the settings of existing Layout Book subsets: the same fields CreateLayoutSubset accepts (name, ID prefix, numbering style, ...).

subsetSettings.description: One item per input navigator item, in the same order: the subset's settings with the field names of CreateLayoutSubset, or an error.

example.description: Prints the ID prefix and numbering settings of every Layout Book subset with GetLayoutSubsetSettings.

commands.name: CreateDrawings
commands.description: Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

name.description: Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.

nameType.description: Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.

position.description: Where the Drawing is placed on the layout, in meters; this becomes its pos. Without clipPolygon it is the lower left corner of the Drawing (before rotation). With clipPolygon it is the point where the origin of the source view lands (on a floor plan the project origin): a model point (x, y) appears at position + scale * drawing scale * (x, y), rotated by angle, and the clipPolygon chooses which part is shown.

scale.description: Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

drawingScale.description: Ignored: Archicad takes the scale from the source view (API_DrawingType::drawingScale is output only). GetDetailsOfElements returns the scale the Drawing got.

modelOffset.description: Offset of the model origin within the drawing, in model meters. Archicad uses it only with clipPolygon and then adds modelOffset * drawing scale (times scale, rotated by angle) to the new Drawing's pos; without clipPolygon it is ignored. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

clipPolygon.description: Optional polygon to clip the drawing with, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as position) - not the coordinates of the source view's model. Stored as given: position, angle, scale and modelOffset are not applied to it, and it does not move the content (see position).

example.description: Places the first story of the project as a Drawing on the first layout with CreateDrawings. Needs at least one layout. Deletes the new Drawing at the end.

commands.name: ChangeDrawingLink
commands.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

items.description: An existing Drawing and the navigator item it should be relinked to.

elements.description: One result per input item. On success, elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the element, it cannot keep the original guid.

example.description: Places a Drawing of the first story on a layout, then links it to the second story with ChangeDrawingLink. Needs at least two stories and a layout. ChangeDrawingLink recreates the Drawing, so it returns a new element id. Deletes the Drawing at the end.

commands.name: GetLayoutSettings
commands.description: Gets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

masterLayoutDatabaseId.description: The database of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.

masterNavigatorItemId.description: The Layout Book navigator item of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.

masterLayoutName.description: The name of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.

example.description: Prints the size, margins, numbering, master layout and custom data of every layout with GetLayoutSettings.

commands.name: SetLayoutSettings
commands.description: Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. In Teamwork the layout settings must be reserved first in Archicad (Layout Book > Reserve Layout Settings); the Archicad API cannot reserve them, and ReserveElements does not. GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases shows who holds a layout.

layoutName.description: The new name of the layout or master layout (its database name, as returned by GetDatabases and GetLayoutSettings). A custom name of its Navigator item is changed with RenameNavigatorItem instead.

masterNavigatorItemId.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, as its Layout Book navigator item. Only layouts can be given a master layout, master layouts cannot.

masterLayoutDatabaseId.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, as its database. Used when masterNavigatorItemId is not given.

masterLayoutName.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, by name. Used when neither masterNavigatorItemId nor masterLayoutDatabaseId is given.

example.description: Renames the first layout with SetLayoutSettings, reads it back, then restores the original name. Needs at least one layout.

commands.name: GetDrawingNumberingGridLines
commands.description: Gets the lines of the grid of the grid-based drawing numbering of the current layout (start and end point, pen index, line type index), for example to find which grid cell a drawing on the layout sits in. The current window must be a layout (see ChangeWindow), and only a layout that uses grid-based drawing numbering has such a grid.

lines.description: The lines of the grid of the grid-based drawing numbering of the current layout. Only a layout that uses grid-based drawing numbering has such a grid.

example.description: Prints the drawing numbering grid of the first layout with GetDrawingNumberingGridLines. Opens the first layout, as the command reads the grid of the current window. Only a layout with grid-based drawing numbering has such a grid.
example.code:
"""Prints the drawing numbering grid of the first layout with GetDrawingNumberingGridLines.

Opens the first layout, as the command reads the grid of the current window. Only a layout
with grid-based drawing numbering has such a grid.
"""
import aclib

layouts = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDatabases', {'types': ['Layout']})['databases']
if not layouts:
    raise SystemExit ('No layout in the project.')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'databaseId': layouts[0]['databaseId']})
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDrawingNumberingGridLines'))

commands.name: FindModelViewOption
commands.description: Finds a model view option combination by id or by name and returns its index, id, name and flags. The index is the one SetViewOptions takes to switch the model view options of a window to the combination. Available from Archicad 27.

inputSchema.description: The model view option combination to find, given by id or by name.

name.description: The name of the model view option combination, as shown in Document > Model View > Model View Options.

outputSchema.description: The model view option combination found.

index.description: The index of the model view option combination.

name.description: The name of the model view option combination.

flags.description: The flags of the model view option combination, as Archicad returns them.

example.description: Finds the first named model view option combination by its name with FindModelViewOption, then by its id. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Finds the first named model view option combination by its name with FindModelViewOption, then by its id.

Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

# Archicad may list a combination without a name once the view options of a window changed.
names = [modelViewOption['name'] for modelViewOption in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetModelViewOptions')['modelViewOptions'] if modelViewOption['name']]
if not names:
    raise SystemExit ('No model view option combination in the project.')

found = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FindModelViewOption', {'name': names[0]})
aclib.PrintJson (found)
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FindModelViewOption', {'modelViewOptionId': found['modelViewOptionId']}))

commands.name: GetModelViewOptionDetails
commands.description: Gets the settings stored in model view option combinations (Document > Model View > Model View Options), all of them or the ones given by id or by name: the model view options in the fields of GetViewOptions, and the options library parts add to the combination (gdlOptions) with their GDL parameter values. Read-only: the Archicad API has no function to change, rename or create a stored combination; SetViewOptions changes the options of the current window. Available from Archicad 27.

modelViewOptions.description: The model view option combinations to read, each given by id or by name. When omitted, every combination of the project is returned.

modelViewOptionDetails.description: The settings of each model view option combination, in the order of the input, or in the order of the project when no input is given.

index.description: The index of the model view option combination, the one SetViewOptions takes as modelViewOptionIndex.

name.description: The name of the model view option combination.

modelViewOptions.description: The fields of API_ModelViewOptions stored in the combination, with the curtainWall, stair and railing parts as nested objects: the same fields as viewOptions.modelViewOptions of GetViewOptions. Values are the numeric API constants; attribute indices are plain integers.

gdlOptions.description: The model view options that library parts add to the combination (the library part settings of the Model View Options dialog, e.g. of doors, windows and objects), with their GDL parameter values.

name.description: The name of the option set, e.g. the name of the library global settings part.

guid.description: The unique id of the option set.

supersetGuid.description: The id of another option set that has all of the functionality of this one. When it is given, this set is filled but not shown in the Model View Options dialog.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the option set with their values in this combination.

example.description: Prints the settings of the first named model view option combination with GetModelViewOptionDetails, then lists the library part options of every combination. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap
commands.description: Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.

viewsData.description: Array of views to clone from the Project Map to the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the Project Map viewpoint to clone.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the View Map folder to place the clone in. Required - Archicad's CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap API leaves a clone created directly at the View Map root in a broken state (it cannot be deleted or moved afterwards, by API or by hand), so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

example.description: Clones the first story of the Project Map into a new View Map folder with CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap. Deletes the clone and the folder at the end.
example.code:
"""Clones the first story of the Project Map into a new View Map folder with CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap.

Deletes the clone and the folder at the end.
"""
import aclib

def AllItems (item):
    for child in item.get ('children', []):
        yield child['navigatorItem']
        yield from AllItems (child['navigatorItem'])

projectMap = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorItemTree', {'navigatorMapId': 'ProjectMap'})['navigatorItemTree']
story = next (item for item in AllItems (projectMap) if item['type'] == 'StoryItem')

# A clone must go into a View Map folder, not to the View Map root.
folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder'})
clones = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap', {
    'viewsData': [{'navigatorItemId': story['navigatorItemId'], 'parentNavigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]
})['navigatorItems']
aclib.PrintJson (clones)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [c for c in clones if 'navigatorItemId' in c]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]})

commands.name: CreateViewsInViewMap

viewsData.description: Array of views to create as independent (non-clone) items in the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Source navigator item whose database and settings are copied: a Project Map item, or a View Map view (e.g. a story view). A View Map view is created from its Project Map source (sourceNavigatorItemId in GetNavigatorItemTree), then gets the view's own view settings, name and ID.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: View Map folder to place the new view in. Required - the underlying Archicad API used to create the item leaves it undeletable and unmovable afterwards when it is attached directly to the View Map root, so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

name.description: Name for the new view. Optional; defaults to the source item name.

example.description: Creates an independent View Map view of the first story in a new folder with CreateViewsInViewMap. Deletes the view and the folder at the end.
example.code:
"""Creates an independent View Map view of the first story in a new folder with CreateViewsInViewMap.

Deletes the view and the folder at the end.
"""
import aclib

def AllItems (item):
    for child in item.get ('children', []):
        yield child['navigatorItem']
        yield from AllItems (child['navigatorItem'])

projectMap = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorItemTree', {'navigatorMapId': 'ProjectMap'})['navigatorItemTree']
story = next (item for item in AllItems (projectMap) if item['type'] == 'StoryItem')

# A new view must go into a View Map folder, not to the View Map root.
folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder'})
views = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewsInViewMap', {
    'viewsData': [{
        'navigatorItemId': story['navigatorItemId'],
        'parentNavigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId'],
        'name': 'Tapir Example View'
    }]
})['navigatorItems']
aclib.PrintJson (views)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [v for v in views if 'navigatorItemId' in v]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]})

commands.name: Get3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the projection type, azimuth and transformation matrix of an axonometry, and the sun position of either (date and time or azimuth and altitude).

isPersp.description: True for a perspective projection, false for an axonometric one.

cameraElementId.description: The Camera element the projection was set from. Missing when the projection does not come from a camera.

activeCameraSetElementId.description: The active Camera Set element. Missing when there is none.

perspective.description: The perspective parameters. Present only when isPersp is true.

axonometric.description: The parameters of an axonometric projection. Present only when isPersp is false.

azimuth.description: The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers).

sun.description: The sun position of the axonometry.

example.description: Prints the perspective camera or the axonometric projection of the 3D window with Get3DProjectionSettings.
example.code:
"""Prints the perspective camera or the axonometric projection of the 3D window with Get3DProjectionSettings."""
import aclib

commands.name: Set3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Sets a perspective or an axonometric projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter but sun is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced. An axonometry changes only the values given: the projection type, the azimuth, the transformation matrix and the sun. The sun of either changes only the values given in it and is kept when sun is missing. The 3D window shows the change after a rebuild (RebuildView), e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.

axonometry.description: Makes the projection axonometric. Only the given values change, in sun too; the others are kept from the current axonometry, or from the last one when the projection is a perspective.

azimuth.description: The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers), as Get3DProjectionSettings returns it. Its 3x3 part must be invertible.

sun.description: The sun position of the axonometry. Only the values given change.

example.description: Raises the camera of the 3D perspective by 1 m and puts its sun at 21 June 13:30, or turns the axonometry to isometric, with Set3DProjectionSettings. The sun of a projection only changes the values given in sun; the others are kept. Restores the original projection at the end.
example.code:
"""Raises the camera of the 3D perspective by 1 m and puts its sun at 21 June 13:30, or turns the axonometry to isometric, with Set3DProjectionSettings.

The sun of a projection only changes the values given in sun; the others are kept.
Restores the original projection at the end.
"""
import copy
import aclib

settings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get3DProjectionSettings')

if settings['isPersp']:
    # Every perspective parameter but sun is required: pass back what was read, with the camera moved.
    original = copy.deepcopy (settings['perspective'])
    perspective = settings['perspective']
    perspective['cameraPosition']['z'] += 1.0
    perspective['sun'] = {'sunPositionOption': 'DateAndTime', 'month': 6, 'day': 21, 'hour': 13, 'minute': 30, 'second': 0}
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Set3DProjectionSettings', {'perspective': perspective}))
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get3DProjectionSettings')['perspective']['sun'])
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Set3DProjectionSettings', {'perspective': original}))
else:
    # An axonometry changes only the given values.
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Set3DProjectionSettings', {'axonometry': {'projectionType': 'Isometric'}}))
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Set3DProjectionSettings', {'axonometry': settings['axonometric']}))

commands.name: GetCameras
commands.description: Gets the Camera Sets (camera paths) of the project with their name, whether the set is the active one, its current camera, and its cameras in path order. Each camera has its element id, whether it is active in the path, and its perspective: camera and target position, distance, azimuth, view cone, roll angle, two-point perspective and sun, in the shape Set3DProjectionSettings accepts, so passing a camera's perspective there shows its view in the 3D window. Archicad cameras are always perspective; they have no name of their own.

cameraSets.description: The Camera Sets (camera paths) of the project, each with its cameras.

name.description: The name of the Camera Set, as the navigator shows it.

isActive.description: True for the active Camera Set.

activeCameraElementId.description: The current camera of the set. Missing when the set has none.

cameras.description: The cameras of the set, in the order of the path.

"""Prints the settings of the first 3D Document of the Project Map with Get3DDocumentSettings.

"""Zooms the current 2D window to the middle of the area it shows now, with SetZoom.

Run it with a floor plan, section, worksheet or layout window in front.
"""
import aclib

# Without parameters GetView2DTransformations returns the zoom of the current window.

height = zoom['yMax'] - zoom['yMin']

    'zoomBox': {
        'xMin': zoom['xMin'] + width / 4,

        'xMax': zoom['xMax'] - width / 4,
        'yMax': zoom['yMax'] - height / 4

}))

commands.name: MoveNavigatorItem
commands.description: Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree, or to a new position within its current parent. Fails when Archicad does not put the item where it was asked to.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: The new parent of the item. It can be the item's current parent, to change the order of the items in it.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: Optional child of parentNavigatorItemId that the item is placed right after. Without it an item moved within its own parent goes to the end of it.

example.description: Creates two View Map folders and moves the second into the first with MoveNavigatorItem. Deletes both folders at the end.
example.code:
"""Creates two View Map folders and moves the second into the first with MoveNavigatorItem.

Deletes both folders at the end.
"""
import aclib

first = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder A'})
second = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder B'})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MoveNavigatorItem', {
    'navigatorItemIdToMove': second['navigatorItemId'],
    'parentNavigatorItemId': first['navigatorItemId']
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorParentItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': second['navigatorItemId']}]})

# A folder that is not empty cannot be deleted: delete the inner one first.
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': second['navigatorItemId']}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': first['navigatorItemId']}]})

commands.name: RenameNavigatorItem
commands.description: Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. Renaming the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing also sets the custom name of the Drawing. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

newName.description: The new name of the item. On the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing it is also set as the custom name of the Drawing (nameType CustomName).

newId.description: The new ID of the item. On a layout it is the custom layout number (customLayoutNumbering is switched on); on a Project Map section, elevation, interior elevation, detail or worksheet it is the reference ID of the element behind the item; on any other item it is the custom ID of the navigator item (customUiId becomes true).

customName.description: Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.

example.description: Creates a View Map folder and renames it with RenameNavigatorItem. Deletes the folder at the end.
example.code:
"""Creates a View Map folder and renames it with RenameNavigatorItem.

Deletes the folder at the end.
"""
import aclib

folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder'})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RenameNavigatorItem', {
    'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId'],
    'newName': 'Tapir Renamed Folder'
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]})

commands.name: DeleteNavigatorItems
commands.description: Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets, View Map folders that are not empty, the other Project Map items and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted; the failed execution result says which case applies. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result. dryRun reports the result of the checks made before deleting (item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty) without deleting anything.

dryRun.description: If true, nothing is deleted: each execution result says what the deletion would do for that item, from the checks made before deleting (corrupt id, item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them: a Project Map item other than an independent worksheet, detail or viewpoint created by the Tapir Add-On, a marker-linked worksheet or detail, or in a Teamwork project an item that is not reserved. Default is false.

example.description: Creates an independent Worksheet and deletes it from the Project Map with DeleteNavigatorItems, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.

commands.name: GetNavigatorItemTree
commands.description: Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set to retrieve. Used only when navigatorMapId is PublisherSets. Without it the first publisher set is returned.

includeChildCount.description: Set to true to add childCount, the number of direct children Archicad reports, to every item. Defaults to false.

example.description: Prints the Layout Book as an indented tree with GetNavigatorItemTree. The other maps are ProjectMap, PublicViewMap and PublisherSets (with publisherSetName).
example.code:
"""Prints the Layout Book as an indented tree with GetNavigatorItemTree.

The other maps are ProjectMap, PublicViewMap and PublisherSets (with publisherSetName).
"""
import aclib

def PrintTree (item, indent):
    print ('  ' * indent + '{} {} ({})'.format (item['uiId'], item['name'], item['type']))
    for child in item.get ('children', []):
        PrintTree (child['navigatorItem'], indent + 1)

tree = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorItemTree', {'navigatorMapId': 'LayoutBook'})['navigatorItemTree']
PrintTree (tree, 0)

folderPath.description: The names of the Project Map items the schedule is in, from the top down, without the project itself (e.g. Schedules, Element). Archicad's API does not say whether a schedule lists elements, components or surfaces; the default Project Map shows it by these folders.

commands.name: SetMasterLayoutContext
commands.description: Sets which layout's context the master layout of the current window is drawn in: its autotexts then show the values of the given layout. The current window must be a master layout, otherwise an error is returned. It does not assign a master layout to a layout. Available from Archicad 27.

example.description: Opens the first master layout and draws it in the context of the first layout with SetMasterLayoutContext. Its autotexts then show the values of that layout. Needs a layout and a master layout. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Opens the first master layout and draws it in the context of the first layout with SetMasterLayoutContext.

Its autotexts then show the values of that layout. Needs a layout and a master layout.
Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

databases = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDatabases', {'types': ['Layout', 'MasterLayout']})['databases']
layouts = [d for d in databases if d['type'] == 'Layout']
masters = [d for d in databases if d['type'] == 'MasterLayout']
if not layouts or not masters:
    raise SystemExit ('The project needs a layout and a master layout.')

# The current window must be a master layout.
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'databaseId': masters[0]['databaseId']})
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMasterLayoutContext', {'layoutDatabaseId': layouts[0]['databaseId']}))

commands.name: CreateAddOnViewpoints
commands.description: Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of a leaf node, as Archicad stores them (a bit field). Ignored for a root or a group.

commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideRule
commands.description: Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

name.description: Name of the override rule. Rule names are unique in the project: an existing rule with this name is overwritten, in whichever rule group it is.

ruleGroupName.description: Rule group of a new rule, created when it does not exist. Default: 'Tapir'. An overwritten rule stays in its own group.

criterionXML.description: Optional criterion XML. Archicad only takes XML in its own format: read it from a rule made in the GUI with GetGraphicalOverrideRules and change the values. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and so is an empty one: the rule then applies to all elements.

surfaceRGB.description: Optional color override of the cut and uncut surfaces. Components are in the 0..1 range.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index override for lines, markers and texts. Only a positive index takes effect.

overrideContours.description: Optional. If true, the contours of the overridden surfaces are recolored too.

ruleId.description: The created or overwritten override rule.

example.description: Creates a graphic override rule that colors surfaces red with CreateGraphicalOverrideRule. The rule is created in the rule group 'Tapir Examples', which is deleted with it at the end. Without criterionXML the rule applies to every element. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a graphic override rule that colors surfaces red with CreateGraphicalOverrideRule.

The rule is created in the rule group 'Tapir Examples', which is deleted with it at the end. Without criterionXML
the rule applies to every element. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateGraphicalOverrideRule', {
    'name': 'Tapir Example Red Surfaces',
    'ruleGroupName': 'Tapir Examples',
    'surfaceRGB': {'red': 1.0, 'green': 0.0, 'blue': 0.0},
    'linePenIndex': 20,
    'overrideContours': True
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetGraphicalOverrideRules')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups', {'ruleGroupNames': ['Tapir Examples'], 'deleteRules': True})

"""Exports a new issue to a temporary BCF file, deletes it, then imports it back with ImportIssuesFromBCF.

Leaves the imported issue in the project.
"""
import os
import tempfile
import aclib

issue = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateIssue', {'name': 'Tapir Example Issue'})
bcfPath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (prefix = 'TapirBCF_'), 'issue.bcfzip')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ExportIssuesToBCF', {
    'issues': [{'issueId': issue['issueId']}],
    'exportPath': bcfPath,
    'useExternalId': False,
    'alignBySurveyPoint': True
})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteIssue', {'issueId': issue['issueId']})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportIssuesFromBCF', {'importPath': bcfPath, 'alignBySurveyPoint': True}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIssues')

example.description: Imports the markups of a PDF file as issues with ImportMarkupsFromPDF, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups. Needs a PDF with markups, here markups.pdf in the home folder. Creates one issue per markup. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Imports the markups of a PDF file as issues with ImportMarkupsFromPDF, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups.

Needs a PDF with markups, here markups.pdf in the home folder. Creates one issue per markup.
Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import os
import aclib

pdfFilePath = os.path.join (os.path.expanduser ('~'), 'markups.pdf')
if not os.path.isfile (pdfFilePath):
    raise SystemExit ('No PDF at {}.'.format (pdfFilePath))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportMarkupsFromPDF', {'pdfFilePath': pdfFilePath}))

folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteFolders', {
    'foldersData': [{'key': 'TAPIR', 'title': 'Tapir Example Folder'}]
})['keynoteFolderIdsOrErrors'][0]
aclib.PrintJson (folder)

# Without parentFolderId the folder is created in the root folder.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteFolders', {
    'foldersData': [{'parentFolderId': folder['keynoteFolderId'], 'key': 'TAPIR-SUB', 'title': 'Tapir Example Subfolder'}]
}))

# Deleting a folder deletes its content too.
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteKeynoteFolders', {'keynoteFolderIds': [{'keynoteFolderId': folder['keynoteFolderId']}]})

commands.name: CreateKeynoteLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create keynote labels.
