commands.name: GetProjectDataKeys
commands.description: Lists the project data stored by Tapir in the project: the names, the identifiers of the add-on objects that store them, whether they are kept on this client only and the Teamwork user who has reserved them. Project data is text (for example JSON) saved in the project file by scripts and Grasshopper definitions, such as their settings or the mapping of elements to an external system.

keys.description: The project data stored by Tapir in the project.

example.description: Prints the names of the project data stored by Tapir, with their Teamwork owners, with GetProjectDataKeys.
example.code:
"""Prints the names of the project data stored by Tapir, with their Teamwork owners, with GetProjectDataKeys."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys'))

commands.name: GetProjectData
commands.description: Gets the content of the project data with the given names.

names.description: The names of the project data to get.

values.description: The project data in the order of the given names, or an error for a name that has no project data.

example.description: Prints the content of every project data stored by Tapir with GetProjectData.
example.code:
"""Prints the content of every project data stored by Tapir with GetProjectData."""
import aclib

keys = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')['keys']
if not keys:
    raise SystemExit ('No project data in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectData', {'names': [k['name'] for k in keys]}))

commands.name: SetProjectData
commands.description: Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

values.description: The project data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

example.description: Saves a JSON text in the project under a name with SetProjectData, reads it back, then deletes it.

commands.name: DeleteProjectData
commands.description: Deletes the project data with the given names.

names.description: The names of the project data to delete.

example.description: Saves a project data and deletes it again with DeleteProjectData.
example.code:
"""Saves a project data and deletes it again with DeleteProjectData."""
import aclib

name = 'tapir-example/to-delete'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'temporary'}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectData', {'names': [name]}))

commands.name: ReserveProjectData
commands.description: Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it.

names.description: The names of the project data to reserve.

conflicts.description: The project data that could not be reserved because another user has reserved it.

example.description: Saves a project data, reserves it in Teamwork with ReserveProjectData, then releases and deletes it. Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation fails.
example.code:
"""Saves a project data, reserves it in Teamwork with ReserveProjectData, then releases and deletes it.

Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation fails.
"""
import aclib

name = 'tapir-example/teamwork'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'shared'}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveProjectData', {'names': [name]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseProjectData', {'names': [name]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectData', {'names': [name]})

commands.name: ReleaseProjectData
commands.description: Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork.

names.description: The names of the project data to release.

example.description: Saves and reserves a project data, then releases it in Teamwork with ReleaseProjectData and deletes it. Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation and the release fail.

"""Saves and reserves a project data, then releases it in Teamwork with ReleaseProjectData and deletes it.

Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation and the release fail.
"""
import aclib

name = 'tapir-example/teamwork'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'shared'}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveProjectData', {'names': [name]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseProjectData', {'names': [name]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectData', {'names': [name]})

commands.name: RequestProjectData
commands.description: Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message.

names.description: The names of the project data to request from the users who have reserved them.

mailText.description: The message sent with the request. The default is empty.

example.description: Requests the project data reserved by other Teamwork users from them, with a message, with RequestProjectData. Needs a Teamwork project. Sends the request to the users who reserved the data.
example.code:
"""Requests the project data reserved by other Teamwork users from them, with a message, with RequestProjectData.

Needs a Teamwork project. Sends the request to the users who reserved the data.
"""
import aclib

keys = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')['keys']
reserved = [k['name'] for k in keys if 'teamworkOwner' in k]
if not reserved:
    raise SystemExit ('No reserved project data.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RequestProjectData', {
    'names': reserved,
    'mailText': 'Please release the Tapir project data.'
}))

commands.name: GrantProjectData
commands.description: Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user.

names.description: The names of the project data, reserved by the current user, to grant.

toUserId.description: The Teamwork user id of the user who gets the project data, for example the userId of a user returned by GetProjectDataKeys or ReserveProjectData.

example.description: Saves and reserves a project data, then grants it to another Teamwork user with GrantProjectData. Needs a Teamwork project. Set toUserId to the user to grant to, e.g. the userId of a teamworkOwner that GetProjectDataKeys lists.
example.code:
"""Saves and reserves a project data, then grants it to another Teamwork user with GrantProjectData.

Needs a Teamwork project. Set toUserId to the user to grant to, e.g. the userId of a teamworkOwner
that GetProjectDataKeys lists.
"""
import aclib

toUserId = 2
name = 'tapir-example/teamwork'

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'shared'}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveProjectData', {'names': [name]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GrantProjectData', {'names': [name], 'toUserId': toUserId}))

commands.name: GetModulData
commands.description: Gets the module data Tapir stored in the project with StoreModulData: the given names, or all of them, with their data version and, unless includeContent is false, their content. Module data are the custom data sections of Archicad's ModulData Manager: text saved in the project file under a name, kept apart from project data (SetProjectData).

names.description: The names of the module data to get; the empty name is the default section. When omitted, every module data Tapir stored in the project is returned.

includeContent.description: Whether the content is returned too. When false, only the names and data versions are read, without loading the data. The default is true.

modulData.description: The module data in the order of the given names (or of the list Archicad returns), or an error for a name that has no module data.

name.description: The name of the module data.

dataVersion.description: The version number stored with the data.

content.description: The content of the module data. Left out when includeContent is false.

example.description: GetModulData returns the module data Tapir stored in the project (StoreModulData): every one without names, or the given names. With includeContent false only the names and data versions are read. A name without module data gets an error item.

commands.name: StoreModulData
commands.description: Creates or overwrites module data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name, with an optional data version. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data. Storing module data is not an undoable step.

modulData.description: The module data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

name.description: The name of the module data; the empty name is the default section.

content.description: The content of the module data, for example a JSON string.

dataVersion.description: A version number stored with the data, returned by GetModulData, for example to tell the formats of your content apart. The default is 1.

example.description: Module data are the custom data sections of Archicad's ModulData Manager: text saved in the project file under a name, kept apart from project data (SetProjectData). StoreModulData creates or overwrites them, with an optional data version; storing is not an undoable step.

commands.name: DeleteModulData
commands.description: Deletes the module data with the given names. Deleting module data is not an undoable step.

names.description: The names of the module data to delete; the empty name is the default section.

example.description: DeleteModulData deletes the module data with the given names; a name without module data gets a failed execution result. Deleting is not an undoable step.

commands.name: GetMEPElements
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project (every element the MEP API lists, and from Archicad 30 the electrical panels and devices), optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

elementTypes.description: Optional filter for the MEP element types.

domains.description: Optional filter for the MEP domains.

elements.description: The MEP elements.

example.description: Lists the duct and pipe routes and terminals of the project with GetMEPElements. Leave out both filters to list every MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Lists the duct and pipe routes and terminals of the project with GetMEPElements.

Leave out both filters to list every MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPElements', {
    'elementTypes': ['RoutingElement', 'Terminal'],
    'domains': ['Ventilation', 'Piping']
}))

commands.name: GetMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, the floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style, insulation thickness and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, preferred transition placement, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28.

example.description: Prints the polyline, segments and nodes of the first MEP routes of the project with GetMEPRoutingElements. Needs at least one MEP route (duct, pipe or cable carrier). Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPPorts
commands.description: Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size, connection status (Archicad 27: whether the port is connected, from Archicad 28: whether it is physically connected) and connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports (from Archicad 28), the nominal size of piping ports (from Archicad 30), and the outer diameter, wall thickness and flange size (Archicad 30) of piping and ventilation ports. Available from Archicad 27.

example.description: Prints the ports of the first MEP elements of the project with GetMEPPorts. Needs at least one MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPDistributionSystems
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute, member elements, physical systems (from Archicad 29) and optionally their tree: the elements from the root element on, each with its previous and next elements and the connecting ports. Available from Archicad 28.

includeTree.description: Whether to return the tree of each system: its elements from the root element on, each with the element it is connected to on the way from the root. False when not given.

distributionSystems.description: The distribution systems of the project.

ports.description: The ports in the distribution systems graph (see GetMEPPorts).

example.description: Prints the MEP distribution systems of the project and their element trees with GetMEPDistributionSystems. The physical systems of a distribution system are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the MEP distribution systems of the project and their element trees with GetMEPDistributionSystems.

The physical systems of a distribution system are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

systems = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPDistributionSystems', {'includeTree': True})['distributionSystems']
for system in systems:
    print (f"{system['domain']} system: {len (system['elements'])} element(s)")
    for node in system.get ('tree', []):
        print (f"{'  ' * (node['depth'] + 1)}{node['elementId']['guid']}")

commands.name: CreateMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP routing elements.

example.description: Creates a rectangular duct route with one corner and a circular pipe route with CreateMEPRoutingElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: CreateMEPElements
commands.description: Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions, optionally with another library part, size (from Archicad 30), MEP system, port sizes and shapes and a changed insulation, which apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

elementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP elements.

example.description: Places a duct terminal and a pipe accessory with the current tool settings using CreateMEPElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, insulation thickness of the whole route (segments, elbows and transitions), and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP routing elements. Only provided fields are changed.

example.description: Changes the cross section and insulation of a duct route with ModifyMEPRoutingElements. Creates a temporary duct route, modifies it, reads it back and deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPPorts
commands.description: Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28.

portsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP ports. Only provided fields are changed.

example.description: Changes the flow direction and outer diameter of a pipe port with ModifyMEPPorts. Creates a temporary pipe route, modifies the port at its start, reads it back and deletes the route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ConnectMEPElements
commands.description: Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. The first or last node of the 'connectToId' route must lie exactly on the 'routingElementId' route, so for a tee pass the main route as 'routingElementId' and the branch as 'connectToId'. A failed connection says which condition is not met. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27.

example.description: Connects a branch duct to the middle of a main duct with ConnectMEPElements, which creates a branch element. Creates the two duct routes; the branch starts on the main route, as the command needs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: CheckMEPPortConnectability
commands.description: Checks whether MEP ports can be connected to other ports, for the given pairs of ports. Archicad 28 and later check the physical connection. Available from Archicad 27.

portPairs.description: The pairs of ports to check.

results.description: The result for each pair of ports, in the order of the input.

example.description: Checks with CheckMEPPortConnectability whether the end port of one duct can be connected to the ports of another. Creates two temporary duct routes that meet at one point and deletes them at the end. The command itself works from Archicad 27; creating the routes requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTables
commands.description: Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, wall thickness, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables, plus the rectangular duct tables of the Ventilation domain or the segment tables of the CableCarrier domain. Each table has its name and whether it is editable; the segment tables also have their segmentation lengths from Archicad 29. The rows of the circular, elbow, branch and transition tables say whether they are valid, and the reference set and the angle set say which of their reference ids and angles are defined. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Every row has its index in the table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Available from Archicad 28.

domain.description: The MEP domain of the segment preference tables.

includeFittingTables.description: Also return the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. Defaults to false. Ignored for the CableCarrier domain.

tables.description: The circular segment preference tables of the domain. Empty for the CableCarrier domain.

rectangularTables.description: The rectangular segment preference tables of the Ventilation domain.

cableCarrierTables.description: The segment preference tables of the CableCarrier domain.

referenceSet.description: The reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain. Not returned for the CableCarrier domain.

elbowTables.description: The elbow preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.

branchTables.description: The branch preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.

transitionTables.description: The transition preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true, available from Archicad 29.

example.description: Prints the pipe preference tables of the project, with the elbow, branch and transition tables, using GetMEPPreferenceTables. The angle set and the transition tables are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the pipe preference tables of the project, with the elbow, branch and transition tables, using GetMEPPreferenceTables.

The angle set and the transition tables are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {
    'domain': 'Piping',
    'includeFittingTables': True
}))

commands.name: ModifyMEPPreferenceTables
commands.description: Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, deletes reference ids from the reference set, and adds and deletes angles of the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.

domain.description: The MEP domain of the segment preference tables.

tablesToAdd.description: New tables to add to the domain, before the other changes.

tables.description: The tables of the domain to change, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Each table is changed in one undoable step.

tablesToDelete.description: The guids of the tables of the domain to delete, after the other table changes.

referenceIdsToDelete.description: Reference ids to delete from the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain.

anglesToAdd.description: Angles in degrees, between 1 and 90, to add to the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, so that elbow and branch rows can have them. They are added before the tables are changed. Available from Archicad 29.

anglesToDelete.description: Angles to delete from the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Available from Archicad 29.

addedTables.description: One item for each item of tablesToAdd: the guid of the new table, or the error.

tables.description: One result for each item of tables.

deletedTables.description: One result for each item of tablesToDelete.

example.description: Adds a cable carrier segment table, renames it and fills it with rows using ModifyMEPPreferenceTables, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, editable flag, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroups.description: The system groups of the project with their physical systems.

example.description: Lists the MEP system groups of the project and their physical systems with GetMEPSystemGroups. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Lists the MEP system groups of the project and their physical systems with GetMEPSystemGroups.

Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""

for systemGroup in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPSystemGroups', {})['systemGroups']:
    if 'error' in systemGroup:
        continue
    print (f"{systemGroup['name']}: {', '.join (s['name'] for s in systemGroup['physicalSystems'] if 'name' in s)}")

commands.name: CreateMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to create system groups.

    'systemGroupsData': [{'name': 'Heating'}]

commands.name: CreateMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to create physical systems.

example.description: Creates a flow and a return physical system in a new MEP system group with CreateMEPPhysicalSystems. Adds a new system group "Heating" on every run. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Renames MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to modify system groups.

example.description: Renames the first editable MEP system group of the project with ModifyMEPSystemGroups and renames it back. Needs at least one system group. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Modifies MEP physical systems: name, root element and the MEP system used as their category. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to modify physical systems. Only the given fields are changed.

example.description: Renames the first editable MEP physical system of the project with ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems and renames it back. Needs at least one physical system. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

commands.name: DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Removes MEP physical systems from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystems.description: The physical systems to remove from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted.

example.description: Creates a physical system in a new MEP system group and removes it again with DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems. Leaves the new, empty system group "Heating" in the project. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPToolDefaults
commands.description: Retrieves the current settings of the MEP tools per domain, without changing them: the routing tool (MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings from Archicad 29, and its segment, node, elbow (Archicad 27 and from Archicad 29) and transition defaults), its rigid segment and branch defaults, the flexible segment tool, the library part, insulation and port settings of the terminal, accessory, fitting and equipment tools, and from Archicad 30 the electrical panel tool with its number of circuit defaults. Archicad 27 gives fewer settings, and only the shape of the ports. Available from Archicad 27.

domains.description: The domains to return the tool defaults of. All three when not given.

toolDefaults.description: The tool defaults of each requested domain, in the order requested.

equipment.description: The default of the Equipment tool, which has no domain. Left out when Archicad gives none.

commands.name: TransferMEPSettings
commands.description: Picks up the settings of an MEP element and injects them into other MEP elements of the same type and domain, like Archicad's pick up and inject parameters. Works for routing elements, terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings, flexible segments, branches, take-offs and (from Archicad 30) electrical panels and devices. Each target is changed in its own undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.

sourceElementId.description: The MEP element to pick up the settings from: a routing element, terminal, accessory, equipment, fitting, flexible segment, branch, take-off, or (from Archicad 30) electrical panel or device.

targetElements.description: The MEP elements to inject the settings into. Each must be of the type and domain of the source element.

example.description: Copies the settings of a wide duct route onto a narrow one with TransferMEPSettings. Creates two temporary duct routes, transfers the settings, reads the target back and deletes both. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: CreateMEPFlexibleSegments
commands.description: Creates MEP flexible segments through the given control points, or along a polyline of alternating line and spline parts (Piping), with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain, optionally with the orientation (control points) or direction (polyline) at both ends. Available from Archicad 28.

flexibleSegmentsData.description: Array of data to place MEP flexible segments with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain (see GetMEPToolDefaults).

example.description: Creates a flexible duct through three control points with CreateMEPFlexibleSegments. Uses the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: CreateMEPTakeOffs
commands.description: Creates MEP take-offs on the given routing segments, at a distance from the beginning of the segment (not more than its length) and optionally rotated around its axis by a multiple of 90 degrees, with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain (by default the domain of the segment's routing element), optionally with their length and without insulation, which apply only to what is created. Archicad only has Ventilation take-offs. Available from Archicad 28.

takeOffsData.description: Array of data to create MEP take-offs on routing segments with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain.

example.description: Creates a take-off 2 m from the start of a new duct route with CreateMEPTakeOffs. Creates the duct route first; the take-off uses the current settings of the Take-Off tool of the route's domain (no 'domain' given), faces up (a quarter turn) and has no insulation. Archicad only has Ventilation take-offs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPElements
commands.description: Modifies placed MEP elements: the anchor point, orientation and library part of terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings and flexible segments, the control points, polyline (Piping, from Archicad 28), and width and height of flexible segments. Only the given fields are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element; an item with a field that does not fit its element changes nothing. Archicad reports a 'libraryPartId' it does not find only after the item's other changes were made, so that item's error says which changes stayed. Available from Archicad 27.

elements.description: The MEP elements to modify, each with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed.

example.description: Requires Archicad 27 or newer. On Archicad 27 this example reads the tool defaults and works on the selected MEP elements (select a flexible segment and a terminal first), because Archicad 27 has no commands to place them. From Archicad 28 it places its own elements and deletes them at the end.

commands.name: GetMEPRoutingParameters
commands.description: Gets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: of a routing element its routing node parameters (preferred transition placement, elbow from Archicad 29, transition) and routing segment parameters (cross section, preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style); of a routing node its elbow (from Archicad 29) and transition parameters; of a routing segment its rigid segment parameters (Archicad 28 only). Available from Archicad 28.

elements.description: MEP routing elements, routing nodes or routing segments.

routingParameters.description: The routing parameters of the given elements, in their order.

example.description: Prints the routing parameters of the first MEP route of the project and of its nodes and segments with GetMEPRoutingParameters. Needs at least one MEP route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the routing parameters of the first MEP route of the project and of its nodes and segments with GetMEPRoutingParameters.

Needs at least one MEP route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

routes = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPElements', {'elementTypes': ['RoutingElement']})['elements']
if not routes:
    raise SystemExit ('No MEP route in the project.')
routeId = routes[0]['elementId']

route = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPRoutingElements', {'elements': [{'elementId': routeId}]})['routingElements'][0]
ids = [routeId] + [node['elementId'] for node in route['nodes']] + [segment['elementId'] for segment in route['segments']]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPRoutingParameters', {
    'elements': [{'elementId': id} for id in ids]
}))

commands.name: SetMEPRoutingParameters
commands.description: Sets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: the routing segment parameters (cross section and preference table) and, from Archicad 29, the routing node parameters (elbow radius factor and preference table, transition preference table) of routing elements, and the elbow and transition parameters of routing nodes (from Archicad 29). Only the given keys are changed, with one execution result per element. A changed preference table is also set on each of the route's segments and nodes and injected into them, because Archicad 29 can otherwise keep the old one; the item fails if they still report the old table. Available from Archicad 28.

elements.description: The routing parameters to change. Only the given keys are changed. An item gives either routingNodeParameters and/or routingSegmentParameters for a routing element, or elbowParameters and/or transitionParameters for a routing node.

example.description: Makes a pipe route circular and changes the elbow radius factor of its nodes with SetMEPRoutingParameters. Creates a temporary pipe route with one corner, changes it, reads the parameters back and deletes it. The elbow parameters can be set from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Gets rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle): whether the row is valid and its values (diameters, wall thickness, radius, length, angle, branch offset, connection length, description), and whether the table exists. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables only give whether they exist, as their rows have no key. On Archicad 27, which has one kind of preference table, a row is found by its shape and index and has a value and a description; the table's name and number of rows per shape are returned too. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

keys.description: The keys of the rows to get.

name.description: Archicad 27 only: the name of the table.

sizes.description: Archicad 27 only: the number of rows of each shape.

rows.description: The rows in the order of the keys.

example.description: Reads the first two rows of the first pipe segment preference table by their reference id with GetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the keys are a shape and an index).
example.code:
"""Reads the first two rows of the first pipe segment preference table by their reference id with GetMEPPreferenceTableRows.

Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the keys are a shape and an index).
"""
import aclib

tables = [t for t in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {'domain': 'Piping'})['tables'] if t['rows']]
if not tables:
    raise SystemExit ('No pipe segment preference table with rows in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTableRows', {
    'tableId': {'guid': tables[0]['guid']},
    'keys': [{'referenceId': row['referenceId']} for row in tables[0]['rows'][:2]]
}))

commands.name: SetMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Sets the given values of rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table, found by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle). Only the given values are changed, in one undo step. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index, its value and description are set, and its index after the call is returned; the keys give the indices before the call. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

rows.description: The rows to change. Only the given values are set.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

example.description: Changes the description of a row of an editable pipe segment preference table with SetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Reads the row, changes it, reads it back and restores the old description. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the key is a shape and an index).

commands.name: AddMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Adds rows with the given keys and optionally values to a branch, elbow or transition preference table and returns their index, in one undo step. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29; segment tables have a row for each reference id. On Archicad 27 a row is added to the list of the given shape of any preference table, and the index of each new row after the call is returned. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

rows.description: The rows to add, with their key and optionally their values. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29. Segment tables have a row for each reference id, so no row can be added to them. Archicad 27: the key has the shape only, the table gives the index.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

example.description: Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table with AddMEPPreferenceTableRows. The new row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet; it is deleted again at the end. Elbow rows can be added from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table with AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.

The new row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row
for yet; it is deleted again at the end. Elbow rows can be added from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

preferences = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {'domain': 'Piping', 'includeFittingTables': True})
elbowTables = [t for t in preferences.get ('elbowTables', []) if t.get ('isEditable') and t['rows']]
if not elbowTables:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable pipe elbow preference table with rows in the project.')
table = elbowTables[0]
referenceId = table['rows'][0]['referenceId']
usedAngles = [row.get ('angle') for row in table['rows'] if row['referenceId'] == referenceId]
freeAngles = [angle for angle in preferences['angleSet']['angles'] if angle not in usedAngles]
if not freeAngles:
    raise SystemExit ('Every angle of the angle set has a row already.')
key = {'referenceId': referenceId, 'angle': freeAngles[0]}

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddMEPPreferenceTableRows', {
    'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']},
    'rows': [{'key': key, 'values': {'description': 'Added by Tapir'}}]
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows', {'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']}, 'keys': [key]})

commands.name: DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Deletes rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle), in one undo step. The rows of segment tables, and of the elbow tables of Archicad 28, are emptied instead. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

keys.description: The keys of the rows to delete. Segment tables, and the elbow tables of Archicad 28, have a row for each reference id, which is emptied instead. Archicad 27: the indices are those before the call; the rows are deleted from the highest index down.

example.description: Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table and deletes it again with DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows. The row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet. Rows of segment tables are emptied instead of deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table and deletes it again with DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.

The row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet.
Rows of segment tables are emptied instead of deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

preferences = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {'domain': 'Piping', 'includeFittingTables': True})
elbowTables = [t for t in preferences.get ('elbowTables', []) if t.get ('isEditable') and t['rows']]
if not elbowTables:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable pipe elbow preference table with rows in the project.')
table = elbowTables[0]
referenceId = table['rows'][0]['referenceId']
usedAngles = [row.get ('angle') for row in table['rows'] if row['referenceId'] == referenceId]
freeAngles = [angle for angle in preferences['angleSet']['angles'] if angle not in usedAngles]
if not freeAngles:
    raise SystemExit ('Every angle of the angle set has a row already.')
key = {'referenceId': referenceId, 'angle': freeAngles[0]}
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddMEPPreferenceTableRows', {'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']}, 'rows': [{'key': key}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows', {
    'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']},
    'keys': [key]
}))

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; before Archicad 27 it is required.

curveMembers.description: The elements of the curve members (beams, columns) of the model.

surfaceMembers.description: The elements of the surface members (walls, slabs, roofs) of the model.

Without 'analyticalModelId' the model of the current view is used, from Archicad 27; before that pass the model.

commands.name: GetAnalyticalMemberDetails
commands.description: Retrieves the curve, surface or segmented surface member of the given elements in a Structural Analytical Model, with their connections. Cross sections, curves, nodes and surfaces are returned with every field the Archicad version has.

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; before Archicad 27 it is required.

segmentationCentralAngle.description: When given, surface members are read as segmented surface members (for curved walls), each segment spanning at most this central angle, in radians.

analyticalMembers.description: The analytical member of each element, in the order of the input. An element that is no member of the model, or whose member cannot be read, is represented by an error object.

example.description: Prints the first curve and surface member of the Structural Analytical Model of the current view with GetAnalyticalMemberDetails. Needs at least one analytical member. Reading the members of the current view requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the first curve and surface member of the Structural Analytical Model of the current view with GetAnalyticalMemberDetails.

Needs at least one analytical member. Reading the members of the current view requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

members = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAnalyticalMembers', {})
elements = members['curveMembers'][:1] + members['surfaceMembers'][:1]
if not elements:
    raise SystemExit ('No analytical member in the current view.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAnalyticalMemberDetails', {
    'elements': elements
}))

links.description: The link the API returns for each element after the conversion, in the order of the input. An element that cannot be converted is represented by an error object.

commands.name: GetAnalyticalLoads
commands.description: Retrieves the settings, the loaded member part, the custom data (the curve of an edge load, the contour of a surface load) and the geometry of the given analytical point, edge and surface loads. Available from Archicad 26.

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model the geometry is read from. The model of the current view is used when it is omitted; in Archicad 26 it is required.

loads.description: The load of each element, in the order of the input, with its geometry in the Structural Analytical Model and, for an edge or a surface load, its custom data (the curve or contour stored with the element). An element that is not an analytical point, edge or surface load, or whose load cannot be got, is represented by an error object.

example.description: Puts a 10 kN point load on the start of the first curve member and prints it with GetAnalyticalLoads. Needs at least one analytical curve member and one load case. Deletes the load at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later (the command itself works from Archicad 26).

commands.name: CreateAnalyticalLoads
commands.description: Creates analytical point, edge and surface loads from their settings, loaded member part and custom data, as GetAnalyticalLoads returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26.

loads.description: The loads to create, as GetAnalyticalLoads returns them without their geometry. Each is created from the defaults of its tool. An edge load needs the curve and a surface load the contour it is applied on, in customData.

example.description: Puts a 10 kN point load and a 5 kN/m line load on the first curve member with CreateAnalyticalLoads. Needs at least one analytical curve member and one load case; the loads go into the first load case. Forces are in newtons, downward along the global z axis. Requires Archicad 27 or later (the command itself works from Archicad 26).

commands.name: CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers
commands.description: Creates elements (beams, columns, walls, slabs, roofs) from the given curve, surface or segmented surface members, in the form GetAnalyticalMemberDetails returns them, optionally with the settings of a favorite, in one undo step. Returns the new elements and, from Archicad 26, the mapping of their edges and vertices to member parts.

members.description: The analytical members to create elements from, in the form GetAnalyticalMemberDetails returns them, so a member read there can be passed on as it is. The elemGuid of a member is ignored. A curve member needs analyticalMemberType and curve, a surface member (or segment) analyticalMemberType and contour; the other fields are zero when left out.

elements.description: The new element of each member, in the order of the input. A member no element could be created from is represented by an error object.

example.description: Creates a copy of the first curve member's element from its analytical member with CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers. Needs at least one analytical curve member; the member is passed on as GetAnalyticalMemberDetails returns it, so the new beam or column lies on top of the original. Reading the members of the current view requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a copy of the first curve member's element from its analytical member with CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers.

Needs at least one analytical curve member; the member is passed on as GetAnalyticalMemberDetails returns it, so the
new beam or column lies on top of the original. Reading the members of the current view requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

curveMembers = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAnalyticalMembers', {})['curveMembers']
if not curveMembers:
    raise SystemExit ('No analytical curve member in the current view.')
details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAnalyticalMemberDetails', {'elements': curveMembers[:1]})['analyticalMembers'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers', {
    'members': [{'curveMember': details['curveMember']}]
}))

commands.name: CreateSolidElementLinks
commands.description: Creates solid element operation links between target and operator elements.

solidLinks.description: List of solid element operation links to create.

example.description: Subtracts a slab from a wall with CreateSolidElementLinks and reads the link back. The wall and the slab are created by the script and deleted at the end.

commands.name: RemoveSolidElementLinks
commands.description: Removes solid element operation links between target and operator elements. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each link that exists gets wouldDelete.

solidLinks.description: List of solid element operation links to remove.

executionResults.description: One result for each input link, in the order of the input. On a dry run a link that exists (the operator is linked to the target) gets wouldDelete.

example.description: Removes the solid element operation link between a wall and a slab with RemoveSolidElementLinks. The wall, the slab and the link between them are created by the script first; the elements are deleted at the end.

commands.name: GetSolidElementLinks
commands.description: Returns solid element operation links for each queried element, grouped by role (target or operator).

elements.description: Elements to query. Returns all solid links where each element is a target or an operator.

solidLinks.description: For each input element, the solid links where it acts as target and where it acts as operator.

example.description: Gets the solid element operation links of the first three walls with GetSolidElementLinks, as target and as operator. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Gets the solid element operation links of the first three walls with GetSolidElementLinks, as target and as operator.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSolidElementLinks', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: CreateSolidOperations
commands.description: Runs a solid operation (subtraction, intersection, addition) on two morphs and returns the resulting morphs, one item per operation. Unlike CreateSolidElementLinks this is not a link: the target and the operator morph are replaced by the result. Morphs only; the operations run in one undo step.

operations.description: The solid operations to run, each on two morphs. The target and the operator morph are replaced by the resulting morph.

results.description: One item per operation, in the order of the input: the resulting morphs, or an error.

elements.description: The morphs created by the operation.

example.description: Subtracts a small box morph from a bigger one with CreateSolidOperations. Both morphs are created by the script and replaced by the resulting morph, which is deleted at the end.

commands.name: TrimElements
commands.description: Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or one given trimming element with a trim type. With several roofs or shells in the list Archicad decides which of them trims which element (they may also trim each other), so not every element is necessarily trimmed by each; to trim each element with each roof or shell, call it once per roof or shell with trimmingElement, and check the result with GetElementTrims.

elements.description: The construction elements to trim. Without trimmingElement the roofs and shells among them do the trimming: Archicad decides which roof or shell trims which element and with which trim type, and may trim the roofs and shells with each other, so not every element is necessarily trimmed by every roof or shell. The call reports no result per pair; read them back with GetElementTrims. For a known result, use trimmingElement and call the command once per roof or shell.

trimmingElement.description: Optional. The roof or shell that trims every element in the list, with trimType.

trimType.description: Used with trimmingElement; defaults to KeepInside.

example.description: Trims two walls to the underside of a roof with TrimElements and reads the trims back. The walls and the roof are created by the script and deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Trims two walls to the underside of a roof with TrimElements and reads the trims back.

The walls and the roof are created by the script and deleted at the end.
"""
import math

import aclib

# Two walls under a pitched roof, created by this script and deleted at the end.
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0},
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0}
]})['elements']
roofs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRoofs', {'roofsData': [{
    'level': 2.7,
    'floorIndex': 0,
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (25.0)}],
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, {'x': 100.0, 'y': 105.0}]
}]})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('TrimElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'trimmingElement': roofs[0]['elementId'],
    'trimType': 'KeepInside'
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementTrims', {'elements': walls})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls + roofs})

commands.name: RemoveElementTrims
commands.description: Removes the trim between an element and the roof or shell trimming it. The Archicad API removes the trimming connection between the two elements, so when they trim each other (two roofs or shells) both directions are removed; trim the other direction again with TrimElements to keep it. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each pair whose element is trimmed by its trimming element gets wouldDelete.

elementPairs.description: The trimmed element and the roof or shell trimming it, per pair. The trimming connection between the two is removed: when they trim each other, both directions are removed.

executionResults.description: One result for each input pair, in the order of the input. On a dry run a pair whose element is trimmed by the trimming element gets wouldDelete.

example.description: Removes the trim between two walls and the roof above them with RemoveElementTrims. The walls, the roof and the trims are created by the script first; the elements are deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Removes the trim between two walls and the roof above them with RemoveElementTrims.

The walls, the roof and the trims are created by the script first; the elements are deleted at the end.
"""
import math

import aclib

# Two walls under a pitched roof, created by this script and deleted at the end.
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0},
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0}
]})['elements']
roofs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRoofs', {'roofsData': [{
    'level': 2.7,
    'floorIndex': 0,
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (25.0)}],
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, {'x': 100.0, 'y': 105.0}]
}]})['elements']

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('TrimElements', {'elements': walls + roofs})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RemoveElementTrims', {
    'elementPairs': [{'elementId': wall['elementId'], 'trimmingElementId': roofs[0]['elementId']} for wall in walls]
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementTrims', {'elements': walls})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls + roofs})

commands.name: MergeElements
commands.description: Merges the given construction elements (the Merge command of Archicad, which cleans up the junctions of slabs, beams, walls and similar elements). Undoable. The element types are not filtered: Archicad reports the ones it cannot merge. The merge is read back: when Archicad records no merge between the given elements (it decides which elements and type combinations it merges), the result is a failure, not a success.

elements.description: The construction elements to merge together. At least two.

example.description: Merges two adjacent slabs with MergeElements, the Merge command of Archicad, and reads the merge back. The slabs are created by the script and deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Merges two adjacent slabs with MergeElements, the Merge command of Archicad, and reads the merge back.

The slabs are created by the script and deleted at the end.
"""
import aclib

# Two adjacent slabs, created by this script and deleted at the end.
slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateSlabs', {
    'slabsData': [
        {'level': 0.0, 'thickness': 0.3, 'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 50.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 54.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 54.0, 'y': 54.0}, {'x': 50.0, 'y': 54.0}]},
        {'level': 0.0, 'thickness': 0.3, 'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 54.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 56.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 56.0, 'y': 54.0}, {'x': 54.0, 'y': 54.0}]}
    ]
})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MergeElements', {'elements': slabs}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMergedElements', {'elements': slabs})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': slabs})

commands.name: ShowScriptUI
commands.description: Shows the given HTML content in a native Archicad palette (a tkinter alternative for Python scripts) and returns the uiId of its window. Each script can have its own window, picked by uiId or scriptId; without them the first window is used.

htmlContent.description: The full HTML document to display in the Script UI palette.

width.description: Optional palette client width in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

height.description: Optional palette client height in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

title.description: Optional palette window title. Leave unset to keep the current title.

resizable.description: Whether the user can drag-resize the palette. Defaults to true.

zoomEnabled.description: Whether Ctrl+scroll/pinch zooming is allowed in the page. Defaults to true.

zoomLevel.description: Optional initial zoom level (1.0 = 100%). Leave unset to keep the current zoom.

scrollBarsVisible.description: Whether the browser's own scrollbars are shown. Defaults to true.

contextMenuEnabled.description: Whether right-click shows the browser's context menu (e.g. Inspect Element). Defaults to true.

navigationDisabled.description: Prevents the page from navigating away (e.g. clicking a link to another site) once it has loaded. Defaults to false.

allowSelfSignedCertificates.description: Only relevant if htmlContent links to a remote https:// resource with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false.

clearCookies.description: Deletes all browser cookies before loading htmlContent. Defaults to false.

autoHeight.description: Automatically resizes the palette's height to fit the page content as it changes. Defaults to false.

uiId.description: The window to use, as returned by ShowScriptUI (1 to 8). Takes precedence over scriptId.

scriptId.description: Any text that identifies the calling script, so it uses its own window: ShowScriptUI gives a script without a window a free one, preferring the closed windows. The Tapir palette gives each script it starts its own id in the TAPIR_SCRIPT_ID environment variable, which aclib passes here automatically; that script's window is titled with its name and is freed when it ends. Without uiId and scriptId the first window is used.

uiId.description: The window the page is shown in (1 to 8). Pass it to GetScriptUIResult, or to a later ShowScriptUI to replace the page.

example.description: Shows a small HTML page with a button in an Archicad palette with ShowScriptUI. The response names the window (uiId). The page sends its result with window.ACAPI.SubmitResult; read it with GetScriptUIResult and that uiId.
example.code:
"""Shows a small HTML page with a button in an Archicad palette with ShowScriptUI. The response names the window (uiId). The page sends its result with window.ACAPI.SubmitResult; read it with GetScriptUIResult and that uiId. """ import aclib html = """

Hello from Tapir!

""" aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ShowScriptUI', { 'htmlContent': html, 'title': 'Tapir', 'width': 300, 'height': 150, 'resizable': False }))

commands.name: GetScriptUIResult
commands.description: Retrieves and clears the result last submitted from a Script UI window's page (via window.ACAPI.SubmitResult), if any, and reports whether the window is still open, so a waiting script can stop when the user closes it. The window is picked by uiId or scriptId; without them the first window is used.

uiId.description: The window to use, as returned by ShowScriptUI (1 to 8). Takes precedence over scriptId.

scriptId.description: Any text that identifies the calling script, so it uses its own window: ShowScriptUI gives a script without a window a free one, preferring the closed windows. The Tapir palette gives each script it starts its own id in the TAPIR_SCRIPT_ID environment variable, which aclib passes here automatically; that script's window is titled with its name and is freed when it ends. Without uiId and scriptId the first window is used.

uiId.description: The window the result was read from (1 to 8). Missing when scriptId was given and that script has no window.

hasResult.description: True if the Script UI page has submitted a result since the last call.

result.description: The submitted content (as passed to window.ACAPI.SubmitResult). Only present when hasResult is true.

isOpen.description: True while the Script UI palette is open. False before the first ShowScriptUI call and once the user closed the palette with its close box, the page called window.ACAPI.ClosePalette or Archicad closed it; stays true while Archicad only temporarily hides all palettes (e.g. during a modal dialog). Lets a waiting script stop polling when the user closes the palette.

example.description: Shows a palette with two buttons and waits for the user's choice with GetScriptUIResult. Polls the window ShowScriptUI returned (its uiId) until a button is clicked or the palette is closed.
example.code:
"""Shows a palette with two buttons and waits for the user's choice with GetScriptUIResult. Polls the window ShowScriptUI returned (its uiId) until a button is clicked or the palette is closed. """ import time import aclib html = """

Continue?

""" shown = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ShowScriptUI', {'htmlContent': html, 'title': 'Tapir', 'width': 300, 'height': 150}) while True: response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetScriptUIResult', {'uiId': shown['uiId']}) if response['hasResult'] or not response['isOpen']: break time.sleep (0.5) print (response.get ('result', 'The palette was closed without an answer.'))

commands.name: GenerateDocumentation

ElementIdOrError.description: An element identifier or an error.

AttributeFolder.description: An attribute folder, identified by the type of the attributes it holds and its path from the root folder of that type. Attribute folders exist from Archicad 26.

path.description: The names of the folders from the root folder down to this folder, the root folder itself not included. An empty array is the root folder.

DatabaseIdOrError.description: An Archicad database identifier or an error.

DatabaseIdsOrErrors.description: A list of Archicad database identifiers or errors.

AttributeIdOrError.description: An attribute identifier or an error.

AttributeIdsOrErrors.description: A list of attribute identifiers or errors.

KeynoteFolderId.description: The identifier of a keynote folder.

KeynoteItemId.description: The identifier of a keynote item.

KeynoteFolderIdOrError.description: A keynote folder identifier or an error.

KeynoteFolderIdsOrErrors.description: A list of keynote folder identifiers or errors.

KeynoteItemIdOrError.description: A keynote item identifier or an error.

KeynoteItemIdsOrErrors.description: A list of keynote item identifiers or errors.

KeynoteAutoTextTokens.description: The autotext tokens of a keynote item. A token can be used as the text content of a label to reference the field of the keynote item.

KeynoteAutoTextTokensOrError.description: The autotext tokens of a keynote item or an error.

KeynoteAutoTextTokensOrErrors.description: A list of keynote autotext tokens or errors.

name.description: The autotext's display name, as shown in the Insert Autotext dialog of Archicad.

AutoTextNameOrError.description: The display name of one autotext key, or an error.

AutoTextNamesOrErrors.description: One result per input key, in the same order.

KeynoteItemDetails.description: The details of a keynote item.

KeynoteFolderDetails.description: The details of a keynote folder, including its subfolders and items recursively.

FavoriteFolderDetails.description: A folder of the Favorites palette with its Favorites and subfolders recursively.

name.description: The name of the folder. Empty for the root folder.

path.description: The names of the folders leading from the root to this folder, this folder's name last. Empty for the root folder.

favorites.description: The names of the Favorites directly in this folder.

DesignOptionId.description: The identifier of a design option.

DesignOptionSetId.description: The identifier of a design option set.

ProjectInfoGroupId.description: The identifier of a Project Info group. Available from Archicad 30.

name.description: The name of the selected printer.

portrait.description: The selected orientation: true for portrait, false for landscape.

name.description: The name of the selected plotter.

model.description: The model of the selected plotter.

databaseId.description: The database shown in the window, as GetDatabases, GetContainingDatabases or GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId return it.

windowType.description: Optional. When given, the window is only closed when its database is of this type.

PolygonInputMethod.description: Polygon input method. 'General' = free polygon, 'Rect' = axis-aligned rectangle, 'RotRect' = rotated rectangle, 'Polyline' = open polyline.

h.description: Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.

v.description: Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

h.description: Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.

v.description: Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

ModelViewOptionId.description: The identifier of the model view option combination.

ViewOptions.description: The model view options and the on-screen view options, every field by its API_ViewOptions name. Values are the numeric API constants; attribute indices are plain integers.

modelViewOptions.description: Fields of API_ModelViewOptions, with the curtainWall, stair and railing parts as nested objects.

ViewOptionsUpdate.description: The fields to change, named as in the response of GetViewOptions. Fields not given keep their current value. Without an index, the window then uses Custom model view options (index 0), also when only on-screen view options are given. To keep the combination, give its index as well.

renovationFilterId.description: Identifier of the renovation filter. The same identifier is the renovationFilterGuid of GetViewSettings and SetViewSettings.

name.description: Name of the renovation filter.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item.

parentViewpointId.description: The identifier of the root or group the item is in. Missing when Archicad reports no parent, as for a root.

itemType.description: Whether the item is a root, a group or a leaf node.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).

data.description: The data the add-on attached to the item, base64 encoded. Empty when there is none.

AddOnViewpointType.description: Whether to create a root, a group or a leaf node. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item to change.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).

data.description: Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded. It replaces the attached data; an empty string removes it.

PlaceSettingsUpdate.description: The place settings to change (API_PlaceInfo), with its field names. Only the given keys are changed; an empty object changes nothing and returns the current settings.

sumTime.description: Whether summer time (+1 hour) is on.

timeZoneInMinutes.description: The time zone, in minutes from Greenwich.

timeZoneOffset.description: Tells apart time zones with the same timeZoneInMinutes.

autotextId.description: The numeric value of the autotext's API_NoteAutotextID in the Archicad API.

elementTypes.description: The element types the autotext is available for.

name.description: The new name of the group. It must not be used by another group.

beforeProjectInfoGroupId.description: The group to move the group before. When omitted, the group is moved to the end of the group list.

location.description: Absolute path of the hotlink's source file.

status.description: The API_HotlinkSourceStatus value without its prefix (AuthCanceld is spelled as in the API).

value.description: The value to convert, in meters, square meters, cubic meters or radians, matching the kind of the preference.

preference.description: The Project Preference whose unit and rounding are applied: WorkModel, WorkLayout and WorkAngle are the Working Units; the Dim ones are the Dimensions (DimDoorWindow the door, window and skylight dimensions, DimParapet the sill height, DimArea the area calculations); the Calc ones are the Calculation Units & Rules.

convertedValue.description: The value as Archicad shows it in the unit of the preference, without the extra accuracy decimals. It may contain the unit.

extraAccuracy.description: The extra accuracy decimals, if any (at most two). Empty when there are none.

unit.description: The unit of the preference. It may be empty.

name.description: The name of the status as the running Archicad shows it (localized).

ProjectInfoFieldId.description: The identifier of a field of a Project Info group. It is not the autotext key that GetProjectInfoFields returns as projectInfoId. Available from Archicad 30.

LayersOfLayerCombination.description: List of Layers included in the Layer Combination.

attributeId.description: The identifier of the Layer attribute.

isHidden.description: Visibility of the Layer in the Layer Combination.

isLocked.description: Lock state of the Layer in the Layer Combination.

isWireframe.description: Is wireframe mode forced for the Layer in the Layer Combination.

intersectionGroupNr.description: Intersection group of the Layer in the Layer Combination. Elements on layers having the same group will be intersected.

LayerCombinationAttributeDetails.description: The details of the layer combination attribute.

attributeId.description: The identifier of the layer combination attribute.

attributeIndex.description: The index identifier of the layer combination attribute.

name.description: The name of the layer combination.

LayerCombinationAttributeOrError.description: A layer combination attribute or an error.

LineAttributeOrError.description: A line attribute or an error.

dash.description: Length of the visible part of the item.

gap.description: Length of the invisible part of the item.

FillAttributeOrError.description: A fill attribute or an error.

frequency.description: The distance between two instances of this item.

direction.description: The angle of the item, measured CCW from the horizontal axis, in radians.

offsetLine.description: The parallel offset of the item, measured from the (rotated) horizontal axis.

offset.description: The offset of the item.

lineLengths.description: Dash-gap length pairs describing this line item. Must contain an even number of items.

angle.description: Arc angle in radians, measured CCW.

FillSymbolSolidFill.description: A filled polygon of a symbol fill's pattern (sfill_SolidFills with sfill_FillCoords, sfill_SubPolys and sfill_PolyArcs), in the same form as other polygons in Tapir: closed contours, the first point repeated at the end of each contour.

subPolygons.description: 1-based index of the last coordinate of each contour (the outline first, then the holes).

ZoneCategoryAttributeOrError.description: A zone category attribute or an error.

domain.description: The domain(s) this system belongs to. Archicad 29+ allows only one; earlier versions may report several.

materialId.description: The surface (material) attribute applied to the 3D model of the elements of the system.

insulationMaterialId.description: The surface (material) attribute applied to the insulation of the elements of the system.

MEPSystemAttributeOrError.description: An MEP system attribute or an error.

PenTableAttributeOrError.description: A pen table attribute or an error.

skins.description: The profile's skins (hatches), each with its building material/surface/fill, contour and cut-end line settings, and per-edge line data.

ProfileModifier.description: A stretchable edge-offset parameter of the profile, as named by the profile's author in the Profile Editor. Its value is a live geometric measurement matching what the Profile Editor's dimension shows.

name.description: User-authored label, e.g. 'Largeur support'. Present only if the profile's author assigned one.

value.description: Present only when the parameter's dimension anchors could be resolved to concrete positions.

ProfileSkin.description: One skin (hatch) of the profile's cross-section.

skinId.description: Internal identifier of this skin, stable for the lifetime of the profile. Pass it back in CreateProfiles' skinOverrides to target this skin for modification.

outlineCoords.description: The skin's outline polygon vertices, present only when the skinOutlines field is requested alongside skins.

outlineSubPolyEnds.description: Index (into outlineCoords) of the last vertex of each contour, for skins whose outline has holes or multiple contours.

outlineArcs.description: Marks which consecutive outlineCoords pairs are connected by an arc instead of a straight edge.

ProfileEdge.description: One edge of a profile skin's outline.

ProfileAttributeOrError.description: A profile attribute or an error.

CompositeAttributeOrError.description: A composite attribute or an error.

SurfaceAttributeOrError.description: A surface attribute or an error.

LayerAttributeOrError.description: A layer attribute or an error.

BuildingMaterialAttributeOrError.description: A building material attribute or an error.

Guid.description: A Globally Unique Identifier (or Universally Unique Identifier) in its string representation as defined in RFC 4122.

Hotlink.description: The details of a hotlink node.

location.description: The path of the hotlink file.

name.description: The display name of the hotlink node.

instances.description: The hotlink instance elements placed from the node, in the order Archicad returns them - the input of ChangeHotlinkInstances and DeleteElements. Omitted when the node's instances cannot be read.

children.description: The children of the hotlink node if it has any.

HotlinkNodeId.description: The identifier of a hotlink node - the reference to a module source file, which instances are placed from.

HotlinkOrigin.description: Where a hotlink instance's origin lands, in the project's coordinates.

HotlinkDetails.description: Details of a placed hotlink instance: which node it comes from and where it sits.

rotationAngle.description: Counter-clockwise rotation about the origin, in radians.

mirrored.description: True when the module's local X axis is reflected.

existing.description: True when a node for the same source file already existed and was returned instead of created.

HotlinkNodeCreatedOrError.description: The created (or already existing) node's guid, or an error.

HotlinkOwnersOfElement.description: The hotlink an element comes from. Both ids are omitted when the element is not part of a hotlinked module.

isInHotlink.description: True when Archicad reports a hotlink for the element, that is, when at least one of the ids below is returned.
